&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:19&gt;C++&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;The reason for this is kind of nasty. From LLVM&amp;rsquo;s perspective, an inline assembly
block is a &lt;code&gt;call asm&lt;/code&gt; instruction to a special function whose name is the
inline assembly string. Although the lack of &lt;code&gt;volatile&lt;/code&gt; marks this function as
pure, making it reorderable, there is no way to tell LLVM that it can be merged.&lt;p&gt;If we try to unroll the loop 32 times, we wind up with 32 calls to a pure
function with the signature &lt;code&gt;i64 -&gt; i64&lt;/code&gt;, and LLVM doesn&amp;rsquo;t know that it&amp;rsquo;s safe
to merge them into an almost identical function call with a signature
&lt;code&gt;&amp;lt;32 x i64&gt; -&gt; &amp;lt;32 x i64&gt;&lt;/code&gt;. Because one of the loop operations cannot be
vectorized (namely, this inline assembly block), vectorization fails.&lt;p&gt;There is no workaround for this. Allowing the inline assembly block to use an
SSE register using the &lt;code&gt;&#34;+x&#34;&lt;/code&gt; constraint doesn&amp;rsquo;t work, because the failure is
&lt;em&gt;not&lt;/em&gt; the assembly constraints: it&amp;rsquo;s that the &lt;code&gt;call asm&lt;/code&gt; instruction does not
support vectorization&lt;sup id=fnref:1&gt;&lt;a href=#fn:1 class=footnote-ref role=doc-noteref&gt;1&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/sup&gt;.&lt;h2 id=is-this-really-a-language-feature&gt;&lt;a href=#is-this-really-a-language-feature&gt;Is This Really a Language Feature?&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;p&gt;For all intents and purposes, this magic incantation is part of C++ (at least,
the dialect that GCC and Clang implement, which are the only compilers that
matter for security&lt;sup id=fnref:2&gt;&lt;a href=#fn:2 class=footnote-ref role=doc-noteref&gt;2&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/sup&gt;).&lt;p&gt;This is because BoringSSL&lt;sup id=fnref:3&gt;&lt;a href=#fn:3 class=footnote-ref role=doc-noteref&gt;3&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/sup&gt;, the most widely-deployed cryptography library in
the world, &lt;a href=https://boringssl.googlesource.com/boringssl/+/15b1f9c6a4f9656e7c172e03064fe7f8e03c666d/crypto/internal.h#343&gt;relies on this trick&lt;/a&gt;.
This feature is critical to the security posture of the two biggest orgs that
fund LLVM: Google and Apple. Tools which break the value barrier have
historically been quickly patched to respect it, usually due to the
consternation of a professional cryptographer.&lt;p&gt;The optimization black box is not quite as critical, but its correctness is
a side-effect of the value barrier&amp;rsquo;s: namely, that the optimizer must never
peek into an inline assembly block.&lt;p&gt;Of course, any professional cryptographer who has to implement constant-time
primitives would tell you that this is a crummy workaround, and that we really
need actual language-level intrinsics for manipulating values in a constant-time
way. The tricky part is specifying semantics for them in a way that makes sure
we don&amp;rsquo;t allow &amp;ldquo;bad&amp;rdquo; optimizations, a notoriously difficult problem in compiler
IR design.&lt;h3 id=postscript&gt;&lt;a href=#postscript&gt;Postscript&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;Shortly after publishing this piece today, I got an email informing me that
Clang 22 is planning to land &lt;code&gt;__builtin_ct_select&lt;/code&gt;, an intrinsic that implements
constant-time select in an optimization-friendly way. It will never be emitted
as a branch, but it lowers to a &lt;code&gt;cmov&lt;/code&gt; on x86 and a &lt;code&gt;csel&lt;/code&gt; on aarch64. More
on this new intrinsic can be found &lt;a href=https://blog.trailofbits.com/2025/12/02/introducing-constant-time-support-for-llvm-to-protect-cryptographic-code/&gt;here&lt;/a&gt;. This
posts suggests that there may be future improvements, such as a true &amp;ldquo;secret
integer&amp;rdquo; type that always guarantees constant-time operations. I&amp;rsquo;m surprised
that neither I nor David Benjamin (the maintainer of BoringSSL) knew about this
LLVM RFC.&lt;p&gt;While discussing this article with David,
I also realized that the &lt;a href=#code:slow-sum&gt;version of &lt;code&gt;sum&lt;/code&gt; with a barrier&lt;/a&gt; can
actually be written in such a way that the barrier is present without breaking
vectorization. If we use the &lt;a href=#code:xor-barrier&gt;xor-with-key&lt;/a&gt; variant of the
value barrier, we can still get the optimizations we want:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:20&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-cpp highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=kt&gt;uint64_t&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;__ct_key&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=c1&gt;// Must not be static or const!
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=kt&gt;uint64_t&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nf&gt;sum&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=kt&gt;uint64_t&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;*&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;p&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=kt&gt;int&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;n&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;n&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;amp;=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;~&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mi&gt;31&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=c1&gt;// Round n to the nearest multiple of 32.
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;u64&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;a&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=mi&gt;0&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=k&gt;for&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=kt&gt;int&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;i&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=mi&gt;0&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;i&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;lt;&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;n&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;i&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;++&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;    &lt;span class=n&gt;a&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;+=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;p&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;[&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;i&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;]&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;^&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;__ct_key&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=k&gt;return&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;a&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:20&gt;C++&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;However, I&amp;rsquo;m fairly certain that LTO and post-link optimization such as BOLT
can potentially shred this barrier, and it comes at the cost of a vectorized
xor each unrolled loop iteration&lt;sup id=fnref:4&gt;&lt;a href=#fn:4 class=footnote-ref role=doc-noteref&gt;4&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/sup&gt;.&lt;div class=footnotes role=doc-endnotes&gt;&lt;hr&gt;&lt;ol&gt;&lt;li id=fn:1&gt;&lt;p&gt;This could be fixed by making &lt;code&gt;asm(&#34;&#34;)&lt;/code&gt; vectorizable, because it &lt;em&gt;is&lt;/em&gt; in
the sense that a no-op is vectorizable. However, it&amp;rsquo;s not immediately clear
to me if this is safe, even though it feels like it aught to be.&amp;#160;&lt;a href=#fnref:1 class=footnote-backref role=doc-backlink&gt;&amp;#8617;&amp;#xfe0e;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;li id=fn:2&gt;&lt;p&gt;For example: all Internet browsers today are built with Clang, because
Chromium only supports Clang builds and Firefox and Safari use Clang because
Rust and Apple, respectively.&amp;#160;&lt;a href=#fnref:2 class=footnote-backref role=doc-backlink&gt;&amp;#8617;&amp;#xfe0e;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;li id=fn:3&gt;&lt;p&gt;The only browsers not shipping BoringSSL are Firefox and Safari; Chromium
and all of its derivatives use it. It is also deployed on every Android
device (not just the most popular mobile OS: horrible little Android
devices, like POS equipment, are everywhere), and, of course, within all
of Google&amp;rsquo;s data centers. Being on every Android device is probably enough
to make the claim of &amp;ldquo;most widely deployed&amp;rdquo;, but being on 90%+ of consumer
equipment, by virtue of Google Chrome being so popular, definitely makes it
enough.&amp;#160;&lt;a href=#fnref:3 class=footnote-backref role=doc-backlink&gt;&amp;#8617;&amp;#xfe0e;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;li id=fn:4&gt;&lt;p&gt;The load from &lt;code&gt;[rip + __ct_key@GOTPCREL]&lt;/code&gt; gets hoisted out of the loop,
thanks to the fact that C++ can safely assume that no writes to &lt;code&gt;__ct_key&lt;/code&gt;
occur on other threads, thanks to &lt;code&gt;__ct_key&lt;/code&gt; being non-atomic and data
races resulting in Undefined Behavior.&amp;#160;&lt;a href=#fnref:4 class=footnote-backref role=doc-backlink&gt;&amp;#8617;&amp;#xfe0e;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/ol&gt;&lt;/div&gt;</content>

  <entry>
    <title>Why SSA?</title>
    <link href="/2025/10/21/ssa-1"/>
    <updated>2025-10-21T00:00:00+00:00</updated>
    <id>/2025/10/21/ssa-1</id>
    <content type="html">&lt;p&gt;If you&amp;rsquo;ve read anything about compilers in the last two decades or so, you have
almost certainly heard of &lt;em&gt;SSA compilers&lt;/em&gt;, a popular architecture featured in
many optimizing compilers, including ahead-of-time compilers such as LLVM, GCC,
Go, CUDA (and various shader compilers), Swift&lt;sup id=fnref:1&gt;&lt;a href=#fn:1 class=footnote-ref role=doc-noteref&gt;1&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/sup&gt;, and MSVC&lt;sup id=fnref:2&gt;&lt;a href=#fn:2 class=footnote-ref role=doc-noteref&gt;2&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/sup&gt;, and
just-in-time compilers such as HotSpot C2&lt;sup id=fnref:3&gt;&lt;a href=#fn:3 class=footnote-ref role=doc-noteref&gt;3&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/sup&gt;, V8&lt;sup id=fnref:4&gt;&lt;a href=#fn:4 class=footnote-ref role=doc-noteref&gt;4&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/sup&gt;,
SpiderMonkey&lt;sup id=fnref:5&gt;&lt;a href=#fn:5 class=footnote-ref role=doc-noteref&gt;5&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/sup&gt;, LuaJIT, and the Android Runtime&lt;sup id=fnref:6&gt;&lt;a href=#fn:6 class=footnote-ref role=doc-noteref&gt;6&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/sup&gt;.&lt;p&gt;SSA is hugely popular, to the point that most compiler projects no longer bother
with other IRs for optimization&lt;sup id=fnref:7&gt;&lt;a href=#fn:7 class=footnote-ref role=doc-noteref&gt;7&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/sup&gt;. This is because SSA is incredibly nimble
at the types of program analysis and transformation that compiler optimizations
want to do on your code. But &lt;em&gt;why&lt;/em&gt;? Many of my friends who don&amp;rsquo;t do compilers
often say that compilers seem like opaque magical black boxes, and SSA, as it
often appears in the literature, is impenetrably complex.&lt;p&gt;But it&amp;rsquo;s not! SSA is actually very simple once you forget everything you think
your programs are actually doing. We will develop the concept of SSA form, a
simple SSA IR, prove facts about it, and design some optimizations on it.&lt;blockquote id=note:1 class=note note&gt;&lt;a href=#note:1&gt;&lt;span class=chip&gt;note&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;p&gt;I have &lt;a href=/2023/08/01/llvm-ir&gt;previously written&lt;/a&gt; about the
granddaddy of all modern SSA compilers, LLVM. This article is about SSA in
general, and won&amp;rsquo;t really have anything to do with LLVM. However, it may be
helpful to read that article to make some of the things in this article feel
more concrete.&lt;/blockquote&gt;&lt;h2 id=what-is-ssa&gt;&lt;a href=#what-is-ssa&gt;What Is SSA?&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;p&gt;SSA is a property of &lt;em&gt;intermediate representations&lt;/em&gt; (IRs), primarily used by
compilers for optimizing imperative code that target a &lt;em&gt;register machine&lt;/em&gt;.
Register machines are computers that feature a fixed set of &lt;em&gt;registers&lt;/em&gt; that can
be used as the operands for instructions: this includes virtually all physical
processors, including CPUs, GPUs, and weird tings like DSPs.&lt;p&gt;SSA is most frequently found in compiler &lt;em&gt;middle-ends&lt;/em&gt;, the optimizing component
between the &lt;em&gt;frontend&lt;/em&gt; (which deals with the &lt;em&gt;surface language&lt;/em&gt; programmers
write, and lowers it into the middle-end&amp;rsquo;s IR), and the &lt;em&gt;backend&lt;/em&gt; (which takes
the optimized IR and lowers it into the target platform&amp;rsquo;s assembly).&lt;p&gt;SSA IRs, however, often have little resemblance to the surface language they
lower out of, or the assembly language they target. This is because neither of
these representations make it easy for a compiler to intuit optimization
opportunities.&lt;h3 id=imperative-code-is-hard&gt;&lt;a href=#imperative-code-is-hard&gt;Imperative Code Is Hard&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;Imperative code consists of a sequence of operations that mutate the executing
machine&amp;rsquo;s state to produce a desired result. For example, consider the following
C program:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:1&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-c highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=kt&gt;int&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nf&gt;main&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=kt&gt;int&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;argc&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=kt&gt;char&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;**&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;argv&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=kt&gt;int&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;a&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;argc&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=kt&gt;int&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;b&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;a&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;+&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=mi&gt;1&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;a&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;b&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;+&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=mi&gt;2&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;b&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;+=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=mi&gt;2&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;a&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;-=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;b&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=k&gt;return&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;a&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:1&gt;C&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;This program returns &lt;code&gt;0&lt;/code&gt; no matter what its input is, so we can optimize it down
to this:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:2&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-c highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=kt&gt;int&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nf&gt;main&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=kt&gt;int&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;argc&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=kt&gt;char&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;**&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;argv&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=k&gt;return&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=mi&gt;0&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:2&gt;C&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;But, how would you write a general algorithm to detect that all of the
operations cancel out? You&amp;rsquo;re forced to keep in mind &lt;em&gt;program order&lt;/em&gt; to perform
the necessary dataflow analysis, following mutations of &lt;code&gt;a&lt;/code&gt; and &lt;code&gt;b&lt;/code&gt; through the
program. But this isn&amp;rsquo;t very general, and traversing all of those paths makes
the search space for large functions very big. Instead, you would like to
rewrite the program such that &lt;code&gt;a&lt;/code&gt; and &lt;code&gt;b&lt;/code&gt; gradually get replaced with the
expression that calculates the most recent value, like this:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:3&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-c highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=kt&gt;int&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nf&gt;main&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=kt&gt;int&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;argc&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=kt&gt;char&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;**&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;argv&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=kt&gt;int&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;a&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;argc&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=kt&gt;int&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;b&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;a&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;+&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=mi&gt;1&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=kt&gt;int&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;a2&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;b&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;+&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=mi&gt;2&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=kt&gt;int&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;b2&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;b&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;+&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=mi&gt;2&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=kt&gt;int&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;a3&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;a2&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;-&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;b2&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt;

&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=kt&gt;int&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;b2&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;argc&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;+&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=mi&gt;3&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=kt&gt;int&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;a3&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;argc&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;-&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;argc&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=k&gt;return&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;argc&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;-&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;argc&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:5&gt;C&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;And finally, we see that we&amp;rsquo;re returning &lt;code&gt;argc - argc&lt;/code&gt;, and can replace it with
&lt;code&gt;0&lt;/code&gt;. All the other variables are now unused, so we can delete them.&lt;p&gt;The reason this works so well is because we took a function with mutation, and
converted it into a &lt;em&gt;combinatorial circuit&lt;/em&gt;, a type of digital logic circuit
that has no state, and which is very easy to analyze. The dependencies between
&lt;em&gt;nodes&lt;/em&gt; in the circuit (corresponding to primitive operations such as addition
or multiplication) are obvious from its structure. For example, consider the
following circuit diagram for a one-bit multiplier:&lt;figure&gt;&lt;img src=/assets/images/multiplier.png style=filter:invert(100%)&gt;&lt;figcaption&gt;A binary multiplier (Wikipedia)&lt;/figcaption&gt;&lt;/figure&gt;&lt;p&gt;This graph representation of an operation program has two huge benefits:&lt;ol&gt;&lt;li&gt;&lt;p&gt;The powerful tools of graph theory can be used to algorithmically analyze the
program and discover useful properties, such as operations that are
independent of each other or whose results are never used.&lt;li&gt;&lt;p&gt;The operations are not ordered with respect to each other except when there
is a dependency; this is useful for reordering operations, something
compilers really like to do.&lt;/ol&gt;&lt;p&gt;The reason combinatorial circuits are the best circuits is because they are
&lt;em&gt;directed acyclic graphs&lt;/em&gt; (DAGs) which admit really nice algorithms. For
example, longest path in a graph is
&lt;a href=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NP-hardness&gt;NP-hard&lt;/a&gt; (and because
&lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.8889em;vertical-align:-.1944em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34; style=margin-right:.13889em&gt;P&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mspace style=margin-right:.2778em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mrel&gt;&lt;span class=mrel&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord vbox&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=thinbox&gt;&lt;span class=rlap&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.8889em;vertical-align:-.1944em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=inner&gt;&lt;span class=mord&gt;&lt;span class=mrel&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=fix&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mrel&gt;=&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mspace style=margin-right:.2778em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.6833em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34; style=margin-right:.13889em&gt;NP&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;sup id=fnref:8&gt;&lt;a href=#fn:8 class=footnote-ref role=doc-noteref&gt;8&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/sup&gt;, has complexity &lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:1em;vertical-align:-.25em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34; style=margin-right:.02778em&gt;O&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mopen&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mord&gt;&lt;span class=mord&gt;2&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=msupsub&gt;&lt;span class=vlist-t&gt;&lt;span class=vlist-r&gt;&lt;span class=vlist style=height:.6644em&gt;&lt;span style=top:-3.063em;margin-right:.05em&gt;&lt;span class=pstrut style=height:2.7em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal mtight&#34;&gt;n&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mclose&gt;)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;). However, if the graph is a
DAG, it admits an &lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:1em;vertical-align:-.25em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34; style=margin-right:.02778em&gt;O&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mopen&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34;&gt;n&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mclose&gt;)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; solution!&lt;p&gt;To understand this benefit, consider another program:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:6&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-c highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=kt&gt;int&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nf&gt;f&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=kt&gt;int&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;x&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=kt&gt;int&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;y&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;x&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;*&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=mi&gt;2&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;x&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;*=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;y&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=k&gt;const&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=kt&gt;int&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;z&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;y&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;y&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;*=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;y&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=k&gt;return&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;x&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;+&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;z&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:6&gt;C&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;Suppose we wanted to replace each variable with its definition like we did
before. We can&amp;rsquo;t &lt;em&gt;just&lt;/em&gt; replace each constant variable with the expression that
defines it though, because we would wind up with a different program!&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:7&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-c highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=kt&gt;int&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nf&gt;f&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=kt&gt;int&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;x&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=kt&gt;int&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;y&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;x&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;*&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=mi&gt;2&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;x&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;*=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;y&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=c1&gt;// const int z = y; // Replace z with its definition.
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;y&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;*=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;y&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=k&gt;return&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;x&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;+&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;y&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:7&gt;C&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;Now, we pick up an extra &lt;code&gt;y&lt;/code&gt; term because the squaring operation is no longer
unused! We can put this into circuit form, but it requires inserting new
variables for every mutation.&lt;p&gt;But we can&amp;rsquo;t do this when complex control flow is involved! So all of our
algorithms need to carefully account for mutations and program order, meaning
that we don&amp;rsquo;t get to use the nice graph algorithms without careful modification.&lt;h2 id=the-ssa-invariant&gt;&lt;a href=#the-ssa-invariant&gt;The SSA Invariant&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;p&gt;SSA stands for &amp;ldquo;static single assignment&amp;rdquo;, and was developed in the 80s as a way
to enhance the existing three-argument code (where every statement is in the
form &lt;code&gt;x = y op z&lt;/code&gt;) so that every program was circuit-like, using a very similar
procedure to the one described above.&lt;p&gt;The SSA invariant states that every variable in the program is assigned to by
precisely one operation. If every operation in the program is visited once, they
form a combinatorial circuit. Transformations are required to respect this
invariant. In circuit form, a program is a graph where operations are nodes, and
&amp;ldquo;registers&amp;rdquo; (which is what variables are usually called in SSA) are edges
(specifically, each output of an operation corresponds to a register).&lt;p&gt;But, again, control flow. We can&amp;rsquo;t hope to circuitize a loop, right? The key
observation of SSA is that &lt;em&gt;most&lt;/em&gt; parts of a program are circuit-like. A &lt;em&gt;basic
block&lt;/em&gt; is a maximal circuital component of a program. Simply put, it is a
sequence of non-control flow operations, and a final &lt;em&gt;terminator&lt;/em&gt; operation that
transfers control to another basic block.&lt;p&gt;The basic blocks themselves form a graph, the &lt;em&gt;control flow graph&lt;/em&gt;, or CFG. This
formulation of SSA is sometimes called SSA-CFG&lt;sup id=fnref:9&gt;&lt;a href=#fn:9 class=footnote-ref role=doc-noteref&gt;9&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/sup&gt;. This graph is &lt;em&gt;not&lt;/em&gt; a
DAG in general; however, separating the program into basic blocks conveniently
factors out the &amp;ldquo;non-DAG&amp;rdquo; parts of the program, allowing for simpler analysis
within basic blocks.&lt;p&gt;There are two equivalent formalisms for SSA-CFG. The traditional one uses
special &amp;ldquo;phi&amp;rdquo; operations (often called &lt;em&gt;phi nodes&lt;/em&gt;, which is what I will call
them here) to link registers across basic blocks. This is the formalism LLVM
uses. A more modern approach, used by MLIR, is &lt;em&gt;block arguments&lt;/em&gt;: each basic
block specifies parameters, like a function, and blocks transferring control
flow to it must pass arguments of those types to it.&lt;h3 id=my-first-ir&gt;&lt;a href=#my-first-ir&gt;My First IR&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;Let&amp;rsquo;s look at some code. First, consider the following C function which
calculates Fibonacci numbers using a loop.&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:8&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-c highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=kt&gt;int&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nf&gt;fib&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=kt&gt;int&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;n&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;

will look a &lt;em&gt;little bit&lt;/em&gt; like LLVM IR, since that&amp;rsquo;s what I&amp;rsquo;m used to looking at.&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:fib-ir&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-ssa-cfg highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;// Globals (including functions) start with $, registers with %.

&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;    &lt;span class=c1&gt;// the given arguments.

&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;  &lt;span class=err&gt;@&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nx&gt;loop&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nf&gt;start&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;%&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nx&gt;n&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;%&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nx&gt;a&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;%&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nx&gt;b&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;:&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nx&gt;i32&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;):&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;    &lt;span class=c1&gt;// Integer comparison: %n &amp;gt; 0.
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;    &lt;span class=o&gt;%&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nx&gt;cont&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nx&gt;cmp&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nx&gt;gt&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;%&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nx&gt;n&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=mi&gt;0&lt;/span&gt;

&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;    &lt;span class=k&gt;goto&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;%&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nx&gt;cont&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;      &lt;span class=mi&gt;0&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;-&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=err&gt;@&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nf&gt;ret&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;%&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nx&gt;a&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;),&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=c1&gt;// Goto can jump to the function exit.
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;      &lt;span class=mi&gt;1&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;-&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=err&gt;@&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nx&gt;loop&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nf&gt;body&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;%&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nx&gt;n&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;%&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nx&gt;a&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;%&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nx&gt;b&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;),&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;    &lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=err&gt;@&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nx&gt;loop&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nf&gt;body&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;%&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nx&gt;n&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;%&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nx&gt;a&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;%&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nx&gt;b&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;:&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nx&gt;i32&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;):&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;    &lt;span class=c1&gt;// Addition and subtraction.
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;    &lt;span class=o&gt;%&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nx&gt;c&lt;/span&gt;    &lt;span class=p&gt;=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nx&gt;add&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;%&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nx&gt;a&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;%&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nx&gt;b&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;    &lt;span class=o&gt;%&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nx&gt;n&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mf&gt;.2&lt;/span&gt;  &lt;span class=p&gt;=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nx&gt;sub&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;%&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nx&gt;n&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=mi&gt;1&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;    &lt;span class=c1&gt;// Note the assignments in @loop.start:
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;    &lt;span class=c1&gt;// %n = %n.2, %a = %b, %b = %c.
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;    &lt;span class=k&gt;goto&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=err&gt;@&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nx&gt;loop&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nf&gt;start&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;%&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nx&gt;n&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mf&gt;.2&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;%&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nx&gt;b&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;%&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nx&gt;c&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:fib-ir&gt;SSA-CFG&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;Every block ends in a &lt;code&gt;goto&lt;/code&gt;, which transfers control to one of several possible
blocks. In the process, it calls that block with the given arguments. One can
think of a basic block as a tiny function which &lt;em&gt;tails&lt;/em&gt;&lt;sup id=fnref:10&gt;&lt;a href=#fn:10 class=footnote-ref role=doc-noteref&gt;10&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/sup&gt; into other
basic blocks in the same function.&lt;blockquote id=aside:1 class=aside aside&gt;&lt;a href=#aside:1&gt;&lt;span class=chip&gt;aside&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;p&gt;LLVM IR is&amp;mldr; older, so it uses the older formalism of phi nodes. &amp;ldquo;Phi&amp;rdquo; comes
from &amp;ldquo;phony&amp;rdquo;, because it is an operation that doesn&amp;rsquo;t do anything; it just
links registers from predecessors.&lt;p&gt;A &lt;code&gt;phi&lt;/code&gt; operation is essentially a switch-case on the predecessors, each case
selecting a register from that predecessor (or an immediate). For example,
&lt;code&gt;@loop.start&lt;/code&gt; has two predecessors, the implicit entry block &lt;code&gt;@entry&lt;/code&gt;, and
&lt;code&gt;@loop.body&lt;/code&gt;. In a phi node IR, instead of taking a block argument for &lt;code&gt;%n&lt;/code&gt;,
it would specify&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:9&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-ssa-cfg highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=o&gt;%&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nx&gt;n&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nx&gt;phi&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=err&gt;@&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nx&gt;entry&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;-&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=mi&gt;0&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=err&gt;@&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nx&gt;loop&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nx&gt;body&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;-&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;%&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nx&gt;n&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mf&gt;.2&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:9&gt;SSA-CFG&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;The value of the &lt;code&gt;phi&lt;/code&gt; operation is the value from whichever block jumped to
this one.&lt;p&gt;This can be awkward to type out by hand and read, but is a more convenient
representation for describing algorithms (just &amp;ldquo;add a phi node&amp;rdquo; instead of
&amp;ldquo;add a parameter and a corresponding argument&amp;rdquo;) and for the in-memory
representation, but is otherwise completely equivalent.&lt;/blockquote&gt;&lt;p&gt;It&amp;rsquo;s a bit easier to understand the transformation from C to our IR if we first
rewrite the C to use goto instead of a for loop:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:10&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-c highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=kt&gt;int&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nf&gt;fib&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=kt&gt;int&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;n&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=kt&gt;int&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;a&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=mi&gt;0&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;b&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=mi&gt;1&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt; &lt;span class=nl&gt;start&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;:&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=k&gt;if&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;n&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=mi&gt;0&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=k&gt;goto&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;ret&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=kt&gt;int&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;c&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;a&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;+&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;b&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;a&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;b&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;b&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;c&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=k&gt;goto&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;start&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=nl&gt;ret&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;:&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=k&gt;return&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;a&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:10&gt;C&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;However, we still have mutation in the picture, so this isn&amp;rsquo;t SSA. To get into
SSA, we need to replace every assignment with a new register, and somehow insert
block arguments&amp;mldr;&lt;h3 id=entering-ssa-form&gt;&lt;a href=#entering-ssa-form&gt;Entering SSA Form&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;The &lt;a href=#code:fib-ir&gt;above IR code&lt;/a&gt; is already partially optimized; the named
variables in the C program have been &lt;em&gt;lifted&lt;/em&gt; out of memory and into registers.
If we represent each named variable in our C program with a pointer, we can
avoid needing to put the program into SSA form immediately. This technique is
used by frontends that lower into LLVM, like Clang.&lt;p&gt;We&amp;rsquo;ll enhance our IR by adding a &lt;code&gt;stack&lt;/code&gt; declaration for functions, which
defines scratch space on the stack for the function to use. Each stack slot
produces a pointer that we can &lt;code&gt;load&lt;/code&gt; from and &lt;code&gt;store&lt;/code&gt; to.&lt;p&gt;Our Fibonacci function would now look like so:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:fib-memory&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-ssa-cfg highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=kd&gt;func&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;amp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nf&gt;fib&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;%&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nx&gt;n&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;:&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nx&gt;i32&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;-&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nx&gt;i32&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;
