    <title>The Best C++ Library</title>
    <link href="/2025/07/14/best"/>
    <updated>2025-07-14T00:00:00+00:00</updated>
    <id>/2025/07/14/best</id>
    <content type="html">&lt;p&gt;It&amp;rsquo;s no secret that my taste in programming languages is very weird for a
programming language ~~enthusiast~~ professional. Several of my
&lt;a href=https://mcyoung.xyz/2025/07/07/nosplit/&gt;last&lt;/a&gt;
&lt;a href=https://mcyoung.xyz/2025/04/21/go-arenas/&gt;few&lt;/a&gt;
&lt;a href=https://mcyoung.xyz/2024/12/16/rangefuncs/&gt;posts&lt;/a&gt; are about Go, broadly
regarded as the programming language equivalent of eating plain oatmeal for
breakfast.&lt;p&gt;To make up for that, I&amp;rsquo;m going to write about the programming language
equivalent of diluting your morning coffee with
&lt;a href=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everclear&gt;Everclear&lt;/a&gt;. I am, of course, talking
about C++.&lt;p&gt;If you&amp;rsquo;ve ever had the misfortune of doing C++ professionally, you&amp;rsquo;ll know that
the C++ standard library is really bad. Where to begin?&lt;p&gt;Well, the associative containers are terrible. Due to bone-headed API decisions,
&lt;a href=https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/container/unordered_map.html&gt;&lt;code&gt;std::unordered_map&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/a&gt;
MUST be a closed-addressing, array-of-linked-lists map, not a Swisstable,
despite closed-addressing being an outdated technology.
&lt;a href=https://www.cppreference.com/w/cpp/container/map.html&gt;&lt;code&gt;std::map&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/a&gt;, which is
not what you usually want, &lt;em&gt;must&lt;/em&gt; be a red-black tree. It can&amp;rsquo;t be a b-tree,
like every sensible language provides for the ordered map.&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href=https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/utility/optional.html&gt;&lt;code&gt;std::optional&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/a&gt; is a
massive pain in the ass to use, and is full of footguns, like &lt;code&gt;operator*&lt;/code&gt;.
&lt;code&gt;std::variant&lt;/code&gt; is also really annoying to use.
&lt;a href=https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/filesystem.html&gt;&lt;code&gt;std::filesystem&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/a&gt; is full
of sharp edges. And where are the APIs for signals?&lt;p&gt;Everything is extremely wordy.
&lt;a href=https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/thread/hardware_destructive_interference_size.html&gt;&lt;code&gt;std::hardware_destructive_interference_size&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/a&gt;
could have been called &lt;code&gt;std::cache_line&lt;/code&gt;.
&lt;a href=https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/container/span/subspan&gt;&lt;code&gt;std::span::subspan&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/a&gt;
could have used &lt;code&gt;opeartor[]&lt;/code&gt;. The standard algorithms are super wordy, because
they deal with iterator pairs. Oh my god, iterator pairs. They added
&lt;a href=https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/ranges.html&gt;&lt;code&gt;std::ranges&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/a&gt;, which do not
measure up to Rust&amp;rsquo;s
&lt;a href=https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/iter/trait.Iterator.html&gt;&lt;code&gt;Iterator&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/a&gt; at all!&lt;p&gt;I&amp;rsquo;m so mad about all this! The people in charge of C++ clearly, actively hate
their users!&lt;sup id=fnref:1&gt;&lt;a href=#fn:1 class=footnote-ref role=doc-noteref&gt;1&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/sup&gt; They want C++ to be as hard and unpleasant as
possible to use. Many brilliant people that I am lucky to consider friends and
colleagues, including Titus Winters, JeanHeyd Meneide, Matt Fowles-Kulukundis,
and Andy Soffer, have tried and mostly failed&lt;sup id=fnref:2&gt;&lt;a href=#fn:2 class=footnote-ref role=doc-noteref&gt;2&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/sup&gt; to improve the language.&lt;p&gt;This is much to say that I believe C++ in its current form is unfixable. But
that&amp;rsquo;s only due to the small-mindedness of a small cabal based out of Redmond.
What if we could do whatever we wanted? What if we used C++&amp;rsquo;s incredible
library-building language features to build a brand-new language?&lt;p&gt;For the last year-or-so I&amp;rsquo;ve been playing with a wild idea: what would C++ look
like if we did it over again? Starting from an empty C++20 file with no access
to the standard library, what can we build in its place?&lt;h2 id=starting-over&gt;&lt;a href=#starting-over&gt;Starting Over&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;p&gt;Titus started Abseil while at Google, whose namespace, &lt;code&gt;absl&lt;/code&gt;, is sometimes said
to stand for &amp;ldquo;a better standard library&amp;rdquo;&lt;sup id=fnref:3&gt;&lt;a href=#fn:3 class=footnote-ref role=doc-noteref&gt;3&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/sup&gt;. To me, Abseil is important
because it was an attempt to work with the existing standard library and make it
better, while retaining a high level of implementation quality that a C++ shop&amp;rsquo;s
home-grown utility library won&amp;rsquo;t have, and a uniformity of vision that
&lt;a href=https://www.boost.org/&gt;Boost&lt;/a&gt; is too all-over-the-place to achieve.&lt;p&gt;Rather than trying to coexist with the standard library, I want to surpass it.
As a form of performance art, I want to discover what the standard library would
look like if we designed it &lt;em&gt;today&lt;/em&gt;, in 2025.&lt;p&gt;In this sense, I want to build something that isn&amp;rsquo;t just &lt;em&gt;better&lt;/em&gt;. It should be
the C++ standard library from the best possible world. It is the best possible
library. This is why my library&amp;rsquo;s namespace is &lt;code&gt;best&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;p&gt;In general, I am trying not to directly copy either what C++, or Abseil, or
Rust, or Go did. However, each of them has really interesting ideas, and the
best library probably lies in some middle-ground somewhere.&lt;p&gt;The rest of this post will be about what I have achieved with &lt;code&gt;best&lt;/code&gt; so far, and
where I want to take it. You can look at the code
&lt;a href=https://github.com/mcy/best&gt;here&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;h3 id=building-a-foundation&gt;&lt;a href=#building-a-foundation&gt;Building a Foundation&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;We&amp;rsquo;re throwing out everything, and that includes &lt;code&gt;&amp;lt;type_traits&gt;&lt;/code&gt;. This is a
header which shows its age: alias templates were&amp;rsquo;t added until C++14, and
variable templates were added in C++17. As a result, many things that really
aught to be concepts have names like &lt;code&gt;best::is_same_v&lt;/code&gt;. All of these now have
concept equivalents in &lt;code&gt;&amp;lt;concepts&gt;&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;p&gt;I have opted to try to classify type traits into separate headers to make them
easier to find. They all live under &lt;code&gt;//best/meta/traits&lt;/code&gt;, and they form the
leaves of the dependency graph.&lt;p&gt;For example, &lt;code&gt;arrays.h&lt;/code&gt; contains all of the array traits, such as
&lt;code&gt;best::is_array&lt;/code&gt;, &lt;code&gt;best::un_array&lt;/code&gt; (to remove an array extent), and
&lt;code&gt;best::as_array&lt;/code&gt;, which applies an extent to a type T, such that
&lt;code&gt;best::as_array&amp;lt;T, 0&gt;&lt;/code&gt; is not an error.&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;types.h&lt;/code&gt; contains very low-level metaprogramming helpers, such as:&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;&lt;code&gt;best::id&lt;/code&gt; and &lt;code&gt;best::val&lt;/code&gt;, the identity traits for type- and value-kinded
traits.&lt;li&gt;&lt;code&gt;best::same&amp;lt;...&gt;&lt;/code&gt;, which returns whether an entire &lt;em&gt;pack&lt;/em&gt; of types is all
equal.&lt;li&gt;&lt;code&gt;best::lie&lt;/code&gt;, our version of &lt;code&gt;std::declval&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;li&gt;&lt;code&gt;best::select&lt;/code&gt;, our &lt;code&gt;std::conditional_t&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;li&gt;&lt;code&gt;best::abridge&lt;/code&gt;, a &amp;ldquo;symbol compression&amp;rdquo; mechanism for shortening the names of
otherwise huge symbols.&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;funcs.h&lt;/code&gt; provides &lt;code&gt;best::tame&lt;/code&gt;, which removes the qualifiers from an
&lt;a href=https://www.open-std.org/jtc1/sc22/wg21/docs/papers/2015/p0172r0.html&gt;abominable function type&lt;/a&gt;.
&lt;code&gt;quals.h&lt;/code&gt; provides &lt;code&gt;best::qualifies_to&lt;/code&gt;, necessary for determining if a type is
&amp;ldquo;more const&amp;rdquo; than another. &lt;code&gt;empty.h&lt;/code&gt; provides a standard empty type that
interoperates cleanly with &lt;code&gt;void&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;p&gt;On top of the type traits is the metaprogramming library &lt;code&gt;//best/meta&lt;/code&gt;, which
includes generalized constructibility traits in &lt;code&gt;init.h&lt;/code&gt; (e.g., to check that
you can, in fact, initialize a &lt;code&gt;T&amp;&lt;/code&gt; from a &lt;code&gt;T&amp;&amp;&lt;/code&gt;, for example). &lt;code&gt;tlist.h&lt;/code&gt;
provides a very general type-level heterogenous list abstraction; a parameter
pack as-a-type.&lt;p&gt;The other part of &amp;ldquo;the foundation&amp;rdquo; is &lt;code&gt;//best/base&lt;/code&gt;, which mostly provides
access to intrinsics, portability helpers, macros, and &amp;ldquo;tag types&amp;rdquo; such as our
versions of &lt;code&gt;std::in_place&lt;/code&gt;. For example, &lt;code&gt;macro.h&lt;/code&gt; provides &lt;code&gt;BEST_STRINGIFY()&lt;/code&gt;,
&lt;code&gt;port.h&lt;/code&gt; provides &lt;code&gt;BEST_HAS_INCLUDE()&lt;/code&gt;, and &lt;code&gt;hint.h&lt;/code&gt; provides
&lt;code&gt;best::unreachable()&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;guard.h&lt;/code&gt; provides our version of the Rust &lt;code&gt;?&lt;/code&gt; operator, which is not an
expression because statement expressions are broken in Clang.&lt;p&gt;Finally, within &lt;code&gt;//best/container&lt;/code&gt; we find &lt;code&gt;best::object&lt;/code&gt;, a special type for
turning any C++ type into an object (i.e., a type that you can form a reference
to). This is useful for manipulating any type generically, without tripping over
the assign-through semantics of references. For example, &lt;code&gt;best::object&amp;lt;T&amp;&gt;&lt;/code&gt; is
essentially a pointer.&lt;h3 id=adt-containers&gt;&lt;a href=#adt-containers&gt;&amp;ldquo;ADT&amp;rdquo; Containers&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;On top of this foundation we build the basic algebraic data types of &lt;code&gt;best&lt;/code&gt;:
&lt;code&gt;best::row&lt;/code&gt; and &lt;code&gt;best::choice&lt;/code&gt;, which replace &lt;code&gt;std::tuple&lt;/code&gt; and &lt;code&gt;std::variant&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;best::row&amp;lt;A, B, C&gt;&lt;/code&gt; is a heterogenous collection of values, stored inside of
&lt;code&gt;best::object&lt;/code&gt;s. This means that &lt;code&gt;best::row&amp;lt;int&amp;&gt;&lt;/code&gt; has natural rebinding, rather
than assign-through, semantics.&lt;p&gt;Accessing elements is done with &lt;code&gt;at()&lt;/code&gt;: &lt;code&gt;my_row.at&amp;lt;0&gt;()&lt;/code&gt; returns a reference to
the first element. Getting the first element is so common that you can also use
&lt;code&gt;my_row.first()&lt;/code&gt;. Using &lt;code&gt;my_row.object&amp;lt;0&gt;()&lt;/code&gt; will return a reference to a
&lt;code&gt;best::object&lt;/code&gt; instead, which can be used for rebinding references. For example:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:1&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-cpp highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=kt&gt;int&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;x&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=mi&gt;0&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;y&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=mi&gt;0&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;best&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;::&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;row&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;lt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=kt&gt;int&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;amp;&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;a&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;x&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;};&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;a&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;at&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;lt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mi&gt;0&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;()&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=mi&gt;42&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt;     &lt;span class=c1&gt;// Writes to x.
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;a&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;object&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;lt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mi&gt;0&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;()&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;y&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt;  &lt;span class=c1&gt;// Rebinds a.0 to y.
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;a&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;at&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;lt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mi&gt;0&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;()&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=mi&gt;2&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;*&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;x&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt;    &lt;span class=c1&gt;// Writes to y.
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:1&gt;C++&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;There is also &lt;code&gt;second()&lt;/code&gt; and &lt;code&gt;last()&lt;/code&gt;, for the other two most common elements to
access.&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;best::row&lt;/code&gt; is named so in reference to database rows: it provides many
operations for slicing and dicing that &lt;code&gt;std::tuple&lt;/code&gt; does not.&lt;p&gt;For example, in addition to extracting single elements, it&amp;rsquo;s also possible to
access contiguous subsequences, using &lt;code&gt;best::bounds&lt;/code&gt;:
&lt;code&gt;a.at&amp;lt;best::bounds{.start = 1, .end = 10}&gt;()&lt;/code&gt;! There are also a plethora of
mutation operations:&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;&lt;code&gt;a + b&lt;/code&gt; concatenates tuples, copying or moving as appropriate
(&lt;code&gt;a + BEST_MOVE(b)&lt;/code&gt; will move out of the elements of &lt;code&gt;b&lt;/code&gt;, for example).&lt;li&gt;&lt;code&gt;a.push(x)&lt;/code&gt; returns a copy of &lt;code&gt;a&lt;/code&gt; with &lt;code&gt;x&lt;/code&gt; appended, while &lt;code&gt;a.insert&amp;lt;n&gt;(x)&lt;/code&gt;
does the same at an arbitrary index.&lt;li&gt;&lt;code&gt;a.update&amp;lt;n&gt;(x)&lt;/code&gt; &lt;em&gt;replaces&lt;/em&gt; the &lt;code&gt;n&lt;/code&gt;th element with &lt;code&gt;x&lt;/code&gt;, potentially of a
different type.&lt;li&gt;&lt;code&gt;a.remove&amp;lt;n&gt;()&lt;/code&gt; deletes the &lt;code&gt;n&lt;/code&gt;th element, while &lt;code&gt;a.erase&amp;lt;...&gt;()&lt;/code&gt; deletes a
contiguous range.&lt;li&gt;&lt;code&gt;a.splice&amp;lt;best::bounds{...}&gt;(...)&lt;/code&gt; splices a row into another row, offering a
general replace/delete operation that all of the above operations are
implemented in terms of.&lt;li&gt;&lt;code&gt;gather()&lt;/code&gt; and &lt;code&gt;scatter()&lt;/code&gt; are even more general, allowing for non-contiguous
indexing.&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;p&gt;Meanwhile, &lt;code&gt;std::apply&lt;/code&gt; is a method now: &lt;code&gt;a.apply(f)&lt;/code&gt; calls &lt;code&gt;f&lt;/code&gt; with &lt;code&gt;a&lt;/code&gt;&amp;rsquo;s
elements as its arguments. &lt;code&gt;a.each(f)&lt;/code&gt; is similar, but instead expands to &lt;code&gt;n&lt;/code&gt;
unary calls of &lt;code&gt;f&lt;/code&gt;, one with each element.&lt;p&gt;And &lt;em&gt;of course&lt;/em&gt;, &lt;code&gt;best::row&lt;/code&gt; supports structured bindings.&lt;p&gt;Meanwhile, &lt;code&gt;best::choice&amp;lt;A, B, C&gt;&lt;/code&gt; contains precisely one value from various
types. There is an underlying &lt;code&gt;best::pun&amp;lt;A, B, C&gt;&lt;/code&gt; type that implements a
variadic untagged union that works around many of C++&amp;rsquo;s bugs relating to unions
with members of non-trivial type.&lt;p&gt;The most common way to operate on a choice is to &lt;code&gt;match&lt;/code&gt; on it:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:2&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-cpp highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;best&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;::&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;choice&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;lt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=kt&gt;int&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;*&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=kt&gt;int&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=kt&gt;void&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;z&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=mi&gt;42&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=kt&gt;int&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;result&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;z&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;match&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=p&gt;[](&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=kt&gt;int&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;x&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=k&gt;return&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;x&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;},&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=p&gt;[](&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=kt&gt;int&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;*&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;x&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=k&gt;return&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;*&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;x&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;},&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=p&gt;[]&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=k&gt;return&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=mi&gt;0&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;);&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:2&gt;C++&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;Which case gets called here is chosen by overload resolution, allowing us to
write a default case as &lt;code&gt;[](auto&amp;&amp;) { ... }&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;p&gt;Which variant is currently selected can be checked with &lt;code&gt;z.which()&lt;/code&gt;, while
specific variants can be accessed with &lt;code&gt;z.at()&lt;/code&gt;, just like a &lt;code&gt;best::row&lt;/code&gt;, except
that it returns a &lt;code&gt;best::option&amp;lt;T&amp;&gt;&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;best::choice&lt;/code&gt; is what all of the other sum types, like &lt;code&gt;best::option&lt;/code&gt; and
&lt;code&gt;best::result&lt;/code&gt;, are built out of. All of the clever layout optimizations live
here.&lt;p&gt;Speaking of &lt;code&gt;best::option&amp;lt;T&gt;&lt;/code&gt;, that&amp;rsquo;s our option type. It&amp;rsquo;s close in spirit to
what &lt;a href=https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/option/enum.Option.html&gt;&lt;code&gt;Option&amp;lt;T&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/a&gt; is in
Rust. &lt;code&gt;best&lt;/code&gt; has a generic niche mechanism that user types can opt into,
allowing &lt;code&gt;best::option&amp;lt;T&amp;&gt;&lt;/code&gt; to be the same size as a pointer, using &lt;code&gt;nullptr&lt;/code&gt;
for the &lt;code&gt;best::none&lt;/code&gt; variant.&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;best::option&lt;/code&gt; provides the usual transformation operations: &lt;code&gt;map&lt;/code&gt;, &lt;code&gt;then&lt;/code&gt;,
&lt;code&gt;filter&lt;/code&gt;. Emptiness can be checked with &lt;code&gt;is_empty()&lt;/code&gt; or &lt;code&gt;has_value()&lt;/code&gt;. You can
even pass a predicate to &lt;code&gt;has_value()&lt;/code&gt; to check the value with, if it&amp;rsquo;s present:
&lt;code&gt;x.has_value([](auto&amp; x) { return x == 42; })&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;p&gt;The value can be accessed using &lt;code&gt;operator*&lt;/code&gt; and &lt;code&gt;operator-&gt;&lt;/code&gt;, like
&lt;code&gt;std::optional&lt;/code&gt;; however, this operation is checked, instead of causing UB if
the option is empty. &lt;code&gt;value_or()&lt;/code&gt; can be used to unwrap with a default; the
default can be any number of arguments, which are used to construct the default,
or even a callback. For example:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:3&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-cpp highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;best&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;::&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;option&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;lt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;Foo&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;x&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;// Pass arguments to the constructor.
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;do_something&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;x&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;value_or&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;args&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;to&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;foo&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;));&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;// Execute arbitrary logic if the value is missing.
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;do_something&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;x&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;value_or&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;([]&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=k&gt;return&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nf&gt;Foo&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(...);&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}))&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:3&gt;C++&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;best::option&amp;lt;void&gt;&lt;/code&gt; also Just Works (in fact, &lt;code&gt;best::option&amp;lt;T&gt;&lt;/code&gt; is a
&lt;code&gt;best::choice&amp;lt;void, T&gt;&lt;/code&gt; internally), allowing for truly generic manipulation of
optional results.&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;best::result&amp;lt;T, E&gt;&lt;/code&gt; is, unsurprisingly, the analogue of Rust&amp;rsquo;s
&lt;a href=https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/result/enum.Result.html&gt;&lt;code&gt;Result&amp;lt;T, E&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/a&gt;. Because
it&amp;rsquo;s a &lt;code&gt;best::choice&lt;/code&gt; internally, &lt;code&gt;best::result&amp;lt;void, E&gt;&lt;/code&gt; works as you might
expect, and is a common return value for I/O operations.&lt;p&gt;It&amp;rsquo;s very similar to &lt;code&gt;best::option&lt;/code&gt;, including offering &lt;code&gt;operator-&gt;&lt;/code&gt; for
accessing the &amp;ldquo;ok&amp;rdquo; variant. This enables succinct idioms:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:4&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-cpp highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;if&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;auto&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;r&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;fallible&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;())&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;r&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;-&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;do_something&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;();&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=k&gt;else&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;best&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;::&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;println&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=s&gt;&amp;#34;{}&amp;#34;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;*&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;r&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;err&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;());&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:4&gt;C++&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;r.ok()&lt;/code&gt; and &lt;code&gt;r.err()&lt;/code&gt; return &lt;code&gt;best::option&lt;/code&gt;s containing references to the ok
and error variants, depending on which is actually present; meanwhile, a
&lt;code&gt;best::option&lt;/code&gt; can be converted into a &lt;code&gt;best::result&lt;/code&gt; using &lt;code&gt;ok_or()&lt;/code&gt; or
&lt;code&gt;err_or()&lt;/code&gt;, just like in Rust.&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;best::result&lt;/code&gt;s are constructed using &lt;code&gt;best::ok&lt;/code&gt; and &lt;code&gt;best::err&lt;/code&gt;. For example:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:5&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-cpp highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;best&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;::&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;result&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;lt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;Foo&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;Error&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;r&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;best&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;::&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;ok&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;args&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;to&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;foo&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;);&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:5&gt;C++&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;These internally use &lt;code&gt;best::args&lt;/code&gt;, a wrapper over &lt;code&gt;best::row&lt;/code&gt; that represents a
&amp;ldquo;delayed initialization&amp;rdquo; that can be stored in a value. It will implicitly
convert into any type that can be constructed from its elements. For example:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:6&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-cpp highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;Foo&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;foo&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;best&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;::&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;args&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;args&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;to&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;foo&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;);&lt;/span&gt;  &lt;span class=c1&gt;// Calls Foo::Foo(args, to, foo).
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:6&gt;C++&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;Also, every one of the above types is a structural type, meaning it can be used
for non-type template parameters!&lt;h3 id=memory-and-pointers&gt;&lt;a href=#memory-and-pointers&gt;Memory and Pointers&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;Of course, all of these ADTs need to be built on top of pointer operations,
which is where &lt;code&gt;//best/memory&lt;/code&gt; comes in. &lt;code&gt;best::ptr&amp;lt;T&gt;&lt;/code&gt; is a generalized pointer
type that provides many of the same operations as Rust&amp;rsquo;s raw pointers, including
offsetting, copying, and indexing. Like Rust pointers, &lt;code&gt;best::ptr&amp;lt;T&gt;&lt;/code&gt; can be a
fat pointer, i.e., it can carry additional metadata on top of the pointer. For
example, &lt;code&gt;best::ptr&amp;lt;int[]&gt;&lt;/code&gt; remembers the size of the array.&lt;p&gt;Providing metadata for a &lt;code&gt;best::ptr&lt;/code&gt; is done through a member alias called
&lt;code&gt;BestPtrMetadata&lt;/code&gt;. This alias should be private, which &lt;code&gt;best&lt;/code&gt; is given access to
by befriending &lt;code&gt;best::access&lt;/code&gt;. Types with custom metadata will usually not be
directly constructible (because they are of variable size), and must be
manipulated exclusively through types like &lt;code&gt;best::ptr&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;p&gt;Specifying custom metadata allows specifying what the pointer dereferences to.
For example, &lt;code&gt;best::ptr&amp;lt;int[]&gt;&lt;/code&gt; dereferences to a &lt;code&gt;best::span&amp;lt;int&gt;&lt;/code&gt;, meaning
that all the span operations are accessible through &lt;code&gt;operator-&gt;&lt;/code&gt;: for example,
&lt;code&gt;my_array_ptr-&gt;first()&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;p&gt;Most of this may seem a bit over-complicated, since ordinary C++ raw pointers
and references are fine for most uses. However, &lt;code&gt;best::ptr&lt;/code&gt; is the foundation
upon which &lt;code&gt;best::box&amp;lt;T&gt;&lt;/code&gt; is built on. &lt;code&gt;best::box&amp;lt;T&gt;&lt;/code&gt; is a replacement for
&lt;a href=https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/memory/unique_ptr.html&gt;&lt;code&gt;std::unique_ptr&amp;lt;T&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/a&gt;
that fixes its const correctness and adds Rust
&lt;a href=https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/boxed/struct.Box.html&gt;&lt;code&gt;Box&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/a&gt;-like helpers.
&lt;code&gt;best::box&amp;lt;T[]&gt;&lt;/code&gt; also works, but unlike &lt;code&gt;std::unique_ptr&amp;lt;T[]&gt;&lt;/code&gt;, it remembers its
size, just like &lt;code&gt;best::ptr&amp;lt;T[]&gt;&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;best::box&lt;/code&gt; is parameterized by its allocator, which must satisfy
&lt;code&gt;best::allocator&lt;/code&gt;, a much less insane API than what
&lt;a href=https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/memory/allocator.html&gt;&lt;code&gt;std::allocator&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/a&gt;
offers. &lt;code&gt;best::malloc&lt;/code&gt; is a singleton allocator representing the system
allocator.&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;best::span&amp;lt;T&gt;&lt;/code&gt;, mentioned before, is the contiguous memory abstraction,
replacing &lt;a href=https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/container/span.html&gt;&lt;code&gt;std::span&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/a&gt;.
Like &lt;code&gt;std::span&lt;/code&gt;, &lt;code&gt;best::span&amp;lt;T, n&gt;&lt;/code&gt; is a fixed-length span of &lt;code&gt;n&lt;/code&gt; elements.
Unlike &lt;code&gt;std::span&lt;/code&gt;, the second parameter is a &lt;code&gt;best::option&amp;lt;size_t&gt;&lt;/code&gt;, not a
&lt;code&gt;size_t&lt;/code&gt; that uses &lt;code&gt;-1&lt;/code&gt; as a sentinel.&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;best::span&amp;lt;T&gt;&lt;/code&gt; tries to approximate the API of
&lt;a href=https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/primitive.slice.html&gt;Rust slices&lt;/a&gt;, providing
indexing, slicing, splicing, search, sort, and more. Naturally, it&amp;rsquo;s also
iterable, both forwards and backwards, and provides splitting iterators, just
like Rust.&lt;p&gt;Slicing and indexing is always bounds-checked. Indexing can be done with
&lt;code&gt;size_t&lt;/code&gt; values, while slicing uses a &lt;code&gt;best::bounds&lt;/code&gt;:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:7&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-cpp highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;best&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;::&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;span&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;lt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=kt&gt;int&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;xs&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;...;&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;auto&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;x&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;xs&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;[&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mi&gt;5&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;];&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;auto&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;ys&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;xs&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;[{.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;start&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=mi&gt;1&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;end&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=mi&gt;6&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}];&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:7&gt;C++&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;best::bounds&lt;/code&gt; is a generic mechanism for specifying slicing bounds, similar to
Rust&amp;rsquo;s &lt;a href=https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/ops/struct.Range.html&gt;range types&lt;/a&gt;. You
can specify the start and end (exclusive), like &lt;code&gt;x..y&lt;/code&gt; in Rust. You can also
specify an inclusive end using &lt;code&gt;.inclusive_end = 5&lt;/code&gt;, equivalent to Rust&amp;rsquo;s
&lt;code&gt;x..=y&lt;/code&gt;. And you can specify a count, like C++&amp;rsquo;s slicing operations prefer:
&lt;code&gt;{.start = 1, .count = 5}&lt;/code&gt;. &lt;code&gt;best::bounds&lt;/code&gt; itself provides all of the necessary
helpers for performing bounds checks and crashing with a nice error message.
&lt;code&gt;best::bounds&lt;/code&gt; is also iterable, as we&amp;rsquo;ll see shortly.&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;best::layout&lt;/code&gt; is a copy of Rust&amp;rsquo;s
&lt;a href=https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/alloc/struct.Layout.html&gt;&lt;code&gt;Layout&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/a&gt; type,
providing similar helpers for performing C++-specific size and address
calculations.&lt;h3 id=iterators&gt;&lt;a href=#iterators&gt;Iterators&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;C++ iterator pairs suck. C++ ranges suck. &lt;code&gt;best&lt;/code&gt; provides a new paradigm for
iteration that is essentially just Rust
&lt;a href=https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/iter/trait.Iterator.html&gt;&lt;code&gt;Iterator&lt;/code&gt;s&lt;/a&gt; hammered
into a C++ shape. This library lives in &lt;code&gt;//best/iter&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;p&gt;To define an iterator, you define an &lt;em&gt;iterator implementation type&lt;/em&gt;, which must
define a member function named &lt;code&gt;next()&lt;/code&gt; that returns a &lt;code&gt;best::option&lt;/code&gt;:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:8&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-cpp highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;class&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nc&gt;my_iter_impl&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=k&gt;final&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=k&gt;public&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;:&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;    &lt;span class=n&gt;best&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;::&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;option&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;lt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=kt&gt;int&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;next&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;();&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;};&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:8&gt;C++&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;This type is an implementation detail; the actual iterator type is
&lt;code&gt;best::iter&amp;lt;my_iter_impl&gt;&lt;/code&gt;. &lt;code&gt;best::iter&lt;/code&gt; provides all kinds of helpers, just
like &lt;code&gt;Iterator&lt;/code&gt;, for adapting the iterator or consuming items out of it.&lt;p&gt;Iterators can override the behavior of some of these adaptors to be more
efficient, such as for making &lt;code&gt;count()&lt;/code&gt; constant-time rather than linear.
Iterators can also offer extra methods if they define the member alias
&lt;code&gt;BestIterArrow&lt;/code&gt;; for example, the iterators for &lt;code&gt;best::span&lt;/code&gt; have a &lt;code&gt;-&gt;rest()&lt;/code&gt;
method for returning the part of the slice that has not been yielded by &lt;code&gt;next()&lt;/code&gt;
yet.&lt;p&gt;One of the most important extension points is &lt;code&gt;size_hint()&lt;/code&gt;, analogous to
&lt;a href=https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/iter/trait.Iterator.html#method.size_hint&gt;&lt;code&gt;Iterator::size_hint()&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/a&gt;,
for right-sizing containers that the iterator is converted to, such as a
&lt;code&gt;best::vec&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;p&gt;And of course, &lt;code&gt;best::iter&lt;/code&gt; provides &lt;code&gt;begin/end&lt;/code&gt; so that it can be used in a C++
range-for loop, just like C++20 ranges do. &lt;code&gt;best::int_range&amp;lt;I&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;sup id=fnref:4&gt;&lt;a href=#fn:4 class=footnote-ref role=doc-noteref&gt;4&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/sup&gt;,
which &lt;code&gt;best::bounds&lt;/code&gt; is an instantiation of, is also an iterator, and can be
used much like Rust ranges would:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:9&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-cpp highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;for&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;auto&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nl&gt;i&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;:&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;best&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;::&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;int_range&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;lt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=kt&gt;int&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;{.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;start&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=mi&gt;1&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;count&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=mi&gt;200&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;})&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=c1&gt;// ...
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:9&gt;C++&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;best::int_range&lt;/code&gt; will carefully handle all of the awkward corner cases around
overflow, such as &lt;code&gt;best::int_range&amp;lt;uint8_t&gt;{.end_inclusive = 255}&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;h3 id=heap-containers&gt;&lt;a href=#heap-containers&gt;Heap Containers&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;Iterators brings us to the most complex container type that&amp;rsquo;s checked in right
now, &lt;code&gt;best::vec&lt;/code&gt;. Not only can you customize its allocator type, but you can
customize its small vector optimization type.&lt;p&gt;In &lt;code&gt;libc++&lt;/code&gt;, &lt;code&gt;std::string&lt;/code&gt;s of at most 23 bytes are stored &lt;em&gt;inline&lt;/em&gt;, meaning
that the strings&amp;rsquo;s own storage, rather than heap storage, is used to hold them.
&lt;code&gt;best::vec&lt;/code&gt; generalizes this, by allowing any trivially copyable type to be
inlined. Thus, a &lt;code&gt;best::vec&amp;lt;int&gt;&lt;/code&gt; will hold at most five &lt;code&gt;int&lt;/code&gt;s inline, on
64-bit targets.&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;best::vec&lt;/code&gt; mostly copies the APIs of &lt;code&gt;std::vector&lt;/code&gt; and Rust&amp;rsquo;s
&lt;a href=https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/vec/struct.Vec.html&gt;&lt;code&gt;Vec&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/a&gt;. Indexing and slicing
works the same as with &lt;code&gt;best::span&lt;/code&gt;, and all of the &lt;code&gt;best::span&lt;/code&gt; operations can
be accessed through &lt;code&gt;-&gt;&lt;/code&gt;, allowing for things like &lt;code&gt;my_vec-&gt;sort(...)&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;p&gt;I have an active (failing) PR which adds &lt;code&gt;best::table&amp;lt;K, V&gt;&lt;/code&gt;, a general hash
table implementation that can be used as either a map or a set. Internally it&amp;rsquo;s
backed by a Swisstable&lt;sup id=fnref:5&gt;&lt;a href=#fn:5 class=footnote-ref role=doc-noteref&gt;5&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/sup&gt; implementation. Its API resembles neither
&lt;code&gt;std::unordered_map&lt;/code&gt;, &lt;code&gt;absl::flat_hash_map&lt;/code&gt;, or Rust&amp;rsquo;s
&lt;a href=https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/collections/struct.HashMap.html&gt;&lt;code&gt;HashMap&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/a&gt;.
Instead, everything is done through a general entry API, similar to that of
Rust, but optimized for clarity and minimizing hash lookups. I want to get it
merged soonish.&lt;p&gt;Beyond &lt;code&gt;best::table&lt;/code&gt;, I plan to add &lt;em&gt;at least&lt;/em&gt; the following containers:&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;&lt;code&gt;best::tree&lt;/code&gt;, a btree map/set with a similar API.&lt;li&gt;&lt;code&gt;best::heap&lt;/code&gt;, a simple min-heap implementation.&lt;li&gt;&lt;code&gt;best::lru&lt;/code&gt;, a &lt;code&gt;best::table&lt;/code&gt; with a linked list running through it for
in-order iteration and oldest-member eviction.&lt;li&gt;&lt;code&gt;best::ring&lt;/code&gt;, a ring buffer like
&lt;a href=https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/collections/struct.VecDeque.html&gt;&lt;code&gt;VecDeque&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;li&gt;&lt;code&gt;best::trie&lt;/code&gt;, a port of my &lt;a href=https://docs.rs/twie/latest/twie/&gt;&lt;code&gt;twie&lt;/code&gt; crate&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;p&gt;Possible other ideas: &lt;a href=https://research.swtch.com/sparse&gt;Russ&amp;rsquo;s sparse array&lt;/a&gt;,
splay trees, something like Java&amp;rsquo;s
&lt;a href=https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/EnumMap.html&gt;&lt;code&gt;EnumMap&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/a&gt;,
bitset types, and so on.&lt;h3 id=text-handling&gt;&lt;a href=#text-handling&gt;Text Handling&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;best&lt;/code&gt;&amp;rsquo;s string handling is intended to resemble Rust&amp;rsquo;s as much as possible; it
lives within &lt;code&gt;//best/text&lt;/code&gt;. &lt;code&gt;best::rune&lt;/code&gt; is the Unicode scalar type, which is
such that it is &lt;em&gt;always&lt;/em&gt; within the valid range for a Unicode scalar, but
including the unpaired surrogates. It offers a number of relatively simple
character operations, but I plan to extend it to all kinds of character classes
in the future.&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;best::str&lt;/code&gt; is our replacement for
&lt;a href=https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/string/basic_string_view.html&gt;&lt;code&gt;best::string_view&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/a&gt;,
close to Rust&amp;rsquo;s &lt;a href=https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/primitive.str.html&gt;&lt;code&gt;str&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/a&gt;: a
sequence of valid UTF-8 bytes, with all kinds of string manipulation operations,
such as rune search, splitting, indexing, and so on.&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;best::rune&lt;/code&gt; and &lt;code&gt;best::str&lt;/code&gt; use compiler extensions to ensure that when
constructed from literals, they&amp;rsquo;re constructed from &lt;em&gt;valid&lt;/em&gt; literals. This means
that the following won&amp;rsquo;t compile!&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:10&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-cpp highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;best&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;::&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;str&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;invalid&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=s&gt;&amp;#34;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=se&gt;\xFF&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=s&gt;&amp;#34;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:10&gt;C++&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;best::str&lt;/code&gt; is a &lt;code&gt;best::span&lt;/code&gt; under the hood, which can be accessed and
manipulated the same way as the underlying &lt;code&gt;&amp;[u8]&lt;/code&gt; to &lt;code&gt;&amp;amp;str&lt;/code&gt; is.&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;best::strbuf&lt;/code&gt; is our
&lt;a href=https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/string/basic_string.html&gt;&lt;code&gt;std::string&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/a&gt;
equivalent. There isn&amp;rsquo;t very much to say about it, because it works just like
you&amp;rsquo;d expect, and provides a Rust
&lt;a href=https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/string/struct.String.html&gt;&lt;code&gt;String&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/a&gt;-like API.&lt;p&gt;Where this library really shines is that everything is parametrized over
encodings. &lt;code&gt;best::str&lt;/code&gt; is actually a &lt;code&gt;best::text&amp;lt;best::utf8&gt;&lt;/code&gt;; &lt;code&gt;best::str16&lt;/code&gt; is
then &lt;code&gt;best::text&amp;lt;best::utf16&gt;&lt;/code&gt;. You can write your own text encodings, too, so
long as they are relatively tame and you provide rune encode/decode for them.
&lt;code&gt;best::encoding&lt;/code&gt; is the concept&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;best::text&lt;/code&gt; is always validly encoded; however, sometimes, that&amp;rsquo;s not possible.
For this reason we have &lt;code&gt;best::pretext&lt;/code&gt;, which is &amp;ldquo;presumed validly encoded&amp;rdquo;;
its operations can fail or produce replacement characters if invalid code units
are found. There is no &lt;code&gt;best::pretextbuf&lt;/code&gt;; instead, you would generally use
something like a &lt;code&gt;best::vec&amp;lt;uint8_t&gt;&lt;/code&gt; instead.&lt;p&gt;Unlike C++, the fact that a &lt;code&gt;best::textbuf&lt;/code&gt; is a &lt;code&gt;best::vec&lt;/code&gt; under the hood is
part of the public interface, allowing for cheap conversions and, of course, we
get &lt;code&gt;best::vec&lt;/code&gt;&amp;rsquo;s small vector optimization for free.&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;best&lt;/code&gt; provides the following encodings out of the box: &lt;code&gt;best::utf8&lt;/code&gt;,
&lt;code&gt;best::utf16&lt;/code&gt;, &lt;code&gt;best::utf32&lt;/code&gt;, &lt;code&gt;best::wtf8&lt;/code&gt;, &lt;code&gt;best::ascii&lt;/code&gt;, and &lt;code&gt;best::latin1&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;h3 id=formatting&gt;&lt;a href=#formatting&gt;Formatting&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;//best/text:format&lt;/code&gt; provides a Rust &lt;code&gt;format!()&lt;/code&gt;-style text formatting library.
It&amp;rsquo;s as easy as:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:11&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-cpp highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;auto&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;str&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;best&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;::&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;format&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=s&gt;&amp;#34;my number: 0x{:08x}&amp;#34;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;n&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;);&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:11&gt;C++&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;Through the power of compiler extensions and &lt;code&gt;constexpr&lt;/code&gt;, the format is actually
checked at compile time!&lt;p&gt;The available formats are the same as Rust&amp;rsquo;s, including the &lt;code&gt;{}&lt;/code&gt; vs &lt;code&gt;{:?}&lt;/code&gt;
distinction. But it&amp;rsquo;s actually way more flexible. You can use any ASCII letter,
and types can provide multiple custom formatting schemes using letters. By
convention, &lt;code&gt;x&lt;/code&gt;, &lt;code&gt;X&lt;/code&gt;, &lt;code&gt;b&lt;/code&gt;, and &lt;code&gt;o&lt;/code&gt; all mean numeric bases. &lt;code&gt;q&lt;/code&gt; will quote
strings, runes, and other text objects; &lt;code&gt;p&lt;/code&gt; will print pointer addresses.&lt;p&gt;The special format &lt;code&gt;{:!}&lt;/code&gt; &amp;ldquo;forwards from above&amp;rdquo;; when used in a formatting
implementation, it uses the format specifier the caller used. This is useful for
causing formats to be &amp;ldquo;passed through&amp;rdquo;, such as when printing lists or
&lt;code&gt;best::option&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;p&gt;Any type can be made formattable by providing a friend template ADL extension
(FTADLE) called &lt;code&gt;BestFmt&lt;/code&gt;. This is analogous to implementing a trait like
&lt;code&gt;fmt::Debug&lt;/code&gt; in Rust, however, all formatting operations use the same function;
this is similar to &lt;a href=https://pkg.go.dev/fmt#Formatter&gt;&lt;code&gt;fmt.Formatter&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/a&gt; in Go.&lt;p&gt;The &lt;code&gt;best::formatter&lt;/code&gt; type, which gets passed into &lt;code&gt;BestFmt&lt;/code&gt;, is similar to
Rust&amp;rsquo;s &lt;a href=https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/fmt/struct.Formatter.html&gt;&lt;code&gt;Formatter&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/a&gt;.
Beyond being a sink, it also exposes information on the specifier for the
formatting operation via &lt;code&gt;current_spec()&lt;/code&gt;, and helpers for printing indented
lists and blocks.&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;BestFmtQuery&lt;/code&gt; is a related FTADLE that is called to determine what the valid
format specifiers for this type are. This allows the format validator to reject
formats that a type does not support, such as formatting a &lt;code&gt;best::str&lt;/code&gt; with
&lt;code&gt;{:x}&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;best::format&lt;/code&gt; returns (or appends to) a &lt;code&gt;best::strbuf&lt;/code&gt;; &lt;code&gt;best::println&lt;/code&gt; and
&lt;code&gt;best::eprintln&lt;/code&gt; can be used to write to stdout and stderr.&lt;h3 id=reflection&gt;&lt;a href=#reflection&gt;Reflection&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;Within the metaprogramming library, &lt;code&gt;//best/meta:reflect&lt;/code&gt; offers a basic form of
reflection. It&amp;rsquo;s not C++26 reflection, because that&amp;rsquo;s wholely overkill. Instead,
it provides a method for introspecting the members of structs and enums.&lt;p&gt;For example, suppose that we want to have a default way of formatting arbitrary
&lt;a href=https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/language/aggregate_initialization.html&gt;aggregate&lt;/a&gt;
structs. The code for doing this is actually devilishly simple:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:12&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-cpp highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=kt&gt;void&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nf&gt;BestFmt&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;auto&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;amp;&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;fmt&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=k&gt;const&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;best&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;::&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;is_reflected_struct&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=k&gt;auto&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;amp;&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;value&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=c1&gt;// Reflect the type of the struct.
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;  &lt;span class=k&gt;auto&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;refl&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;best&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;::&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;reflect&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;lt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;decltype&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;value&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=c1&gt;// Start formatting a &amp;#34;record&amp;#34; (key-value pairs).
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;  &lt;span class=k&gt;auto&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;rec&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;fmt&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;record&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;refl&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;name&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;());&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=c1&gt;// For each field in the struct...
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;refl&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;each&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;([&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;amp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;](&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;auto&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;field&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;    &lt;span class=c1&gt;// Add a field to the formatting record...
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;    &lt;span class=n&gt;rec&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;field&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;      &lt;span class=n&gt;field&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;name&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(),&lt;/span&gt;   &lt;span class=c1&gt;// ...whose name is the field...
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;      &lt;span class=n&gt;value&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;-&amp;gt;*&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;field&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;  &lt;span class=c1&gt;// ...and with the appropriate value.
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;    &lt;span class=p&gt;);&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=p&gt;});&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:12&gt;C++&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;best::reflect&lt;/code&gt; provides access to the fields (or enum variants) of a
user-defined type that opts itself in by providing the &lt;code&gt;BestReflect&lt;/code&gt; FTADLE,
which tells the reflection framework what the fields are. The simplest version
of this FTADLE looks like this:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:13&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-cpp highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;friend&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=k&gt;constexpr&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=k&gt;auto&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nf&gt;BestReflect&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;auto&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;amp;&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;mirror&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;MyStruct&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;*&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=k&gt;return&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;mirror&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;infer&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;();&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:13&gt;C++&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;best::mirror&lt;/code&gt; is essentially a &amp;ldquo;reflection builder&amp;rdquo; that offers fine-grained
control over what reflection actually shows of a struct. This allows for hiding
fields, or attaching &lt;em&gt;tags&lt;/em&gt; to specific fields, which generic functions can then
introspect using &lt;code&gt;best::reflected_field::tags()&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;p&gt;The functions on &lt;code&gt;best::reflected_type&lt;/code&gt; allow iterating over and searching for
specific fields (or enum variants); these &lt;code&gt;best::reflected_field&lt;/code&gt;s provide
metadata about a field (such as its name) and allow accessing it, with the same
syntax as a pointer-to-member: &lt;code&gt;value-&gt;*field&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;p&gt;Explaining the full breadth (and implementation tricks) of &lt;code&gt;best::reflect&lt;/code&gt; would
be a post of its own, so I&amp;rsquo;ll leave it at that.&lt;h3 id=unit-tests-and-apps&gt;&lt;a href=#unit-tests-and-apps&gt;Unit Tests and Apps&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;best&lt;/code&gt; provides a unit testing framework under &lt;code&gt;//best/test&lt;/code&gt;, like any good
standard library should. To define a test, you define a special kind of global
variable:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:14&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-cpp highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;best&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;::&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;test&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;MyTest&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;[](&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;best&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;::&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;test&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;amp;&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;t&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=c1&gt;// Test code.
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;};&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:14&gt;C++&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;This is very similar to a Go unit test, which defines a function that starts
with &lt;code&gt;Test&lt;/code&gt; and takes a &lt;code&gt;*testing.T&lt;/code&gt; as its argument. The &lt;code&gt;best::test&amp;&lt;/code&gt; value
offers test assertions and test failures. Through the power of looking at
debuginfo, we can extract the name &lt;code&gt;MyTest&lt;/code&gt; from the binary, and use that as the
name of the test directly.&lt;p&gt;That&amp;rsquo;s right, this is a C++ test framework with &lt;em&gt;no macros at all&lt;/em&gt;!&lt;p&gt;Meanwhile, at &lt;code&gt;//best/cli&lt;/code&gt; we can find a robust CLI parsing library, in the
spirit of
&lt;a href=https://docs.rs/clap/latest/clap/_derive/index.html&gt;&lt;code&gt;#[derive(clap::Parser)]&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/a&gt;
and other similar Rust libraries. The way it works is you first define a
reflectable struct, whose fields correspond to CLI flags. A very basic example
of this can be found in &lt;code&gt;test.h&lt;/code&gt;, since test binaries define their own flags:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:15&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-cpp highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;struct&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nc&gt;test&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;::&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;flags&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=k&gt;final&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;best&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;::&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;vec&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;lt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;best&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;::&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;strbuf&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;skip&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;best&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;::&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;vec&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;lt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;best&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;::&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;strbuf&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;filters&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=k&gt;constexpr&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=k&gt;friend&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=k&gt;auto&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nf&gt;BestReflect&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;auto&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;amp;&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;m&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;flags&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;*&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;    &lt;span class=k&gt;return&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;m&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;infer&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;()&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;      &lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;with&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;best&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;::&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;cli&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;::&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;app&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;{.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;about&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=s&gt;&amp;#34;a best unit test binary&amp;#34;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;})&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;      &lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;with&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;amp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;flags&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;::&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;skip&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;            &lt;span class=n&gt;best&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;::&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;cli&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;::&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;flag&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;              &lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;arg&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=s&gt;&amp;#34;FILTER&amp;#34;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;              &lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;help&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=s&gt;&amp;#34;Skip tests whose names contain FILTER&amp;#34;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;            &lt;span class=p&gt;})&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;      &lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;with&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;amp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;flags&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;::&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;filters&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;            &lt;span class=n&gt;best&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;::&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;cli&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;::&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;positional&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;              &lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;name&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=s&gt;&amp;#34;FILTERS&amp;#34;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;              &lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;help&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=s&gt;&amp;#34;Include only tests whose names contain FILTER&amp;#34;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;            &lt;span class=p&gt;});&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;};&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:15&gt;C++&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;Using &lt;code&gt;best::mirror::with&lt;/code&gt;, we can apply tags to the individual fields that
describe how they should be parsed and displayed as CLI flags. A more
complicated, full-featured example can be found at
&lt;a href=https://github.com/mcy/best/blob/main/best/cli/toy_flags.h&gt;&lt;code&gt;toy_flags.h&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/a&gt;,
which exercises most of the CLI parser&amp;rsquo;s features.&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;best::parse_flags&amp;lt;MyFlags&gt;(...)&lt;/code&gt; can be used to parse a particular flag struct
from program inputs, independent of the actual &lt;code&gt;argv&lt;/code&gt; of the program. A
&lt;code&gt;best::cli&lt;/code&gt; contains the actual parser metadata, but this is not generally
user-accessible; it is constructed automatically using reflection.&lt;p&gt;Streamlining top-level app execution can be done using &lt;code&gt;best::app&lt;/code&gt;, which fully
replaces the &lt;code&gt;main()&lt;/code&gt; function. Defining an app is very similar to defining a
test:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:16&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-cpp highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;best&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;::&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;app&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;MyApp&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;[](&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;MyFlags&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;amp;&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;flags&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=c1&gt;// Do something cool!
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;};&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:16&gt;C++&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;This will automatically record the program inputs, run the flag parser for
&lt;code&gt;MyFlags&lt;/code&gt; (printing &lt;code&gt;--help&lt;/code&gt; and existing, when requested), and then call the
body of the lambda.&lt;p&gt;The lambda can either return &lt;code&gt;void&lt;/code&gt;, an &lt;code&gt;int&lt;/code&gt; (as an exit code) or even a
&lt;code&gt;best::result&lt;/code&gt;, like Rust. &lt;code&gt;best::app&lt;/code&gt; is also where the &lt;code&gt;argv&lt;/code&gt; of the program
can be requested by other parts of the program.&lt;h2 id=whats-next&gt;&lt;a href=#whats-next&gt;What&amp;rsquo;s Next?&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;p&gt;There&amp;rsquo;s still a lot of stuff I want to add to &lt;code&gt;best&lt;/code&gt;. There&amp;rsquo;s no synchronization
primitives, neither atomics nor locks or channels. There&amp;rsquo;s no I/O; I have a
work-in-progress PR to add &lt;code&gt;best::path&lt;/code&gt; and &lt;code&gt;best::file&lt;/code&gt;. I&amp;rsquo;d like to write my
own math library, &lt;code&gt;best::rc&lt;/code&gt; (reference-counting), and portable SIMD. There&amp;rsquo;s
also some other OS APIs I want to build, such as signals and subprocesses. I
want to add a robust PRNG, time APIs, networking, and stack symbolization.&lt;p&gt;Building the best C++ library is a lot of work, not the least because C++ is a
very tricky language and writing exhaustive tests is tedious. But it manages to
make C++ fun for me again!&lt;p&gt;I would love to see contributions some day. I don&amp;rsquo;t expect anyone to actually
use this, but to me, it proves C++ could be so much better.&lt;div class=footnotes role=doc-endnotes&gt;&lt;hr&gt;&lt;ol&gt;&lt;li id=fn:1&gt;&lt;p&gt;They are also &lt;a href=https://patricia.no/2022/03/08/cppcon.html&gt;terrible people&lt;/a&gt;.&amp;#160;&lt;a href=#fnref:1 class=footnote-backref role=doc-backlink&gt;&amp;#8617;&amp;#xfe0e;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;li id=fn:2&gt;&lt;p&gt;I will grant that JeanHeyd has made significant process where many people
believed was impossible. He appears to have the indomitable willpower of a
shōnen protagonist.&amp;#160;&lt;a href=#fnref:2 class=footnote-backref role=doc-backlink&gt;&amp;#8617;&amp;#xfe0e;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;li id=fn:3&gt;&lt;p&gt;I have heard an apocryphal story that the namespace was going to be &lt;code&gt;abc&lt;/code&gt; or
&lt;code&gt;abcl&lt;/code&gt;, because it was &amp;ldquo;Alphabet&amp;rsquo;s library&amp;rdquo;. This name was ultimately shot
down by the office of the CEO, or so the legend goes.&amp;#160;&lt;a href=#fnref:3 class=footnote-backref role=doc-backlink&gt;&amp;#8617;&amp;#xfe0e;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;li id=fn:4&gt;&lt;p&gt;This may get renamed to &lt;code&gt;best::interval&lt;/code&gt; or even &lt;code&gt;best::range&lt;/code&gt; We&amp;rsquo;ll see!&amp;#160;&lt;a href=#fnref:4 class=footnote-backref role=doc-backlink&gt;&amp;#8617;&amp;#xfe0e;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;li id=fn:5&gt;&lt;p&gt;The fourth time I&amp;rsquo;ve written one in my career, lmao. I also wrote a
&lt;a href=https://github.com/google/cwisstable&gt;C implementation&lt;/a&gt; at one point. My

&lt;a href=&#34;https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ncHmEUmJZf4&#34;&gt;excellent introduction&lt;/a&gt; to the
Swisstable data structure.&amp;#160;&lt;a href=#fnref:5 class=footnote-backref role=doc-backlink&gt;&amp;#8617;&amp;#xfe0e;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/ol&gt;&lt;/div&gt;</content>
