  <entry>
    <title>What&#39;s //go:nosplit for?</title>
    <link href="/2025/07/07/nosplit"/>
    <updated>2025-07-07T00:00:00+00:00</updated>
    <id>/2025/07/07/nosplit</id>
    <content type="html">&lt;p&gt;Most people don&amp;rsquo;t know that Go has special syntax for directives. Unfortunately,
it&amp;rsquo;s not real syntax, it&amp;rsquo;s just a comment. For example, &lt;code&gt;//go:noinline&lt;/code&gt; causes
the next function declaration to never get inlined, which is useful for changing
the inlining cost of functions that call it.&lt;p&gt;There are three types of directives:&lt;ol&gt;&lt;li&gt;&lt;p&gt;The ones documented in
&lt;a href=https://pkg.go.dev/cmd/compile#hdr-Function_Directives&gt;&lt;code&gt;gc&lt;/code&gt;&amp;rsquo;s doc comment&lt;/a&gt;.
This includes &lt;code&gt;//go:noinline&lt;/code&gt; and &lt;code&gt;//line&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;li&gt;&lt;p&gt;The ones documented elsewhere, such as &lt;code&gt;//go:build&lt;/code&gt; and &lt;code&gt;//go:generate&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;li&gt;&lt;p&gt;The ones documented in
&lt;a href=https://cs.opensource.google/go/go/+/refs/tags/go1.24.4:src/runtime/HACKING.md&gt;runtime/HACKING.md&lt;/a&gt;,
which can only be used if the &lt;code&gt;-+&lt;/code&gt; flag is passed to &lt;code&gt;gc&lt;/code&gt;. This includes
&lt;code&gt;//go:nowritebarrier&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;li&gt;&lt;p&gt;The ones not documented at all, whose existence can be discovered by
searching the compiler&amp;rsquo;s tests. These include &lt;code&gt;//go:nocheckptr&lt;/code&gt;,
&lt;code&gt;//go:nointerface&lt;/code&gt;, and &lt;code&gt;//go:debug&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;/ol&gt;&lt;p&gt;We are most interested in a directive of the first type, &lt;code&gt;//go:nosplit&lt;/code&gt;.
According to the documentation:&lt;blockquote id=ref:1 class=ref ref math&gt;&lt;a href=#ref:1&gt;&lt;span class=chip&gt;reference&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;p&gt;The &lt;code&gt;//go:nosplit&lt;/code&gt; directive must be followed by a function declaration. It
specifies that the function must omit its usual stack overflow check. This is
most commonly used by low-level runtime code invoked at times when it is
unsafe for the calling goroutine to be preempted.&lt;/blockquote&gt;&lt;p&gt;What does this even mean? Normal program code can use this annotation, but its
behavior is poorly specified. Let&amp;rsquo;s dig in.&lt;h2 id=go-stack-growth&gt;&lt;a href=#go-stack-growth&gt;Go Stack Growth&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;p&gt;Go allocates very small stacks for new goroutines, which grow their stack
dynamically. This allows a program to spawn a large number of short-lived
goroutines without spending a lot of memory on their stacks.&lt;p&gt;This means that it&amp;rsquo;s very easy to overflow the stack. Every function knows how
large its stack is, and &lt;code&gt;runtime.g&lt;/code&gt;, the goroutine struct, contains the end
position of the stack; if the stack pointer is less than it (the stack grows up)
control passes to &lt;code&gt;runtime.morestack&lt;/code&gt;, which effectively preempts the goroutine
while its stack is resized.&lt;p&gt;In effect, every Go function has the following code around it:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:1&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-x86-go highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=err&gt;TEXT&lt;/span&gt;    &lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=err&gt;f&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=err&gt;SB&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;),&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=err&gt;ABIInternal&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=err&gt;$&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=m&gt;24-16&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=err&gt;CMPQ&lt;/span&gt;    &lt;span class=err&gt;SP&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=m&gt;16&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=err&gt;R&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=m&gt;14&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=err&gt;JLS&lt;/span&gt;     &lt;span class=err&gt;grow&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=err&gt;PUSHQ&lt;/span&gt;   &lt;span class=err&gt;BP&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=err&gt;MOVQ&lt;/span&gt;    &lt;span class=err&gt;SP&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=err&gt;BP&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=err&gt;SUBQ&lt;/span&gt;    &lt;span class=err&gt;$&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=m&gt;16&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=err&gt;SP&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=err&gt;//&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=err&gt;Function&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=err&gt;body&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;...&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=err&gt;ADDQ&lt;/span&gt;    &lt;span class=err&gt;$&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=m&gt;16&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=err&gt;SP&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=err&gt;POPQ&lt;/span&gt;    &lt;span class=err&gt;BP&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=err&gt;RET&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=nl&gt;grow:&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=err&gt;MOVQ&lt;/span&gt;    &lt;span class=err&gt;AX&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=m&gt;8&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=err&gt;SP&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=err&gt;MOVQ&lt;/span&gt;    &lt;span class=err&gt;BX&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=m&gt;16&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=err&gt;SP&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=err&gt;CALL&lt;/span&gt;    &lt;span class=err&gt;runtime&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=err&gt;morestack_noctxt&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=err&gt;SB&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=err&gt;MOVQ&lt;/span&gt;    &lt;span class=m&gt;8&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=err&gt;SP&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;),&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=err&gt;AX&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=err&gt;MOVQ&lt;/span&gt;    &lt;span class=m&gt;16&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=err&gt;SP&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;),&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=err&gt;BX&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=err&gt;JMP&lt;/span&gt;     &lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=err&gt;f&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=err&gt;SB&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:1&gt;x86 Assembly (Go Syntax)&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;Note that &lt;code&gt;r14&lt;/code&gt; holds a pointer to the current &lt;code&gt;runtime.g&lt;/code&gt;, and the stack limit
is the third word-sized field (&lt;code&gt;runtime.g.stackguard0&lt;/code&gt;) in that struct, hence
the offset of 16. If the stack is about to be exhausted, it jumps to a special
block at the end of the function that spills all of the argument registers,
traps into the runtime, and, once that&amp;rsquo;s done, unspills the arguments and
re-starts the function.&lt;p&gt;Note that arguments are spilled &lt;em&gt;before&lt;/em&gt; adjusting &lt;code&gt;rsp&lt;/code&gt;, which means that the
arguments are written to the &lt;em&gt;caller&amp;rsquo;s&lt;/em&gt; stack frame. This is part of Go&amp;rsquo;s ABI;
callers must allocate space at the top of their stack frames for any function
that they call to spill all of its registers for preemption&lt;sup id=fnref:1&gt;&lt;a href=#fn:1 class=footnote-ref role=doc-noteref&gt;1&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/sup&gt;.&lt;p&gt;Preemption is not reentrant, which means that functions that are running in the
context of a preempted G or with no G at all must not be preempted by this
check.&lt;h2 id=nosplit-functions&gt;&lt;a href=#nosplit-functions&gt;Nosplit Functions&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;p&gt;The &lt;code&gt;//go:nosplit&lt;/code&gt; directive marks a function as &amp;ldquo;nosplit&amp;rdquo;, or a &amp;ldquo;non-splitting
function&amp;rdquo;. &amp;ldquo;Splitting&amp;rdquo; has nothing to do with what this directive does.&lt;blockquote id=aside:1 class=aside aside&gt;&lt;a href=#aside:1&gt;&lt;span class=chip&gt;aside&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;p&gt;In the bad old days, Go&amp;rsquo;s stacks were &lt;em&gt;split&lt;/em&gt; up into &lt;em&gt;segments&lt;/em&gt;, where each
segment ended with a pointer to the next, effectively replacing the stack&amp;rsquo;s
single array with a linked list of such arrays.&lt;p&gt;Segmented stacks were terrible. Instead of triggering a resize, these
prologues were responsible for updating &lt;code&gt;rsp&lt;/code&gt; to the next (or previous) block
by following this pointer, whenever the current segment bottomed out. This
meant that if a function call happened to be on a segment boundary, it would
be &lt;em&gt;extremely slow&lt;/em&gt; in comparison to other function calls, due to the
significant work required to update &lt;code&gt;rsp&lt;/code&gt; correctly.&lt;p&gt;This meant that unlucky sizing of stack frames meant sudden performance
cliffs. Fun!&lt;p&gt;Go has since figured out that segmented stacks are a terrible idea. In the
process of implementing a correct GC stack scanning algorithm (which it did
not have for many stable releases), it also gained the ability to copy the
contents of a stack from one location to another, updating pointers in such a
way that user code wouldn&amp;rsquo;t notice.&lt;p&gt;This stack splitting code is where the name &amp;ldquo;nosplit&amp;rdquo; comes from.&lt;/blockquote&gt;&lt;p&gt;A nosplit function does not load and branch on &lt;code&gt;runtime.g.stackguard0&lt;/code&gt;, and
simply assumes it has enough stack. This means that nosplit functions will not
preempt themselves, and, as a result, are noticeably faster to call in a hot
loop. Don&amp;rsquo;t believe me?&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:2&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-go highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;//go:noinline
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=kd&gt;func&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nf&gt;noinline&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nx&gt;x&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=kt&gt;int&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;{}&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;//go:nosplit
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=kd&gt;func&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nf&gt;nosplit&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nx&gt;x&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=kt&gt;int&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nf&gt;noinline&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nx&gt;x&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=kd&gt;func&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nf&gt;yessplit&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nx&gt;x&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=kt&gt;int&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nf&gt;noinline&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nx&gt;x&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=kd&gt;func&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nf&gt;BenchmarkCall&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nx&gt;b&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;*&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nx&gt;testing&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nx&gt;B&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=nx&gt;b&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nf&gt;Run&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=s&gt;&amp;#34;nosplit&amp;#34;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=kd&gt;func&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nx&gt;b&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;*&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nx&gt;testing&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nx&gt;B&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;    &lt;span class=k&gt;for&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nx&gt;b&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nf&gt;Loop&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;()&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nf&gt;nosplit&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mi&gt;42&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;

&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;    &lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;          &lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;   &lt;span class=m&gt;51&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nl&gt;fdc5:&lt;/span&gt;     &lt;span class=err&gt;MOVQ&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=m&gt;0x8&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=err&gt;SP&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;),&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=err&gt;AX&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;    &lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;          &lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;   &lt;span class=m&gt;51&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nl&gt;fdca:&lt;/span&gt;     &lt;span class=err&gt;JMP&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=err&gt;yessplit&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=err&gt;SB&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:3&gt;x86 Assembly (Go Syntax)&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;The time spent at each instruction (for the whole benchmark, where I made sure
equal time was spent on each test case with &lt;code&gt;-benchtime Nx&lt;/code&gt;) is comparable for
all of the instructions these functions share, but an additional ~2% cost is
incurred for the stack check.&lt;p&gt;This is a very artificial setup, because the &lt;code&gt;g&lt;/code&gt; struct is always in L1 in the
&lt;code&gt;yessplit&lt;/code&gt; benchmark due to the fact that no other memory operations occur in
the loop. However, for very hot code that needs to saturate the cache, this can
have an outsized effect due to cache misses. We can enhance this benchmark by
adding an assembly function that executes &lt;code&gt;clflush [r14]&lt;/code&gt;, which causes the &lt;code&gt;g&lt;/code&gt;
struct to be ejected from all caches.&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:4&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-x86-go highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=err&gt;TEXT&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=err&gt;clflush&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=err&gt;SB&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=err&gt;CLFLUSH&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=err&gt;R&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=m&gt;14&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt;  &lt;span class=err&gt;//&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=err&gt;Eject&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=err&gt;the&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=err&gt;pointee&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=err&gt;of&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=err&gt;r&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=m&gt;14&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=k&gt;from&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=err&gt;all&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=err&gt;caches&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=err&gt;RET&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:4&gt;x86 Assembly (Go Syntax)&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;If we add a call to this function to both benchmark loops, we see the staggering
cost of a cold fetch from RAM show up in every function call: 120.1 nanosecods
for &lt;code&gt;BenchmarkCall/nosplit&lt;/code&gt;, versus 332.1 nanoseconds for
&lt;code&gt;BenchmarkCall/yessplit&lt;/code&gt;. The 200 nanosecond difference is a fetch from main
memory. An L1 miss is about 15 times less expensive, so if the &lt;code&gt;g&lt;/code&gt; struct
manages to get kicked out of L1, you&amp;rsquo;re paying about 15 or so nanoseconds, or
about two map lookups!&lt;p&gt;Despite the language resisting adding an inlining heuristic, which programmers
would place everywhere without knowing what it does, they &lt;em&gt;did&lt;/em&gt; provide
something worse that makes code noticeably faster: nosplit.&lt;h2 id=but-its-harmless&gt;&lt;a href=#but-its-harmless&gt;But It&amp;rsquo;s Harmless&amp;mldr;?&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;p&gt;Consider the following program&lt;sup id=fnref:2&gt;&lt;a href=#fn:2 class=footnote-ref role=doc-noteref&gt;2&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/sup&gt;:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:5&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-go highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;//go:nosplit
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=kd&gt;func&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nf&gt;x&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nx&gt;y&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=kt&gt;int&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nf&gt;x&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nx&gt;y&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mi&gt;1&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:5&gt;Go&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;Naturally, this will instantly overflow the stack. Instead, we get a really
scary linker error:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:6&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-console highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=go&gt;x.x: nosplit stack over 792 byte limit
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=go&gt;x.x&amp;lt;1&amp;gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=go&gt;    grows 24 bytes, calls x.x&amp;lt;1&amp;gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=go&gt;    infinite cycle
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:6&gt;Console&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;The Go linker contains a check to verify that any chain of nosplit functions
which call nosplit functions do not overflow a small window of extra stack,
which is where the stack frames of nosplit functions live if they go past
&lt;code&gt;stackguard0&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;p&gt;Every stack frame contributes some stack use (for the return address, at
minimum), so the number of functions you can call before you get this error is
limited. And because every function needs to allocate space for all of its
callees to spill their arguments if necessary, you can hit this limit every fast
if every one of these functions uses every available argument register (ask me
how I know).&lt;p&gt;Also, turning on fuzzing instruments the code by inserting nosplit calls into
the fuzzer runtime around branches, meaning that turning on fuzzing can
&lt;em&gt;previously fine code to no longer link&lt;/em&gt;. Stack usage also varies slightly by
architecture, meaning that code which builds in one architecture fails to link
in others (most visible when going from 32-bit to 64-bit).&lt;p&gt;There is no easy way to control directives using build tags (two poorly-designed
features collide), so you cannot just &amp;ldquo;turn off&amp;rdquo; performance-sensitive nosplits
for debugging, either.&lt;p&gt;For this reason, you must be &lt;em&gt;very very careful&lt;/em&gt; about using nosplit for
performance.&lt;h3 id=virtual-nosplit-functions&gt;&lt;a href=#virtual-nosplit-functions&gt;Virtual Nosplit Functions&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;Excitingly, nosplit functions whose addresses are taken do not have special
codegen, allowing us to defeat the linker stack check by using virtual function
calls.&lt;p&gt;Consider the following program:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:7&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-go highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=kn&gt;package&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nx&gt;main&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=kd&gt;var&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nx&gt;f&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=kd&gt;func&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=kt&gt;int&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;//go:nosplit
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=kd&gt;func&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nf&gt;x&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nx&gt;y&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=kt&gt;int&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nf&gt;f&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nx&gt;y&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mi&gt;1&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=kd&gt;func&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nf&gt;main&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;()&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=nx&gt;f&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nx&gt;x&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=nf&gt;f&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mi&gt;0&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:7&gt;Go&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;This will quickly exhaust the main G&amp;rsquo;s tiny stack and segfault in the most
violent way imaginable, preventing the runtime from printing a debug trace. All
this program outputs is &lt;code&gt;signal: segmentation fault&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;p&gt;This is &lt;a href=https://github.com/golang/go/issues/74478&gt;probably a bug&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;h2 id=other-side-effects&gt;&lt;a href=#other-side-effects&gt;Other Side Effects&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;p&gt;It turns out that nosplit has various other fun side-effects that are not
documented anywhere. The main thing it does is it contributes to whether a
function is considered &amp;ldquo;unsafe&amp;rdquo; by the runtime.&lt;p&gt;Consider the following program:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:8&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-go highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=kn&gt;package&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nx&gt;main&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=kn&gt;import&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=s&gt;&amp;#34;fmt&amp;#34;&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=s&gt;&amp;#34;os&amp;#34;&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=s&gt;&amp;#34;runtime&amp;#34;&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=s&gt;&amp;#34;time&amp;#34;&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=kd&gt;func&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nf&gt;main&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;()&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=k&gt;for&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=k&gt;range&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nx&gt;runtime&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nf&gt;GOMAXPROCS&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mi&gt;0&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;    &lt;span class=k&gt;go&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=kd&gt;func&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;()&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;      &lt;span class=k&gt;for&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;{}&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;    &lt;span class=p&gt;}()&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=nx&gt;time&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nf&gt;Sleep&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nx&gt;time&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nx&gt;Second&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=c1&gt;// Wait for all the other Gs to start.
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=nx&gt;fmt&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nf&gt;Println&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=s&gt;&amp;#34;Hello, world!&amp;#34;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=nx&gt;os&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nf&gt;Exit&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mi&gt;0&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:8&gt;Go&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;This program will make sure that every P becomes bound to a G that loops
forever, meaning they will never trap into the runtime. Thus, this program will
hang forever, never printing its result and exiting. But that&amp;rsquo;s not what
happens.&lt;p&gt;Thanks to asynchronous preemption, the scheduler will detect Gs that have been
running for too long, and preempt its M by sending a signal to it
(&lt;a href=&#34;https://cs.opensource.google/go/go/+/master:src/runtime/signal_unix.go;l=43&#34;&gt;due to happenstance&lt;/a&gt;,
this is &lt;code&gt;SIGURG&lt;/code&gt; of all things.)&lt;p&gt;However, asynchronous preemption is only possible when the M stops due to the
signal at a safe point, as determined by &lt;code&gt;runtime.isAsyncSafePoint&lt;/code&gt;. It includes
the following block of code:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:9&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-go highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;	&lt;span class=nx&gt;up&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nx&gt;startpc&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;:=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nf&gt;pcdatavalue2&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nx&gt;f&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nx&gt;abi&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nx&gt;PCDATA_UnsafePoint&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nx&gt;pc&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;	&lt;span class=k&gt;if&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nx&gt;up&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;==&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nx&gt;abi&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nx&gt;UnsafePointUnsafe&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;		&lt;span class=c1&gt;// Unsafe-point marked by compiler. This includes
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;		&lt;span class=c1&gt;// atomic sequences (e.g., write barrier) and nosplit
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;		&lt;span class=c1&gt;// functions (except at calls).
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;		&lt;span class=k&gt;return&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=kc&gt;false&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=mi&gt;0&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;	&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:9&gt;Go&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;If we chase down where this value is set, we&amp;rsquo;ll find that it is set explicitly
for write barrier sequences, for any function that is &amp;ldquo;part of the runtime&amp;rdquo; (as
defined by being built with the &lt;code&gt;-+&lt;/code&gt; flag) and &lt;em&gt;for any nosplit function&lt;/em&gt;.&lt;p&gt;With a small modification of hoisting the &lt;code&gt;go&lt;/code&gt; body into a nosplit function, the
following program will run forever: it will never wake up from &lt;code&gt;time.Sleep&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:10&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-go highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=kn&gt;package&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nx&gt;main&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=kn&gt;import&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=s&gt;&amp;#34;fmt&amp;#34;&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=s&gt;&amp;#34;os&amp;#34;&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=s&gt;&amp;#34;runtime&amp;#34;&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=s&gt;&amp;#34;time&amp;#34;&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;//go:nosplit
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=kd&gt;func&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nf&gt;forever&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;()&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=k&gt;for&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;{}&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=kd&gt;func&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nf&gt;main&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;()&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=k&gt;for&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=k&gt;range&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nx&gt;runtime&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nf&gt;GOMAXPROCS&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mi&gt;0&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;    &lt;span class=k&gt;go&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nf&gt;forever&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;()&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=nx&gt;time&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nf&gt;Sleep&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nx&gt;time&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nx&gt;Second&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=c1&gt;// Wait for all the other Gs to start.
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=nx&gt;fmt&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nf&gt;Println&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=s&gt;&amp;#34;Hello, world!&amp;#34;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=nx&gt;os&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nf&gt;Exit&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mi&gt;0&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:10&gt;Go&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;Even though there is work to do, every P is bound to a G that will never reach a
safe point, so there will never be a P available to run the main goroutine.&lt;p&gt;This represents another potential danger of using nosplit functions: those that
do not call preemptable functions must terminate promptly, or risk livelocking
the whole runtime.&lt;h2 id=conclusion&gt;&lt;a href=#conclusion&gt;Conclusion&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;p&gt;I use nosplit &lt;em&gt;a lot&lt;/em&gt;, because I write high-performance, low-latency Go. This is
a very insane thing to do, which has caused me to slowly generate bug reports
whenever I hit strange corner cases.&lt;p&gt;For example, there are many cases where spill regions are allocated for
functions that never use them, for example, functions which only call nosplit
functions allocate space for them to spill their arguments, which they don&amp;rsquo;t
do.&lt;sup id=fnref:3&gt;&lt;a href=#fn:3 class=footnote-ref role=doc-noteref&gt;3&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/sup&gt;&lt;p&gt;This is a documented Go language feature which:&lt;ol&gt;&lt;li&gt;Isn&amp;rsquo;t very well-documented (the async preemption behavior certainly isn&amp;rsquo;t)!&lt;li&gt;Has very scary optimization-dependent build failures.&lt;li&gt;Can cause livelock and mysterious segfaults.&lt;li&gt;Can be used in user programs that don&amp;rsquo;t &lt;code&gt;import &#34;unsafe&#34;&lt;/code&gt;!&lt;li&gt;And it makes code faster!&lt;/ol&gt;&lt;p&gt;I&amp;rsquo;m surprised such a massive footgun exists at all, buuuut it&amp;rsquo;s a measureable
benchmark improvement for me, so it&amp;rsquo;s impossible to tell if it&amp;rsquo;s bad or not.&lt;div class=footnotes role=doc-endnotes&gt;&lt;hr&gt;&lt;ol&gt;&lt;li id=fn:1&gt;&lt;p&gt;The astute reader will observe that because preemption is not reentrant,
only one of these spill regions will be in use at at time in a G. This is a
known bug in the ABI, and is essentially a bodge to enable easy adoption of
passing arguments by register, without needing all of the parts of the
runtime that expect arguments to be spilled to the stack, as was the case in
the slow old days when Go&amp;rsquo;s ABI on every platform was &amp;ldquo;&lt;code&gt;i386-unknown-linux&lt;/code&gt;
but worse&amp;rdquo;, i.e., arguments went on the stack and made the CPU&amp;rsquo;s store queue
sad.&lt;p&gt;I recently filed
&lt;a href=https://github.com/golang/go/issues/74413&gt;a bug about this&lt;/a&gt; that boils
down to &amp;ldquo;add a field to &lt;code&gt;runtime.g&lt;/code&gt; to use a spill space&amp;rdquo;, which seems to me
to be simpler than the alternatives described in the &lt;code&gt;ABIInternal&lt;/code&gt; spec.&amp;#160;&lt;a href=#fnref:1 class=footnote-backref role=doc-backlink&gt;&amp;#8617;&amp;#xfe0e;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;li id=fn:2&gt;&lt;p&gt;Basically every bug report I write starts with these four words and it means
you&amp;rsquo;re about to see the worst program ever written.&amp;#160;&lt;a href=#fnref:2 class=footnote-backref role=doc-backlink&gt;&amp;#8617;&amp;#xfe0e;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;li id=fn:3&gt;&lt;p&gt;The spill area is also used for spilling arguments across calls, but in this
case, it is not necessary for the caller to allocate it for a nosplit
function.&amp;#160;&lt;a href=#fnref:3 class=footnote-backref role=doc-backlink&gt;&amp;#8617;&amp;#xfe0e;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/ol&gt;&lt;/div&gt;</content>
  </entry>

    <title>Protobuf Tip #7: Scoping It Out</title>
    <link href="/2025/06/03/protobuf-tip-7"/>
    <updated>2025-06-03T00:00:00+00:00</updated>
    <id>/2025/06/03/protobuf-tip-7</id>
    <content type="html">&lt;p&gt;&lt;em&gt;You&amp;rsquo;d need a very specialized electron microscope to get down to the level to
actually see a single strand of DNA. &amp;ndash; Craig Venter&lt;/em&gt;&lt;p&gt;TL;DR: &lt;code&gt;buf convert&lt;/code&gt; is a powerful tool for examining wire format dumps, by
converting them to JSON and using existing JSON analysis tooling. &lt;code&gt;protoscope&lt;/code&gt;
can be used for lower-level analysis, such debugging messages that have been
corrupted.&lt;blockquote id=note:1 class=note note&gt;&lt;a href=#note:1&gt;&lt;span class=chip&gt;note&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;p&gt;I&amp;rsquo;m editing a series of best practice pieces on Protobuf, a language that I
work on which has lots of evil corner-cases.These are shorter than what I
typically post here, but I think it fits with what you, dear reader, come to
this blog for. These tips are also posted on the
&lt;a href=https://buf.build/blog/totw-7-scoping-it-out&gt;buf.build blog&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/blockquote&gt;&lt;h2 id=json-from-protobuf&gt;&lt;a href=#json-from-protobuf&gt;JSON from Protobuf?&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;p&gt;JSON’s human-readable syntax is a big reason why it’s so popular, possibly
second only to built-in support in browsers and many languages. It’s easy to
examine any JSON document using tools like online prettifiers and the inimitable
&lt;code&gt;jq&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;p&gt;But Protobuf is a binary format! This means that you can’t easily use &lt;code&gt;jq&lt;/code&gt; -like
tools with it…or can you?&lt;h2 id=transcoding-with-buf-convert&gt;&lt;a href=#transcoding-with-buf-convert&gt;Transcoding with &lt;code&gt;buf convert&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;p&gt;The Buf CLI offers a utility for transcoding messages between the three Protobuf
encoding formats: the wire format, JSON, and textproto; it also supports YAML.
This is &lt;code&gt;buf convert&lt;/code&gt;, and it’s very powerful.&lt;p&gt;To perform a conversion, we need four inputs:&lt;ol&gt;&lt;li&gt;A Protobuf source to get types out of. This can be a local &lt;code&gt;.proto&lt;/code&gt; file, an
encoded &lt;code&gt;FileDescriptorSet&lt;/code&gt; , or a remote BSR module.&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;If not provided, but run in a directory that is within a local Buf module,
that module will be used as the Protobuf type source.&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;The name of the top-level type for the message we want to transcode, via the
&lt;code&gt;--type&lt;/code&gt; flag.&lt;li&gt;The input message, via the &lt;code&gt;--from&lt;/code&gt; flag.&lt;li&gt;A location to output to, via the &lt;code&gt;--to&lt;/code&gt; flag.&lt;/ol&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;buf convert&lt;/code&gt; supports input and output redirection, making it usable as part of
a shell pipeline. For example, consider the following Protobuf code in our local
Buf module:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:1&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-protobuf highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;// my_api.proto
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;syntax&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=s&gt;&amp;#34;proto3&amp;#34;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=err&gt;

That’s wrong. The answer should be &lt;code&gt;9&lt;/code&gt;. This illustrates one pitfall to
keep in mind when using &lt;code&gt;jq&lt;/code&gt; with Protobuf. Protobuf will &lt;em&gt;sometimes&lt;/em&gt; serialize
numbers as quoted strings (the C++ reference implementation only does this when
they’re integers outside of the IEEE754 representable range, but Go is somewhat
lazier, and does it for all 64-bit values).&lt;blockquote&gt;&lt;p&gt;You can test if an &lt;code&gt;x int64&lt;/code&gt; is in the representable float range with this
very simple check: &lt;code&gt;int64(float64(x)) == x)&lt;/code&gt;. See
&lt;a href=https://go.dev/play/p/T81SbbFg3br&gt;https://go.dev/play/p/T81SbbFg3br&lt;/a&gt;. The
&lt;a href=https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/blob/main/src/google/protobuf/json/internal/unparser.cc#L96&gt;equivalent version in C++&lt;/a&gt;
is much more complicated.&lt;/blockquote&gt;&lt;p&gt;This means we need to use the &lt;code&gt;tonumber&lt;/code&gt; conversion function:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:7&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-console highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=gp&gt;$&lt;/span&gt; buf-jq my.api.v1.Cart dump.pb &lt;span class=s1&gt;&amp;#39;[.orders[].count | tonumber] | add&amp;#39;&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=go&gt;9
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:7&gt;Console&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;jq&lt;/code&gt; ’s whole deal is JSON, so it brings with it all of JSON’s pitfalls. This is
notable for Protobuf when trying to do arithmetic on 64-bit values. As we saw
above, Protobuf serializes integers outside of the 64-bit float representable
range (and in some runtimes, some integers inside it).&lt;p&gt;For example, if you have a &lt;code&gt;repeated int64&lt;/code&gt; that you want to sum over, it may
produce incorrect answers due to floating-point rounding. For notes on
conversions in &lt;code&gt;jq&lt;/code&gt;, see
&lt;a href=https://jqlang.org/manual/#identity&gt;https://jqlang.org/manual/#identity&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;h2 id=disassembling-with-protoscope&gt;&lt;a href=#disassembling-with-protoscope&gt;Disassembling with &lt;code&gt;protoscope&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href=https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protoscope&gt;&lt;code&gt;protoscope&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/a&gt; is a tool provided
by the Protobuf team (which I originally wrote!) for decoding arbitrary data as
if it were encoded in the Protobuf wire format. This process is called
&lt;em&gt;disassembly&lt;/em&gt;. It’s designed to work without a schema available, although it
doesn’t produce especially clean output.&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:8&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-console highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=gp&gt;$&lt;/span&gt; go install github.com/protocolbuffers/protoscope/cmd/protoscope...@latest

&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=go&gt;  3: 1
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=go&gt;}

&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=go&gt;    13:SGROUP
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=go&gt;  }

&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=go&gt;}
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=go&gt;2: {
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=go&gt;  1: 2300094522i64
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=go&gt;  2: {&amp;#34;isopropyl alcohol 70%, 1 gallon&amp;#34;}
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=go&gt;  3: 2
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=go&gt;}
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:8&gt;Console&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;The field names are gone; only field numbers are shown. This example also
reveals an especially glaring limitation of &lt;code&gt;protoscope&lt;/code&gt;, which is that it can’t
tell the difference between string and message fields, so it guesses according
to some heuristics. For the first and third elements it was able to grok them as
strings, but for &lt;code&gt;orders[1].sku_name&lt;/code&gt;, it incorrectly guessed it was a message
and produced garbage.&lt;p&gt;The tradeoff is that not only does &lt;code&gt;protoscope&lt;/code&gt; not need a schema, it also
tolerates almost any error, making it possible to analyze messages that have
been partly corrupted. If we flip a random bit somewhere in &lt;code&gt;orders[0]&lt;/code&gt;,
disassembling the message still succeeds:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:9&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-console highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=gp&gt;$&lt;/span&gt; protoscope dump.pb
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=go&gt;1: 9001
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=go&gt;2: {`0f7ac8e80400000000120e76616375756d20636c65616e65721801`}
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=go&gt;2: {
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=go&gt;  1: 431294823i64
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=go&gt;  2: {
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=go&gt;    13: 101
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=go&gt;    14: 97
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=go&gt;    4: 102
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=go&gt;    13: 1.3518748403899336e-153   # 0x2032202c7265746ci64
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=go&gt;    14: 97
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=go&gt;    12:SGROUP
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=go&gt;    13:SGROUP
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=go&gt;  }
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=go&gt;  3: 6
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=go&gt;}
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=go&gt;2: {
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=go&gt;  1: 2300094522i64
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=go&gt;  2: {&amp;#34;isopropyl alcohol 70%, 1 gallon&amp;#34;}
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=go&gt;  3: 2
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=go&gt;}
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:9&gt;Console&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;Although &lt;code&gt;protoscope&lt;/code&gt; did give up on disassembling the corrupted submessage, it
still made it through the rest of the dump.&lt;p&gt;Like &lt;code&gt;buf convert&lt;/code&gt;, we can give &lt;code&gt;protoscope&lt;/code&gt; a &lt;code&gt;FileDescriptorSet&lt;/code&gt; to make its
heuristic a little smarter.&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:10&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-console highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=gp&gt;$&lt;/span&gt; protoscope &lt;span class=se&gt;\
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=se&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=go&gt;  --descriptor-set &amp;lt;(buf build -o -) \
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=go&gt;  --message-type my.api.v1.Cart \
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=go&gt;  --print-field-names \
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=go&gt;  dump.pb
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=go&gt;1: 9001                   # user_id
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=go&gt;2: {                      # orders
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=go&gt;  1: 82364538i64          # sku
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=go&gt;  2: {&amp;#34;vacuum cleaner&amp;#34;}   # sku_name
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=go&gt;  3: 1                    # count
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=go&gt;}
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=go&gt;2: {                          # orders
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=go&gt;  1: 431294823i64             # sku
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=go&gt;  2: {&amp;#34;hepa filter, 2 pack&amp;#34;}  # sku_name
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=go&gt;  3: 6                        # count
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=go&gt;}
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=go&gt;2: {                                      # orders
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=go&gt;  1: 2300094522i64                        # sku
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=go&gt;  2: {&amp;#34;isopropyl alcohol 70%, 1 gallon&amp;#34;}  # sku_name
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=go&gt;  3: 2                                    # count
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=go&gt;}
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:10&gt;Console&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;Not only is the second order decoded correctly now, but &lt;code&gt;protoscope&lt;/code&gt; shows the
name of each field (via &lt;code&gt;--print-field-names&lt;/code&gt; ). In this mode, &lt;code&gt;protoscope&lt;/code&gt;
still decodes partially-valid messages.&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;protoscope&lt;/code&gt; also provides a number of other flags for customizing its heuristic
in the absence of a &lt;code&gt;FileDescriporSet&lt;/code&gt;. This enables it to be used as a forensic
tool for debugging messy data corruption bugs.</content>
