&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;    &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=kd&gt;let&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;hi&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;ptr&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;add&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;len&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;-&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mi&gt;1&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;).&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;read&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;()&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;as&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=kt&gt;u32&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;    &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=kd&gt;let&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;data&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;lo&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;|&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;mid&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;lt;&amp;lt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;((&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;len&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;/&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mi&gt;2&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;*&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mi&gt;8&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;))&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;|&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;hi&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;lt;&amp;lt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;((&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;len&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;-&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mi&gt;1&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;*&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mi&gt;8&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;);&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;    &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=kd&gt;let&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;z&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=kt&gt;u32&lt;/span&gt;::&lt;span class=n&gt;from_ne_bytes&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;([&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=sc&gt;b&amp;#39;A&amp;#39;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mi&gt;4&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;])&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;lt;&amp;lt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;len&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;*&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mi&gt;8&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;);&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;    &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;write_at&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;cast&lt;/span&gt;::&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;lt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=kt&gt;u32&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;().&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;write_unaligned&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;data&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;|&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;z&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;);&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:24&gt;Rust&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;I learned this type of loading code while contributing to Abseil: it&amp;rsquo;s very
useful for loading variable-length data for data-hungry algorithms, like a codec
or a hash function.&lt;p&gt;Here&amp;rsquo;s the same benchmark again, but with our new loading code.&lt;figure&gt;&lt;img src=/assets/images/simd-b64/graph.png alt=&#34;a performance graph; our code is even better and the variance is very tight&#34;&gt;&lt;/figure&gt;&lt;p&gt;The results are really, really good. The variance is super tight, and our
performance is 2x that of the baseline pretty much everywhere. &lt;em&gt;Success.&lt;/em&gt;&lt;h3 id=encoding-web-safe&gt;&lt;a href=#encoding-web-safe&gt;Encoding? Web-Safe?&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;Writing an encoding function is simple enough: first, implement an
&lt;code&gt;encode_hot()&lt;/code&gt; function that reverses the operations from &lt;code&gt;decode_hot()&lt;/code&gt;. The
perfect hash from before won&amp;rsquo;t work, so you&amp;rsquo;ll need to
&lt;a href=https://github.com/mcy/vb64/blob/main/src/simd.rs#L170&gt;invent a new one&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;p&gt;Also, the loading/storing code around the encoder is slightly different, too.
&lt;code&gt;vb64&lt;/code&gt; implements a very efficient encoding routine too, so I suggest taking a
look at the source code if you&amp;rsquo;re interested.&lt;p&gt;There is a base64 variant called web-safe base64, that replaces the &lt;code&gt;+&lt;/code&gt; and &lt;code&gt;/&lt;/code&gt;
characters with &lt;code&gt;-&lt;/code&gt; and &lt;code&gt;_&lt;/code&gt;. Building a perfect hash for these is trickier: you
would probably have to do something like
&lt;code&gt;(byte &gt;&gt; 4) - (byte == &#39;_&#39; ? &#39;_&#39; : 0)&lt;/code&gt;. I don&amp;rsquo;t support web-safe base64 yet,
but only because I haven&amp;rsquo;t gotten around to it.&lt;h2 id=conclusion&gt;&lt;a href=#conclusion&gt;Conclusion&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;p&gt;My library doesn&amp;rsquo;t really solve an important problem; base64 decoding isn&amp;rsquo;t a
bottleneck&amp;mldr; anywhere that I know of, really. But writing SIMD code is really
fun! Writing branchless code is often overkill but can give you a good
appreciation for what your compilers can and &lt;em&gt;can&amp;rsquo;t&lt;/em&gt; do for you.&lt;p&gt;This project was also an excuse to try &lt;code&gt;std::simd&lt;/code&gt;. I think it&amp;rsquo;s great overall,
and generates excellent code. There&amp;rsquo;s some rough edges I&amp;rsquo;d like to see fixed to
make SIMD code even simpler, but overall I&amp;rsquo;m very happy with the work that&amp;rsquo;s
been done there.&lt;p&gt;This is probably one of the most complicated posts I&amp;rsquo;ve written in a long time.
SIMD (and performance in general) is a complex topic that requires a breadth of
knowledge of tricks and hardware, a lot of which isn&amp;rsquo;t written down. More of it
is written down now, though.&lt;div class=footnotes role=doc-endnotes&gt;&lt;hr&gt;&lt;ol&gt;&lt;li id=fn:1&gt;&lt;p&gt;Shifts are better understood as arithmetic. They have a lane width, and
closely approximate multiplication and division. AVX2 doesn&amp;rsquo;t even have
vector shift &lt;em&gt;or&lt;/em&gt; vector division: you emulate it with multiplication.&amp;#160;&lt;a href=#fnref:1 class=footnote-backref role=doc-backlink&gt;&amp;#8617;&amp;#xfe0e;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;li id=fn:2&gt;&lt;p&gt;The two common representations of &lt;code&gt;true&lt;/code&gt; and &lt;code&gt;false&lt;/code&gt;, i.e. &lt;code&gt;1&lt;/code&gt; and &lt;code&gt;0&lt;/code&gt; or
&lt;code&gt;0xff...&lt;/code&gt; and &lt;code&gt;0&lt;/code&gt;, are related by the two&amp;rsquo;s complement operation.&lt;p&gt;For example, if I write &lt;code&gt;uint32_t m = -(a == b);&lt;/code&gt;, &lt;code&gt;m&lt;/code&gt; will be zero if
&lt;code&gt;a == b&lt;/code&gt; is false, and all-ones otherwise. This because applying any
arithmetic operation to a &lt;code&gt;bool&lt;/code&gt; promotes it to &lt;code&gt;int&lt;/code&gt;, so &lt;code&gt;false&lt;/code&gt; maps to
&lt;code&gt;0&lt;/code&gt; and &lt;code&gt;true&lt;/code&gt; maps to &lt;code&gt;1&lt;/code&gt;. Applying the &lt;code&gt;-&lt;/code&gt; sends &lt;code&gt;0&lt;/code&gt; to &lt;code&gt;0&lt;/code&gt; and &lt;code&gt;1&lt;/code&gt; to
&lt;code&gt;-1&lt;/code&gt;, and it&amp;rsquo;s useful to know that in two&amp;rsquo;s complement, &lt;code&gt;-1&lt;/code&gt; is represented
as all-ones.&lt;p&gt;The all-ones representation for &lt;code&gt;true&lt;/code&gt; is useful, because it can be used
to implement branchless select very easily. For example,&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:25&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-c++ highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=kt&gt;int&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nf&gt;select_if_eq&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=kt&gt;int&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;a&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=kt&gt;int&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;b&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=kt&gt;int&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;x&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=kt&gt;int&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;y&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=kt&gt;int&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;mask&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;-&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;a&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;==&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;b&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;);&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=k&gt;return&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;mask&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;amp;&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;x&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;|&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;~&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;mask&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;amp;&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;y&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;);&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:25&gt;C++&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;This function returns &lt;code&gt;x&lt;/code&gt; if &lt;code&gt;a == b&lt;/code&gt;, and &lt;code&gt;y&lt;/code&gt; otherwise. Can you tell why?&amp;#160;&lt;a href=#fnref:2 class=footnote-backref role=doc-backlink&gt;&amp;#8617;&amp;#xfe0e;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;li id=fn:3&gt;&lt;p&gt;Target features also affect ABI in subtle ways that I could write many, many
more words on. Compiling libraries you plan to distribute with weird target
feature flags is a recipe for disaster.&amp;#160;&lt;a href=#fnref:3 class=footnote-backref role=doc-backlink&gt;&amp;#8617;&amp;#xfe0e;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;li id=fn:4&gt;&lt;p&gt;Why can&amp;rsquo;t we leave this kind of thing to LLVM? Finding this particular
branchless implementation is tricky. LLVM is smart enough to fold the match
into a switch table, but that&amp;rsquo;s unnecessary memory traffic to look at the
table. (In this domain, unnecessary memory traffic makes our code slower.)&lt;p&gt;Incidentally, with the code I wrote for the original &lt;code&gt;decoded_len()&lt;/code&gt;, LLVM
produces a jump &lt;em&gt;and&lt;/em&gt; a lookup table, which is definitely an odd choice? I
went down something of a rabbit-hole.
https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/118306&lt;p&gt;As for getting LLVM to find the &amp;ldquo;branchless&amp;rdquo; version of the lookup table?
The search space is quite large, and this kind of &amp;ldquo;general strength
reduction&amp;rdquo; problem is fairly open (keywords: &amp;ldquo;superoptimizers&amp;rdquo;).&amp;#160;&lt;a href=#fnref:4 class=footnote-backref role=doc-backlink&gt;&amp;#8617;&amp;#xfe0e;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;li id=fn:5&gt;&lt;p&gt;To be clear on why this works: suppose that in our reference implementation,
we only handle inputs that are a multiple-of-4 length, and are padded with
&lt;code&gt;=&lt;/code&gt; as necessary, and we treat &lt;code&gt;=&lt;/code&gt; as zero in the &lt;code&gt;match&lt;/code&gt;. Then, for the
purposes of computing the &lt;code&gt;bytes&lt;/code&gt; value (before appending it to &lt;code&gt;out&lt;/code&gt;), we
can assume the chunk length is always 4.&amp;#160;&lt;a href=#fnref:5 class=footnote-backref role=doc-backlink&gt;&amp;#8617;&amp;#xfe0e;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;li id=fn:6&gt;&lt;p&gt;See
&lt;a href=https://github.com/mcy/vb64/blob/ed75566393a25d174a2766c3f8947d9c6a506315/src/util.rs&gt;&lt;code&gt;vb64/src/util.rs&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/a&gt;.&amp;#160;&lt;a href=#fnref:6 class=footnote-backref role=doc-backlink&gt;&amp;#8617;&amp;#xfe0e;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/ol&gt;&lt;/div&gt;</content>

  <entry>
    <title>What is a Matrix? A Miserable Pile of Coefficients!</title>
    <link href="/2023/09/29/what-is-a-matrix"/>
    <updated>2023-09-29T00:00:00+00:00</updated>
    <id>/2023/09/29/what-is-a-matrix</id>
    <content type="html">&lt;p&gt;Linear algebra is undoubtedly the most useful field in all of algebra. It finds
applications in all kinds of science and engineering, like quantum mechanics,
graphics programming, and machine learning. It is the &amp;ldquo;most well-behaved&amp;rdquo;
algebraic theory, in that other abstract algebra topics often try to approximate
linear algebra, when possible.&lt;p&gt;For many students, linear algebra means vectors and matrices and determinants,
and complex formulas for computing them. Matrices, in particular, come equipped
with a fairly complicated, and &lt;em&gt;a fortiori&lt;/em&gt; convoluted, multiplication
operation.&lt;p&gt;This is not the only way to teach linear algebra, of course. Matrices and their
multiplication appear complicated, but actually are a natural and compact way to
represent a particular type of &lt;em&gt;function&lt;/em&gt;, i.e., a linear map (or linear
transformation).&lt;p&gt;This article is a short introduction to viewing linear algebra from the
perspective of abstract algebra, from which matrices arise as a computational
tool, rather than an object of study in and of themselves. I do assume some
degree of familiarity with the idea of a matrix.&lt;h2 id=linear-spaces&gt;&lt;a href=#linear-spaces&gt;Linear Spaces&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;p&gt;Most linear algebra courses open with a description of vectors in Euclidean
space: &lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.6889em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mord&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathbb&#34;&gt;R&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=msupsub&gt;&lt;span class=vlist-t&gt;&lt;span class=vlist-r&gt;&lt;span class=vlist style=height:.6644em&gt;&lt;span style=top:-3.063em;margin-right:.05em&gt;&lt;span class=pstrut style=height:2.7em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal mtight&#34;&gt;n&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;. Vectors there are defined as tuples of real numbers that can be
added, multiplied, and scaled. Two vectors can be combined into a number through
the dot product. Vectors come equipped with a notion of magnitude and direction.&lt;p&gt;However, this highly geometric picture can be counterproductive, since it is
hard to apply geometric intuition directly to higher dimensions. It also
obscures how this connects to working over a different number system, like the
complex numbers.&lt;p&gt;Instead, I&amp;rsquo;d like to open with the concept of a &lt;em&gt;linear space&lt;/em&gt;, which is
somewhat more abstract than a vector space&lt;sup id=fnref:1&gt;&lt;a href=#fn:1 class=footnote-ref role=doc-noteref&gt;1&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/sup&gt;.&lt;p&gt;First, we will need a notion of a &amp;ldquo;coefficient&amp;rdquo;, which is essentially something
that you can do arithmetic with. We will draw coefficients from a designated
&lt;em&gt;ground field&lt;/em&gt; &lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.6833em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34; style=margin-right:.07153em&gt;K&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;. A field is a setting for doing arithmetic: a set of
objects that can be added, subtracted, and multiplied, and divided in the &amp;ldquo;usual
fashion&amp;rdquo; along with special &lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.6444em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mord&gt;0&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; and &lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.6444em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mord&gt;1&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; values. &lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.6889em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathbb&#34;&gt;C&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;, and the rational numbers &lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.8556em;vertical-align:-.1667em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathbb&#34;&gt;Q&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;. If we drop the &amp;ldquo;division&amp;rdquo; requirement,
we can also include the integers &lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.6889em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathbb&#34;&gt;Z&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;, or polynomials with rational
coefficients &lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:1em;vertical-align:-.25em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathbb&#34;&gt;Q&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mopen&gt;[&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34;&gt;x&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mclose&gt;]&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;, for example.&lt;p&gt;Having chosen our coefficients &lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.6833em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34; style=margin-right:.07153em&gt;K&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;, a linear space &lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.6833em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34; style=margin-right:.22222em&gt;V&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; &lt;em&gt;over&lt;/em&gt; &lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.6833em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34; style=margin-right:.07153em&gt;K&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; is
another set of objects that can be added and subtracted (and including a special
value &lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.6444em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mord&gt;0&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;)&lt;sup id=fnref:2&gt;&lt;a href=#fn:2 class=footnote-ref role=doc-noteref&gt;2&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/sup&gt;, along with a &lt;em&gt;scaling operation&lt;/em&gt;, which takes a
coefficient &lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.5782em;vertical-align:-.0391em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34;&gt;c&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mspace style=margin-right:.2778em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mrel&gt;∈&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mspace style=margin-right:.2778em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.6833em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34; style=margin-right:.07153em&gt;K&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; and one of our objects &lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.5782em;vertical-align:-.0391em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34; style=margin-right:.03588em&gt;v&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mspace style=margin-right:.2778em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mrel&gt;∈&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mspace style=margin-right:.2778em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.6833em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34; style=margin-right:.22222em&gt;V&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; and produces a new
&lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.5782em;vertical-align:-.0391em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34;&gt;c&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34; style=margin-right:.03588em&gt;v&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mspace style=margin-right:.2778em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mrel&gt;∈&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mspace style=margin-right:.2778em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.6833em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34; style=margin-right:.22222em&gt;V&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;.&lt;p&gt;The important part of the scaling operation is that it&amp;rsquo;s compatible with
addition: if we have &lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.8889em;vertical-align:-.1944em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34;&gt;a&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mpunct&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mspace style=margin-right:.1667em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34;&gt;b&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mspace style=margin-right:.2778em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mrel&gt;∈&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mspace style=margin-right:.2778em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.6833em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34; style=margin-right:.07153em&gt;K&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; and &lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.7335em;vertical-align:-.1944em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34; href=#code:1&gt;LaTeX&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;This is what makes a linear space &amp;ldquo;linear&amp;rdquo;: you can write equations that look
like first-degree polynomials (e.g. &lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.6667em;vertical-align:-.0833em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34;&gt;a&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34;&gt;x&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mspace style=margin-right:.2222em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mbin&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mspace style=margin-right:.2222em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.6944em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34;&gt;b&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;), and which can be &lt;em&gt;manipulated
like first-degree polynomials&lt;/em&gt;.&lt;p&gt;These polynomials are called linear because their graph looks like a line.
There&amp;rsquo;s no multiplication, so we can&amp;rsquo;t have &lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.8141em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mord&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34;&gt;x&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=msupsub&gt;&lt;span class=vlist-t&gt;&lt;span class=vlist-r&gt;&lt;span class=vlist style=height:.8141em&gt;&lt;span style=top:-3.063em;margin-right:.05em&gt;&lt;span class=pstrut style=height:2.7em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mtight&#34;&gt;2&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;, but we do have
multiplication by a coefficient. This is what makes linear algebra is &amp;ldquo;linear&amp;rdquo;.&lt;p&gt;Some examples: &lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.4306em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34;&gt;n&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;-tuples of elements drawn from any field are a linear space
over that field, by componentwise addition and scalar multiplication; e.g.,
&lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.8141em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mord&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathbb&#34;&gt;R&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=msupsub&gt;&lt;span class=vlist-t&gt;&lt;span class=vlist-r&gt;&lt;span class=vlist style=height:.8141em&gt;&lt;span style=top:-3.063em;margin-right:.05em&gt;&lt;span class=pstrut style=height:2.7em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mtight&#34;&gt;3&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;. Setting &lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.4306em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34;&gt;n&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mspace style=margin-right:.2778em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mrel&gt;=&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mspace style=margin-right:.2778em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.6444em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mord&gt;1&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; shows that every field is a linear space over itself.&lt;p&gt;Polynomials in one variable over some field, &lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:1em;vertical-align:-.25em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34; style=margin-right:.07153em&gt;K&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mopen&gt;[&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34;&gt;x&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mclose&gt;]&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;, are also a linear space,
since polynomials can be added together and scaled by a any value in &lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.6833em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34; style=margin-right:.07153em&gt;K&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;
(since lone coefficients are degree zero polynomials). Real-valued functions
also form a linear space over &lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.6889em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathbb&#34;&gt;R&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; in a similar way.&lt;h3 id=linear-transformations&gt;&lt;a href=#linear-transformations&gt;Linear Transformations&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;A linear map is a function &lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.8889em;vertical-align:-.1944em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34; style=margin-right:.10764em&gt;f&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mspace style=margin-right:.2778em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mrel&gt;:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mspace style=margin-right:.2778em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.6833em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34; style=margin-right:.22222em&gt;V&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mspace style=margin-right:.2778em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mrel&gt;→&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mspace style=margin-right:.2778em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.6833em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34; style=margin-right:.13889em&gt;W&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; between two linear spaces &lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.6833em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34; style=margin-right:.22222em&gt;V&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; and
&lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.6833em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34; style=margin-right:.13889em&gt;W&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; over &lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.6833em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34; style=margin-right:.07153em&gt;K&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; which &amp;ldquo;respects&amp;rdquo; the linear structure in a particular way. That
is, for any &lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.5782em;vertical-align:-.0391em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34;&gt;c&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mspace style=margin-right:.2778em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mrel&gt;∈&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mspace style=margin-right:.2778em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.6833em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34; style=margin-right:.07153em&gt;K&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; and &lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.7335em;vertical-align:-.1944em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34; style=margin-right:.03588em&gt;v&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mpunct&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mspace style=margin-right:.1667em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34; style=margin-right:.02691em&gt;w&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mspace style=margin-right:.2778em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mrel&gt;∈&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mspace style=margin-right:.2778em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.6833em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34; style=margin-right:.10764em&gt;f&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mopen&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34; style=margin-right:.03588em&gt;v&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mclose&gt;)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mspace style=margin-right:.2222em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mbin&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mspace style=margin-right:.2222em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34; style=margin-right:.10764em&gt;f&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mopen&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34; style=margin-right:.02691em&gt;w&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mclose&gt;)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style=top:-2.41em&gt;&lt;span class=pstrut style=height:3em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mord&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34; style=margin-right:.10764em&gt;f&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mopen&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34;&gt;c&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34; style=margin-right:.03588em&gt;v&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mclose&gt;)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mspace style=margin-right:.2778em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mrel&gt;=&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mspace style=margin-right:.2778em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34;&gt;c&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mspace style=margin-right:.2222em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mbin&gt;⋅&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mspace style=margin-right:.2222em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34; style=margin-right:.10764em&gt;f&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mopen&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34; style=margin-right:.03588em&gt;v&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mclose&gt;)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=vlist-s&gt;​&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=vlist-r&gt;&lt;span class=vlist style=height:1.25em&gt;&lt;span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:2&gt;LaTeX&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;We call this type of relationship (respecting addition and scaling) &amp;ldquo;linearity&amp;rdquo;.
One way to think of this relationship is that &lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.8889em;vertical-align:-.1944em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34; style=margin-right:.10764em&gt;f&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; is kind of like a different
kind of coefficient, in that it distributes over addition, which commutes with
the &amp;ldquo;ordinary&amp;rdquo; coefficients from &lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.6833em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34; style=margin-right:.07153em&gt;K&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;. However, applying &lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.8889em;vertical-align:-.1944em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34; style=margin-right:.10764em&gt;f&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; produces a value
from &lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.6833em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34; style=margin-right:.13889em&gt;W&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; rather than &lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.6833em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34; style=margin-right:.22222em&gt;V&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;.&lt;p&gt;Another way to think of it is that if we have a linear polynomial like
&lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:1em;vertical-align:-.25em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34;&gt;p&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mopen&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34;&gt;x&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mclose&gt;)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mspace style=margin-right:.2778em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mrel&gt;=&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mspace style=margin-right:.2778em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.6667em;vertical-align:-.0833em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34;&gt;a&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34;&gt;x&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mspace style=margin-right:.2222em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mbin&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mspace style=margin-right:.2222em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.6944em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34;&gt;b&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; in &lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.4306em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34;&gt;x&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;, then &lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:1em;vertical-align:-.25em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34; style=margin-right:.10764em&gt;f&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mopen&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34;&gt;p&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mopen&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34;&gt;x&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mclose&gt;))&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mspace style=margin-right:.2778em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mrel&gt;=&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mspace style=margin-right:.2778em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:1em;vertical-align:-.25em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34;&gt;p&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mopen&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34; style=margin-right:.10764em&gt;f&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mopen&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34;&gt;x&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mclose&gt;))&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;. We say that &lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.8889em;vertical-align:-.1944em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34; style=margin-right:.10764em&gt;f&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;em&gt;commutes&lt;/em&gt; with all linear polynomials.&lt;p&gt;The most obvious sort of linear map is scaling. Given any coefficient
&lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.5782em;vertical-align:-.0391em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34;&gt;c&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mspace style=margin-right:.2778em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mrel&gt;∈&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mspace style=margin-right:.2778em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.6833em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34; style=margin-right:.07153em&gt;K&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;, it defines a &amp;ldquo;scaling map&amp;rdquo;:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:3&gt;&lt;span class=katex-display&gt;&lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:3em;vertical-align:-1.25em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mord&gt;&lt;span class=mtable&gt;&lt;span class=col-align-c&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;vlist-t vlist-t2&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=vlist-r&gt;&lt;span class=vlist style=height:1.75em&gt;&lt;span style=top:-3.91em&gt;&lt;span class=pstrut style=height:3em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mord&gt;&lt;span class=mord&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34;&gt;μ&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=msupsub&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;vlist-t vlist-t2&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=vlist-r&gt;&lt;span class=vlist style=height:.1514em&gt;&lt;span style=top:-2.55em;margin-left:0;margin-right:.05em&gt;&lt;span class=pstrut style=height:2.7em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal mtight&#34;&gt;c&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=vlist-s&gt;​&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=vlist-r&gt;&lt;span class=vlist style=height:.15em&gt;&lt;span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mspace style=margin-right:.2778em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mrel&gt;:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mspace style=margin-right:.2778em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34; style=margin-right:.22222em&gt;V&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mspace style=margin-right:.2778em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mrel&gt;→&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mspace style=margin-right:.2778em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34; style=margin-right:.22222em&gt;V&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style=top:-2.41em&gt;&lt;span class=pstrut style=height:3em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mord&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34; style=margin-right:.03588em&gt;v&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mspace style=margin-right:.2778em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mrel&gt;↦&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mspace style=margin-right:.2778em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34;&gt;c&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34; style=margin-right:.03588em&gt;v&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=vlist-s&gt;​&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=vlist-r&gt;&lt;span class=vlist style=height:1.25em&gt;&lt;span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:3&gt;LaTeX&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;It&amp;rsquo;s trivial to check this is a linear map, by plugging it into the above
equations: it&amp;rsquo;s linear because scaling is distributive and commutative.&lt;p&gt;Linear maps are the essential thing we study in linear algebra, since they
describe all the different kinds of relationships between linear spaces.&lt;p&gt;Some linear maps are complicated. For example, a function from &lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.8141em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mord&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathbb&#34;&gt;R&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=msupsub&gt;&lt;span class=vlist-t&gt;&lt;span class=vlist-r&gt;&lt;span class=vlist style=height:.8141em&gt;&lt;span style=top:-3.063em;margin-right:.05em&gt;&lt;span class=pstrut style=height:2.7em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mtight&#34;&gt;2&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mspace style=margin-right:.2778em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mrel&gt;→&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mspace style=margin-right:.2778em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.8141em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mord&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathbb&#34;&gt;R&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=msupsub&gt;&lt;span class=vlist-t&gt;&lt;span class=vlist-r&gt;&lt;span class=vlist style=height:.8141em&gt;&lt;span style=top:-3.063em;margin-right:.05em&gt;&lt;span class=pstrut style=height:2.7em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mtight&#34;&gt;2&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;
that rotates the plane by some angle &lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.6944em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34; style=margin-right:.02778em&gt;θ&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; is linear, as are operations
that stretch or shear the plane. However, they can&amp;rsquo;t &amp;ldquo;bend&amp;rdquo; or &amp;ldquo;fold&amp;rdquo; the plane:
they are all fairly rigid motions. In the linear space &lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:1em;vertical-align:-.25em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathbb&#34;&gt;Q&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mopen&gt;[&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34;&gt;x&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mclose&gt;]&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; of rational
polynomials, multiplication by &lt;em&gt;any&lt;/em&gt; polynomial, such as &lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.4306em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34;&gt;x&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; or &lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.8974em;vertical-align:-.0833em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mord&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34;&gt;x&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=msupsub&gt;&lt;span class=vlist-t&gt;&lt;span class=vlist-r&gt;&lt;span class=vlist style=height:.8141em&gt;&lt;span style=top:-3.063em;margin-right:.05em&gt;&lt;span class=pstrut style=height:2.7em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mtight&#34;&gt;2&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mspace style=margin-right:.2222em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mbin&gt;−&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mspace style=margin-right:.2222em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.6444em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mord&gt;1&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;,
is a linear map. The notion of &amp;ldquo;linear map&amp;rdquo; depends heavily on the space we&amp;rsquo;re
in.&lt;p&gt;Unfortunately, linear maps as they are quite opaque, and do not lend themselves
well to calculation. However, we can build an explicit representation using a

construction of &lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:1em;vertical-align:-.25em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34; is essentially &amp;ldquo;collapsing&amp;rdquo; the dimension &lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.5806em;vertical-align:-.15em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mord&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34;&gt;e&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=msupsub&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;vlist-t vlist-t2&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=vlist-r&gt;&lt;span class=vlist style=height:.3011em&gt;&lt;span style=top:-2.55em;margin-left:0;margin-right:.05em&gt;&lt;span class=pstrut style=height:2.7em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mtight&#34;&gt;1&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=vlist-s&gt;​&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=vlist-r&gt;&lt;span class=vlist style=height:.15em&gt;&lt;span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;
&amp;ldquo;points&amp;rdquo; in, giving us a new space where we&amp;rsquo;ve &amp;ldquo;deleted&amp;rdquo; all of the elements
that have a nonzero &lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.5806em;vertical-align:-.15em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mord&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34;&gt;e&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=msupsub&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;vlist-t vlist-t2&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=vlist-r&gt;&lt;span class=vlist style=height:.3011em&gt;&lt;span style=top:-2.55em;margin-left:0;margin-right:.05em&gt;&lt;span class=pstrut style=height:2.7em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mtight&#34;&gt;1&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=vlist-s&gt;​&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=vlist-r&gt;&lt;span class=vlist style=height:.15em&gt;&lt;span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; component.&lt;p&gt;However, this only works when the dimension is finite; more complex methods must

may be more computationally convenient.&lt;p&gt;Over &lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.8141em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mord&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathbb&#34;&gt;R&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=msupsub&gt;&lt;span class=vlist-t&gt;&lt;span class=vlist-r&gt;&lt;span class=vlist style=height:.8141em&gt;&lt;span style=top:-3.063em;margin-right:.05em&gt;&lt;span class=pstrut style=height:2.7em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mtight&#34;&gt;2&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;, &lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:1em;vertical-align:-.25em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mopen&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mord&gt;1&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mpunct&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mspace style=margin-right:.1667em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mord&gt;0&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mclose&gt;)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; and &lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:1em;vertical-align:-.25em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mopen&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mord&gt;0&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mpunct&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mspace style=margin-right:.1667em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mord&gt;1&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mclose&gt;)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; are sometimes called the &amp;ldquo;standard
basis&amp;rdquo;, but &lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:1em;vertical-align:-.25em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mopen&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mord&gt;1&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mpunct&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mspace style=margin-right:.1667em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mord&gt;2&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mclose&gt;)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; and &lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:1em;vertical-align:-.25em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mopen&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mord&gt;3&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mpunct&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mspace style=margin-right:.1667em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mord&gt;−&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mord&gt;4&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mclose&gt;)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; are also a basis for this space. One easy
mistake to make, particularly when working over the tuple space &lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.6833em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mord&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34; style=margin-right:.07153em&gt;K&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=msupsub&gt;&lt;span class=vlist-t&gt;&lt;span class=vlist-r&gt;&lt;span class=vlist style=height:.6644em&gt;&lt;span style=top:-3.063em;margin-right:.05em&gt;&lt;span class=pstrut style=height:2.7em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal mtight&#34;&gt;n&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;, is to
confuse the actual elements of the linear space with the coefficient vectors
that represent them. Working with abstract linear spaces eliminates this source

bases &lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.5806em;vertical-align:-.15em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mord&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34;&gt;e&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=msupsub&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;vlist-t vlist-t2&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=vlist-r&gt;&lt;span class=vlist style=height:.3117em&gt;&lt;span style=top:-2.55em;margin-left:0;margin-right:.05em&gt;&lt;span class=pstrut style=height:2.7em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal mtight&#34;&gt;i&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=vlist-s&gt;​&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=vlist-r&gt;&lt;span class=vlist style=height:.15em&gt;&lt;span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; and &lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.9805em;vertical-align:-.2861em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mord&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34;&gt;d&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=msupsub&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;vlist-t vlist-t2&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=vlist-r&gt;&lt;span class=vlist style=height:.3117em&gt;&lt;span style=top:-2.55em;margin-left:0;margin-right:.05em&gt;&lt;span class=pstrut style=height:2.7em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal mtight&#34; style=margin-right:.05724em&gt;j&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=vlist-s&gt;​&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=vlist-r&gt;&lt;span class=vlist style=height:.2861em&gt;&lt;span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; for them, and let&amp;rsquo;s consider a linear map

Thus,
it will swap the first two coefficients of any column vector.&lt;p&gt;Matrices may seem unintuitive when they&amp;rsquo;re introduced as a subject of study.
Every student encountering matrices for the same time may ask &amp;ldquo;If they add
componentwise, why don&amp;rsquo;t they multiply componentwise too?&amp;rdquo;&lt;p&gt;However, approaching matrices as a computational and representational tool shows
that the convoluted-looking matrix multiplication formula is a direct
consequence of linearity.&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:18&gt;&lt;span class=katex-display&gt;&lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:3em;vertical-align:-1.25em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mord&gt;&lt;span class=mtable&gt;&lt;span class=col-align-c&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;vlist-t vlist-t2&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=vlist-r&gt;&lt;span class=vlist style=height:1.75em&gt;&lt;span style=top:-3.91em&gt;&lt;span class=pstrut style=height:3em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mord&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34; spaces, which I think generates unnecessary confusion in this case. &amp;ldquo;Linear
space&amp;rdquo; is a bit more on the nose for what I&amp;rsquo;m going for.&amp;#160;&lt;a href=#fnref:1 class=footnote-backref role=doc-backlink&gt;&amp;#8617;&amp;#xfe0e;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;li id=fn:2&gt;&lt;p&gt;This type of structure (just the addition part) is also called an &amp;ldquo;abelian

I will not bother giving
this index set a name.&amp;#160;&lt;a href=#fnref:3 class=footnote-backref role=doc-backlink&gt;&amp;#8617;&amp;#xfe0e;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;li id=fn:4&gt;&lt;p&gt;This is sometimes called the
&lt;a href=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dimension_theorem_for_vector_spaces&gt;&lt;em&gt;dimension theorem&lt;/em&gt;&lt;/a&gt;,
which is somewhat tedious to prove.&amp;#160;&lt;a href=#fnref:4 class=footnote-backref role=doc-backlink&gt;&amp;#8617;&amp;#xfe0e;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;li id=fn:5&gt;&lt;p&gt;An example of a messy infinite-dimensional basis is &lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.6889em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathbb&#34;&gt;R&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; considered as
linear space over &lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.8556em;vertical-align:-.1667em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathbb&#34;&gt;Q&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; (in general, every field is a linear space over its
subfields). The basis for this space essentially has to be &amp;ldquo;&lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.6444em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mord&gt;1&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;, and all

&lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.4306em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34;&gt;e&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; and &lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.4306em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathnormal&#34; style=margin-right:.03588em&gt;π&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;.&lt;p&gt;On the other hand, &lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.6889em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathbb&#34;&gt;C&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; is two-dimensional over &lt;span class=katex&gt;&lt;span class=katex-html aria-hidden=true&gt;&lt;span class=base&gt;&lt;span class=strut style=height:.6889em&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&#34;mord mathbb&#34;&gt;R&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;, with basis
