&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=fm&gt;println!&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=s&gt;&amp;#34;{}&amp;#34;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mf&gt;42.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;string&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;());&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button godbolt&#34; href=https://godbolt.&gt;godbolt&lt;/a&gt;
&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:1&gt;Rust&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;Notice that we call the trait method &lt;code&gt;Stringer::string&lt;/code&gt; directly on the value in
question. This means that traits (at least, those currently in scope) inject
their methods into the namespace of anything that implements them.&lt;p&gt;Now, this isn&amp;rsquo;t immediately a problem, because Rust&amp;rsquo;s namespace lookup rules are
such that methods &lt;em&gt;inherent&lt;/em&gt; to a type are searched for first:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:2&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-rust highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;trait&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;Stringer&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;fn&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nf&gt;string&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;amp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=bp&gt;self&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;-&amp;gt; &lt;span class=nb&gt;String&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;struct&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nc&gt;Woofer&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;impl&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;Stringer&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;for&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;Woofer&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;fn&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nf&gt;string&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;amp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=bp&gt;self&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;-&amp;gt; &lt;span class=nb&gt;String&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;    &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=fm&gt;format!&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=s&gt;&amp;#34;woof&amp;#34;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;impl&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;Woofer&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;fn&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nf&gt;string&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;amp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=bp&gt;self&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;-&amp;gt; &lt;span class=nb&gt;String&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;    &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=fm&gt;format!&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=s&gt;&amp;#34;bark&amp;#34;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;// Prints `bark`.
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=fm&gt;println!&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=s&gt;&amp;#34;{}&amp;#34;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;Woofer&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;string&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;());&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button godbolt&#34; href=&#34;https://godbolt.&#34;&gt;godbolt&lt;/a&gt;
&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:2&gt;Rust&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;This means that traits cannot &lt;em&gt;easily&lt;/em&gt; break downstream code by adding new
methods, but there are a few possible hazards:&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;&lt;p&gt;If the owner of a type adds a method with the same name as a trait method, it
will override direct (i.e., &lt;code&gt;foo.string()&lt;/code&gt;) calls to that trait method, even
if the type owner is unaware of the trait method.&lt;li&gt;&lt;p&gt;If traits &lt;code&gt;A&lt;/code&gt; and &lt;code&gt;B&lt;/code&gt; are in scope, and &lt;code&gt;String&lt;/code&gt; implements both, and we call
&lt;code&gt;str.foo()&lt;/code&gt; (which resolves to &lt;code&gt;A::foo()&lt;/code&gt;), and later &lt;code&gt;B&lt;/code&gt; adds a new method
&lt;code&gt;B::foo()&lt;/code&gt;, the callsite for &lt;code&gt;String&lt;/code&gt; will break. &lt;code&gt;A&lt;/code&gt; and &lt;code&gt;B&lt;/code&gt;&amp;rsquo;s owners do not
need to be aware of each other for this to happen.&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;p&gt;Of course, Rust has a disambiguation mechanism. Given any trait implementation
&lt;code&gt;Foo: Bar&lt;/code&gt;, we can reference its items by writing &lt;code&gt;&amp;lt;Foo as Bar&gt;::baz&lt;/code&gt;. However,
this syntax is &lt;em&gt;very&lt;/em&gt; unweildy (it doesn&amp;rsquo;t work with method chaining), so it
doesn&amp;rsquo;t get used. As a result, small evolution hazards can build up in a large
codebase.&lt;p&gt;Those who know me know that I often talk about a syntax that I call
&lt;code&gt;foo.Trait::method()&lt;/code&gt;, or &amp;ldquo;qualified method call syntax&amp;rdquo;. In this post, I want
to discuss this syntax in more detail, and some related ideas, and how they
factor into type and trait design.&lt;h2 id=paths-as-methods&gt;&lt;a href=#paths-as-methods&gt;Paths-as-Methods&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;p&gt;This idea isn&amp;rsquo;t new; others have proposed it, and it forms the core of Carbon&amp;rsquo;s
version of trait method calls (you can read more about Carbon&amp;rsquo;s name lookup
story
&lt;a href=https://github.com/carbon-language/carbon-lang/blob/trunk/docs/design/expressions/member_access.md&gt;here&lt;/a&gt;).&lt;p&gt;Let&amp;rsquo;s recreate the original example in Carbon (bear in mind that I am not an
expert on this language, and the semantics are still up in the air).&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:3&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-carbon highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;interface&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;Stringer&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;fn&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nf&gt;String&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;[&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=bp&gt;self&lt;/span&gt;: &lt;span class=nc&gt;Self&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;]()&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;-&amp;gt; &lt;span class=nb&gt;String&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;external&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;impl&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=kt&gt;i32&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;as&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;Stringer&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;fn&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nf&gt;String&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;[&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=bp&gt;self&lt;/span&gt;: &lt;span class=nc&gt;Self&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;]()&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;-&amp;gt; &lt;span class=nb&gt;String&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;..&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;fn&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nf&gt;Run&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;()&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;Carbon&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;Print&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mf&gt;42.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;Stringer&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nb&gt;String&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)())&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:3&gt;Carbon&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;Notice &lt;code&gt;42.(Stringer.String)()&lt;/code&gt;: Carbon &lt;em&gt;requires&lt;/em&gt; that we qualify the method
call, because &lt;code&gt;42&lt;/code&gt; has the concrete type &lt;code&gt;i32&lt;/code&gt;. If this were in a generic
context and we had a type variable bounded by &lt;code&gt;Stringer&lt;/code&gt;, we could just write
&lt;code&gt;x.String()&lt;/code&gt;; no ambiguity.&lt;p&gt;In Carbon, all qualification uses &lt;code&gt;.&lt;/code&gt;, so they have to add parens. Because Rust
uses &lt;code&gt;::&lt;/code&gt; for qualifying paths, we don&amp;rsquo;t have this syntactic abiguity, so we can
augment the syntax to allow more path expressions after the &lt;code&gt;.&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;p&gt;The current grammar is&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:4&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language- highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;MethodCallExpression :
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;   Expression . PathExprSegment (CallParams?)
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;PathExprSegment :
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;   PathIdentSegment (:: GenericArgs)?
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:4&gt;Plaintext&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;That is, exactly one identifier and an optional turbofish. I would like to see
this extended to allow any &lt;code&gt;QualifiedPathInExpression&lt;/code&gt; after the &lt;code&gt;.&lt;/code&gt; and before
the parens. This would allow, for example:&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;&lt;code&gt;expr.Trait::method()&lt;/code&gt;&lt;li&gt;&lt;code&gt;expr.Self::method()&lt;/code&gt;&lt;li&gt;&lt;code&gt;expr.&amp;lt;Foo as Trait&gt;::method()&lt;/code&gt;&lt;li&gt;&lt;code&gt;expr.::path::to::Trait::&amp;lt;Args&gt;::method::&amp;lt;MoreArgs&gt;()&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;p&gt;These would all be desugared as the equivalent UFCS, taking into account that
method call syntax can trigger autoref.&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;&lt;code&gt;Trait::method(expr)&lt;/code&gt;&lt;li&gt;&lt;code&gt;Self::method(expr)&lt;/code&gt;&lt;li&gt;&lt;code&gt;&amp;lt;Foo as Trait&gt;::method(expr)&lt;/code&gt;&lt;li&gt;&lt;code&gt;::path::to::Trait::&amp;lt;Args&gt;::method::&amp;lt;MoreArgs&gt;(expr)&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;p&gt;The method would still need to be valid to have been called via &lt;code&gt;.&lt;/code&gt; syntax; I&amp;rsquo;m
not proposing we add the following, even though it is unambiguous.&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:5&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-rust highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;fn&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nf&gt;square&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;x&lt;/span&gt;: &lt;span class=kt&gt;i32&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;-&amp;gt; &lt;span class=kt&gt;i32&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;x&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;*&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;x&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;// Would be equivalent to `square(42)`.
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mf&gt;42.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=bp&gt;self&lt;/span&gt;::&lt;span class=n&gt;square&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;()&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:5&gt;Rust&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;Trait method callers can now use qualified method call syntax where they might
want to use UFCS without issues around wordiness.&lt;h2 id=impl-modality&gt;&lt;a href=#impl-modality&gt;Impl Modality&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;p&gt;Of course, this isn&amp;rsquo;t the only idea from Carbon&amp;rsquo;s interfaces worth stealing;
Carbon also has a notion of &amp;ldquo;external&amp;rdquo; and &amp;ldquo;internal&amp;rdquo; &lt;code&gt;impl&lt;/code&gt;s; I will call these
&amp;ldquo;&lt;code&gt;impl&lt;/code&gt; modes&amp;rdquo;.&lt;p&gt;An external &lt;code&gt;impl&lt;/code&gt; is like the one we showed above, whose methods can only be
found by qualified lookup: &lt;code&gt;foo.(Bar.Baz)()&lt;/code&gt;. An internal &lt;code&gt;impl&lt;/code&gt; is one which is
&amp;ldquo;part&amp;rdquo; of a type.&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:6&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-carbon highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;interface&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;Stringer&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;fn&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nf&gt;String&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;[&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=bp&gt;self&lt;/span&gt;: &lt;span class=nc&gt;Self&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;]()&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;-&amp;gt; &lt;span class=nb&gt;String&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;class&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;Woofer&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;impl&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;as&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;Stringer&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;    &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;fn&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nf&gt;String&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;[&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=bp&gt;self&lt;/span&gt;: &lt;span class=nc&gt;Self&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;]()&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;-&amp;gt; &lt;span class=nb&gt;String&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;..&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;fn&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nf&gt;Run&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;()&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=kd&gt;let&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;w&lt;/span&gt;: &lt;span class=nc&gt;Woofer&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;..&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;w&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nb&gt;String&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;()&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;// Unqualified!
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:6&gt;Carbon&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;This also implies that we don&amp;rsquo;t need to import &lt;code&gt;Stringer&lt;/code&gt; to call &lt;code&gt;w.String()&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;p&gt;There are definitely traits in Rust which fit into these modes.&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;Clone&lt;/code&gt; and &lt;code&gt;Iterator&lt;/code&gt; almost always want to be internal. An iterator exists to
implement &lt;code&gt;Iterator&lt;/code&gt;, and cloning is a fundamental operation. Because both of
these traits are in the prelude, it&amp;rsquo;s not a problem, but it is a problem for
traits provided by a non-&lt;code&gt;std&lt;/code&gt; crate, like
&lt;a href=https://docs.rs/rand/latest/rand/trait.Rng.html&gt;&lt;code&gt;rand::Rng&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/a&gt;. The lack of a
way to do this leads to the proliferation of &lt;code&gt;prelude&lt;/code&gt; modules and namespace
pollution. (I think that &lt;code&gt;prelude&lt;/code&gt;s are bad library design.)&lt;p&gt;On the other hand, something like &lt;code&gt;Debug&lt;/code&gt; wants to be external very badly. It
almost never makes sense to call &lt;code&gt;foo.fmt()&lt;/code&gt;, since that gets called for you by
&lt;code&gt;println!&lt;/code&gt; and friends; not to mention that all of the &lt;code&gt;std::fmt&lt;/code&gt; traits have a
method &lt;code&gt;fmt()&lt;/code&gt;, making such a call likely to need disambiguation with UFCS.
&lt;code&gt;Borrow&lt;/code&gt; is similar; it exists to be a bound for things like &lt;code&gt;Cow&lt;/code&gt; more than to
provide the &lt;code&gt;.borrow()&lt;/code&gt; method.&lt;p&gt;There&amp;rsquo;s also a third mode, which I will call &amp;ldquo;extension impls&amp;rdquo;. These want to
inject methods into a type, either to extend it, like
&lt;a href=https://docs.rs/itertools/latest/itertools/&gt;&lt;code&gt;itertools&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/a&gt;, or as part of some
framework, like &lt;a href=https://docs.rs/tap/latest/tap/&gt;&lt;code&gt;tap&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/a&gt;. This use of traits is
somewhat controversial, but I can sympathize with wanting to have this.&lt;p&gt;If we have paths-as-methods, we can use this classification to move towards
something more like the Carbon model of method lookup, without impacting
existing uses.&lt;p&gt;My strawman is to add a &lt;code&gt;#[mode]&lt;/code&gt; attribute to place on trait &lt;code&gt;impls&lt;/code&gt;, which
allows a caller to select the behavior:&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;&lt;code&gt;#[mode(extension)]&lt;/code&gt; is today&amp;rsquo;s behavior. The &lt;code&gt;impl&lt;/code&gt;&amp;rsquo;s trait must be in scope
so that unqualified calls like &lt;code&gt;foo.method()&lt;/code&gt; resolve to it.&lt;li&gt;&lt;code&gt;#[mode(internal)]&lt;/code&gt; makes it so that &lt;code&gt;foo.method()&lt;/code&gt; can resolve to a method
from this &lt;code&gt;impl&lt;/code&gt; without its trait being in scope&lt;sup id=fnref:1&gt;&lt;a href=#fn:1 class=footnote-ref role=doc-noteref&gt;1&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/sup&gt;. It
can only be applied to &lt;code&gt;impl&lt;/code&gt;s that are such that you could write a
corresponding inherent impl, so things like
&lt;code&gt;#[mode(internal)] impl&amp;lt;T&gt; Trait for T { .. }&lt;/code&gt; are forbidden.&lt;li&gt;&lt;code&gt;#[mode(external)]&lt;/code&gt; makes it so that &lt;code&gt;foo.method()&lt;/code&gt; never resolves to a method
from this &lt;code&gt;impl&lt;/code&gt;. It must be called as &lt;code&gt;Trait::method(foo)&lt;/code&gt; or
&lt;code&gt;foo.Trait::method()&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;p&gt;Every trait would be &lt;code&gt;#[mode(extension)]&lt;/code&gt; if not annotated, and it would be easy
to migrate to external-by-default across an edition. Similarly, we could change
whether a &lt;code&gt;std&lt;/code&gt; impl is external vs extension based on the edition of the
caller, and provide a &lt;code&gt;cargo fix&lt;/code&gt; rewrite to convert from &lt;code&gt;foo.method()&lt;/code&gt; to
&lt;code&gt;foo.Trait::method()&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;p&gt;It may also make sense for traits to be able to specify the default modality of
their &lt;code&gt;impl&lt;/code&gt;s, but I haven&amp;rsquo;t thought very carefully about this.&lt;p&gt;Note that moving in the external -&gt; extension -&gt; internal direction is not a
breaking change, but moving the other way is.&lt;h2 id=what-about-delegation&gt;&lt;a href=#what-about-delegation&gt;What about Delegation?&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;p&gt;A related feature that I will touch on lightly is delegation; that is, being
able to write something like the following:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:7&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-rust highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;// crate a
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;struct&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nc&gt;Foo&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;..&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;impl&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;Foo&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;fn&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nf&gt;boing&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;()&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;-&amp;gt; &lt;span class=kt&gt;i32&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;..&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;// crate b
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;trait&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;Bar&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;fn&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nf&gt;boing&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;()&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;-&amp;gt; &lt;span class=kt&gt;i32&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;impl&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;Bar&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;for&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;Foo&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;use&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;Foo&lt;/span&gt;::&lt;span class=n&gt;boing&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:7&gt;Rust&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;The &lt;code&gt;use&lt;/code&gt; in the &lt;code&gt;impl&lt;/code&gt; indicates that we want to re-use &lt;code&gt;Foo::boing&lt;/code&gt; to
implement &lt;code&gt;&amp;lt;Foo as Bar&gt;::boing&lt;/code&gt;. This saves us having to write out a function
signature, and results in less work for the compiler because that&amp;rsquo;s one less
function we risk asking LLVM to codegen for us (at scale, this is a Big Deal).&lt;p&gt;You could imagine using delegation instead of &lt;code&gt;#[mode]&lt;/code&gt;:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:8&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-rust highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;struct&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nc&gt;Woofer&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;impl&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;Stringer&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;for&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;Woofer&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;fn&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nf&gt;string&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;amp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=bp&gt;self&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;-&amp;gt; &lt;span class=nb&gt;String&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;    &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=fm&gt;format!&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=s&gt;&amp;#34;woof&amp;#34;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;impl&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;Woofer&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;use&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;Stringer&lt;/span&gt;::&lt;span class=o&gt;*&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:8&gt;Rust&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;The reason I haven&amp;rsquo;t gone down this road is because delegation is a very large
feature, and doesn&amp;rsquo;t give us a clean way to express &lt;code&gt;#[mode(external)]&lt;/code&gt;, which
is a big part of what I want. A delegation-compatible way to express this
proposal is to not add &lt;code&gt;#[mode(internal)]&lt;/code&gt;, and add &lt;code&gt;use Trait::method;&lt;/code&gt; and
&lt;code&gt;use Trait::*;&lt;/code&gt; (and no other variations) inside of inherent &lt;code&gt;impl&lt;/code&gt; blocks.&lt;h2 id=conclusion&gt;&lt;a href=#conclusion&gt;Conclusion&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;p&gt;I don&amp;rsquo;t have the personal bandwidth to write RFCs for any of this stuff, but
it&amp;rsquo;s something I talk about a lot as a potential evolution hazard for Rust. I
hope that putting these ideas to paper can help make name resolution in Rust
more robust.&lt;div class=footnotes role=doc-endnotes&gt;&lt;hr&gt;&lt;ol&gt;&lt;li id=fn:1&gt;&lt;p&gt;This needs to carry a bunch of other restrictions, because it&amp;rsquo;s equivalent
to adding inherent methods to the implee. For example, none of the methods
can have the same name as a method in any other inherent or internal impl
block, and internal impl methods should take lookup priority over extension
impl methods during name lookup.&amp;#160;&lt;a href=#fnref:1 class=footnote-backref role=doc-backlink&gt;&amp;#8617;&amp;#xfe0e;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/ol&gt;&lt;/div&gt;</content>
  </entry>
  <entry>
    <title>Atomicless Concurrency</title>
    <link href="/2023/03/29/rseq-checkout"/>
    <updated>2023-03-29T00:00:00+00:00</updated>
    <id>/2023/03/29/rseq-checkout</id>
    <content type="html">&lt;p&gt;Let&amp;rsquo;s say we&amp;rsquo;re building an allocator. Good allocators need to serve many
threads simultaneously, and as such any lock they take is going to be highly
contended. One way to work around this, pioneered by TCMalloc, is to have
thread-local caches of blocks (hence, the &amp;ldquo;TC&amp;rdquo; - thread cached).&lt;p&gt;Unfortunately threads can be ephemeral, so book-keeping needs to grow
dynamically, and large, complex programs (like the Google Search ranking server)
can have tens of thousands of threads, so per-thread cost can add up. Also, any
time a thread context-switches and resumes, its CPU cache will contain different
cache lines &amp;ndash; likely the wrong ones. This is because either another thread
doing something compeltely different executed on that CPU, or the switched
thread &lt;em&gt;migrated&lt;/em&gt; to execute on a different core.&lt;p&gt;These days, instead of caching per-thread, TCMalloc uses &lt;em&gt;per-CPU&lt;/em&gt; data. This
means that book-keeping is fixed, and this is incredibly friendly to the CPU&amp;rsquo;s
cache: in the steady-state, each piece of the data will only ever be read or
written to by a single CPU. It also has the amazing property that &lt;em&gt;there are no
atomic operations involved&lt;/em&gt; in the fast path, because operations on per-CPU
data, by definition, do not need to be synchronized with other cores.&lt;p&gt;This post gives an overview of how to build a CPU-local data structure on modern
Linux. The exposition will be for x86, but other than the small bits of assembly
you need to write, the technique is architecture-independent.&lt;h2 id=the-kernel-primitive&gt;&lt;a href=#the-kernel-primitive&gt;The Kernel Primitive&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;p&gt;Concurrency primitives require cooperating with the kernel, which is responsible
for global scheduling decisions on the system. However, making syscalls is quite
expensive; to alieviate this, there has been a trend in Linux to use shared
memory as a kernelspace/userspace communication channel.&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Futex&gt;Futexes&lt;/a&gt; are the classic
&amp;ldquo;cas-with-the-kernel&amp;rdquo; syscall (I&amp;rsquo;m assuming basic knowledge of atomic operations
like cas in this article). In the happy path, we just need to cas on some memory
to lock a futex, and only make a syscall if we need to go to sleep because of
contention. The kernel will perform its own cas on this variable if necessary.&lt;p&gt;&lt;em&gt;Restartable sequences&lt;/em&gt; are another such proto-primitive, which are used for
per-CPUuprogramming. The relevant syscall for us, &lt;code&gt;rseq(2)&lt;/code&gt;, was added in Linux
4.18. Its manpage reads&lt;blockquote id=ref:1 class=ref ref math&gt;&lt;a href=#ref:1&gt;&lt;span class=chip&gt;reference&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;p&gt;A restartable sequence is a sequence of instructions guaranteed to be executed
atomically with respect to other threads and signal handlers on the current
CPU. If its execution does not complete atomically, the kernel changes the
execution flow by jumping to an abort handler defined by userspace for that
restartable sequence.&lt;/blockquote&gt;&lt;p&gt;A restartable sequence, or &amp;ldquo;rseq&amp;rdquo; is a special kind of critical section that the
kernel guarantees executes from start to finish without any kind of preemption.
If preemption &lt;em&gt;does&lt;/em&gt; happen (because of a signal or whatever), userspace
observes this as a jump to a special handler for that critical section.
Conceptually it&amp;rsquo;s like handling an exception:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:1&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-c++ highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;try&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=c1&gt;// Per-CPU code here.
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=k&gt;catch&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;PremptionException&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=c1&gt;// Handle having been preempted, which usally just means
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;  &lt;span class=c1&gt;// &amp;#34;try again&amp;#34;.
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:1&gt;C++&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;These critical sections are usually of the following form:&lt;ol&gt;&lt;li&gt;Read the current CPU index (the rseq mechanism provides a way to do this).&lt;li&gt;Index into some data structure and do something to it.&lt;li&gt;Complete the operation with a single memory write. This is the &amp;ldquo;commit&amp;rdquo;.&lt;/ol&gt;&lt;p&gt;All the kernel tells us is that we couldn&amp;rsquo;t finish successfully. We can always
try again, but the critical section needs to be such that executing any prefix
of it, up to the commit, has no effect on the data structure. We get no
opportunity to perform &amp;ldquo;partial rollbacks&amp;rdquo;.&lt;p&gt;In other words, the critical section must be a &lt;em&gt;transaction&lt;/em&gt;.&lt;h3 id=enabling-rseq&gt;&lt;a href=#enabling-rseq&gt;Enabling &lt;code&gt;rseq&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;Using rseqs requires turning on support for it for a particular thread; this is
what calling &lt;code&gt;rseq(2)&lt;/code&gt; (the syscall) accomplishes.&lt;p&gt;The signature for this syscall looks like this:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:2&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-rust highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;// This type is part of Linux&amp;#39;s ABI.
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=cp&gt;#[repr(C, align(32))]&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;struct&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nc&gt;Rseq&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;cpu_id_start&lt;/span&gt;: &lt;span class=kt&gt;u32&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;

&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;

&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;fn&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nf&gt;rseq&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;rseq&lt;/span&gt;: &lt;span class=o&gt;*&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;mut&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;Rseq&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;len&lt;/span&gt;: &lt;span class=kt&gt;u32&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;flags&lt;/span&gt;: &lt;span class=kt&gt;i32&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;signature&lt;/span&gt;: &lt;span class=kt&gt;u32&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;-&amp;gt; &lt;span class=kt&gt;i32&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:2&gt;Rust&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;The syscall registers &amp;ldquo;the&amp;rdquo; &lt;code&gt;Rseq&lt;/code&gt; struct for the current thread; there can be
at most one, per thread.&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;rseq&lt;/code&gt; is a pointer to this struct. &lt;code&gt;len&lt;/code&gt; should be &lt;code&gt;size_of::&amp;lt;Rseq&gt;()&lt;/code&gt;, and
&lt;code&gt;signature&lt;/code&gt; can be any 32-bit integer (more on this later). For our purposes, we
can ignore &lt;code&gt;flags&lt;/code&gt; on the struct.&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;flags&lt;/code&gt; on the syscall, on the other hand, is used to indicate whether we&amp;rsquo;re
unregistering the struct; this is explained below.&lt;p&gt;In the interest of exposition, we&amp;rsquo;ll call the syscall directly. If you&amp;rsquo;ve never
seen how a Linux syscall is done (on x86), you load the syscall number into
&lt;code&gt;rax&lt;/code&gt;, then up to six arguments in &lt;code&gt;rdi&lt;/code&gt;, &lt;code&gt;rsi&lt;/code&gt;, &lt;code&gt;rdx&lt;/code&gt;, &lt;code&gt;r10&lt;/code&gt;, &lt;code&gt;r8&lt;/code&gt;,
&lt;code&gt;r9&lt;/code&gt;&lt;sup id=fnref:1&gt;&lt;a href=#fn:1 class=footnote-ref role=doc-noteref&gt;1&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/sup&gt;. We only need the first four.&lt;p&gt;The return value comes out in &lt;code&gt;rax&lt;/code&gt;, which is 0 on success, and a negative of
an &lt;code&gt;errno&lt;/code&gt; code otherwise. In particular, we need to check for &lt;code&gt;EINTR&lt;/code&gt; to deal
with syscall interruption. (every Linux syscall can be interrupted).&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:3&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-rust highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;unsafe&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;fn&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nf&gt;raw_rseq&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;rseq&lt;/span&gt;: &lt;span class=o&gt;*&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;mut&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;Rseq&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;unregister&lt;/span&gt;: &lt;span class=kt&gt;bool&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;signature&lt;/span&gt;: &lt;span class=kt&gt;u32&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;

&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;      &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mi&gt;0&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;=&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;break&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;      &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;// Success, we&amp;#39;re done.
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;      &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;-&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mi&gt;4&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;=&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;continue&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;// EINTR, try again.
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;      &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;errno&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;=&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=fm&gt;panic!&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=s&gt;&amp;#34;error calling rseq(2): {}&amp;#34;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;-&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;errno&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;),&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;    &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:3&gt;Rust&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;Note the &lt;code&gt;unregister&lt;/code&gt; parameter: this is used to tear down &lt;code&gt;rseq&lt;/code&gt; support on the
way out of a thread. Generally, &lt;code&gt;rseq&lt;/code&gt; will be a thread-local, and registration
happens at thread startup. Glibc will do this and has a mechanism for acquiring
the &lt;code&gt;rseq&lt;/code&gt; pointer. Unfortunately, the glibc I have isn&amp;rsquo;t new enough to know to
do this, so I hacked up something to register my own thread local.&lt;p&gt;I had the bright idea of putting my &lt;code&gt;Rseq&lt;/code&gt; struct in a box, which triggered an
interesting bug: when a thread exits, it destroys all of the thread local
variables, including the box to hold our &lt;code&gt;Rseq&lt;/code&gt;. But if the thread then syscalls
to deallocate its stack, when the kernel goes to resume, it will attempt to
write the current CPU index to the &lt;code&gt;rseq.cpu_id&lt;/code&gt; field.&lt;p&gt;This presents a problem, because the kernel is probably going to write to a
garbage location. This is all but guaranteed to result in a segfault. Debuggers
observe this as a segfault on the instruction right after the &lt;code&gt;syscall&lt;/code&gt;
instruction; I spent half an hour trying to figure out what was causing a call
to &lt;code&gt;madvise(2)&lt;/code&gt; to segfault.&lt;p&gt;Hence, we need to wrap our thread local in something that will call &lt;code&gt;rseq(2)&lt;/code&gt; to
unregister the struct. Putting everything together we get something like this.&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:4&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-rust highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;fn&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nf&gt;current_thread_rseq&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;()&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;-&amp;gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;*&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;mut&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;Rseq&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;

&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;        &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;crit_sec&lt;/span&gt;: &lt;span class=mi&gt;0&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;

&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;      &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;})));&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;

&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;      &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;unsafe&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;raw_rseq&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;rseq&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mf&gt;0.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;get&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(),&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=kc&gt;false&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;RSEQ_SIG&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;);&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;      &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;rseq&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;    &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;};&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;RSEQ&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;with&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;|&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;ra&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;|&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;ra&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mf&gt;0.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;get&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;())&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:4&gt;Rust&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;Per Rust&amp;rsquo;s semantics, this will execute the first time we access this thread
local, instead of at thread startup. Not &lt;em&gt;ideal&lt;/em&gt;, since now we pay for an
(uncontended) atomic read every time we touch RSEQ, but it will do.&lt;h3 id=creating-a-critical-section&gt;&lt;a href=#creating-a-critical-section&gt;Creating a Critical Section&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;To set up and execute a restartable sequence, we need to assemble a struct that
describes it. The following struct is also defined by Linux&amp;rsquo;s syscall ABI:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:5&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-rust highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=cp&gt;#[repr(C, align(32))]&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;struct&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nc&gt;CritSec&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;version&lt;/span&gt;: &lt;span class=kt&gt;u32&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;flags&lt;/span&gt;: &lt;span class=kt&gt;u32&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;start&lt;/span&gt;: &lt;span class=kt&gt;u64&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;len&lt;/span&gt;: &lt;span class=kt&gt;u64&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;abort_handler&lt;/span&gt;: &lt;span class=kt&gt;u64&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:5&gt;Rust&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;start&lt;/code&gt; is the address of the first instruction in the sequence, and &lt;code&gt;len&lt;/code&gt; is
the length of the sequence in bytes. &lt;code&gt;abort_handler&lt;/code&gt; is the address of the abort
handler. &lt;code&gt;version&lt;/code&gt; must be 0 and we can ignore &lt;code&gt;flags&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;p&gt;Once we have a value of this struct (on the stack or as a constant), we grab
&lt;code&gt;RSEQ&lt;/code&gt; and atomically store the address of our &lt;code&gt;CritSec&lt;/code&gt; to &lt;code&gt;RSEQ.crit_sec&lt;/code&gt;.
This needs to be atomic because the kernel may decide to look at this pointer
from a different CPU core, but it likely will not be contended.&lt;p&gt;Note that &lt;code&gt;RSEQ.crit_sec&lt;/code&gt; should be null before we do this; restartable
sequences can&amp;rsquo;t nest.&lt;p&gt;Next time the kernel preempts our thread (and later gets ready to resume it), it
will look at &lt;code&gt;RSEQ.crit_sec&lt;/code&gt; to decide if it preempted a restartable sequence
and, if so, jump to the abort handler.&lt;p&gt;Once we finish our critical section, we must reset &lt;code&gt;RSEQ.crit_sec&lt;/code&gt; to 0.&lt;blockquote id=aside:1 class=aside aside&gt;&lt;a href=#aside:1&gt;&lt;span class=chip&gt;aside&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;p&gt;There is a wrinkle: we would like for our &lt;code&gt;CritSec&lt;/code&gt; value to be a constant,
but Rust doesn&amp;rsquo;t provide us with a way to initialize the &lt;code&gt;start&lt;/code&gt; and
&lt;code&gt;abort_handler&lt;/code&gt; fields directly, since it doesn&amp;rsquo;t have a way to
refer&lt;sup id=fnref:2&gt;&lt;a href=#fn:2 class=footnote-ref role=doc-noteref&gt;2&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/sup&gt; to the labels (jump targets) inside the inline assembly.
The simplest way to get around this is to assemble (lol) the &lt;code&gt;CritSec&lt;/code&gt; on the
stack, with inline assembly. The overhead is quite minimal.&lt;/blockquote&gt;&lt;p&gt;On x86, this is what our boilerplate will look like:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:6&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-rust highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=kd&gt;let&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;mut&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;cs&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;MaybeUninit&lt;/span&gt;::&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;lt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;CritSec&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;::&lt;span class=n&gt;uninit&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;();&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=kd&gt;let&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;mut&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;ok&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mi&gt;1&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=fm&gt;asm!&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=s&gt;r&amp;#34;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=s&gt;  // We meed to do `rip`-relative loads so that this code is PIC;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=s&gt;  // otherwise we&amp;#39;ll get linker errors. Thus, we can&amp;#39;t `mov`
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=s&gt;  // directly; we need to compute the address with a `lea`
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=s&gt;  // first.
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=s&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=s&gt;  // Initialize the first two fields to zero.
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=s&gt;  mov qword ptr [{_cs}], 0
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=s&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=s&gt;  // Load `90f` into `cs.start`. Note that this is &amp;#39;forward
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=s&gt;  // reference&amp;#39; to the jump target `90:` below.
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=s&gt;  lea {_pc}, [90f + rip]
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=s&gt;  mov qword ptr [{_cs} + 8], {_pc}
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=s&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=s&gt;  // We need to get the difference `91f - 90f` into `cs.len`.
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=s&gt;  // To do that, we write `-90f` to it, and then add `91f`.
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=s&gt;  neg {_pc}
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=s&gt;  mov qword ptr [{_cs} + 16], {_pc}
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=s&gt;  lea {_pc}, [91f + rip]
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=s&gt;  add qword ptr [{_cs} + 16], {_pc}
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=s&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=s&gt;  // Same as the first line, but loading `cs.abort_handler`.

&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=s&gt;  // This is written this way simply because we can&amp;#39;t early-return

&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;_ok&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;inout&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;reg&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;ok&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;_cs&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;in&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;reg&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;amp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;mut&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;cs&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;as&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;*&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;mut&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;CritSec&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;rseq&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;in&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;reg&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;current_thread_rseq&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(),&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:6&gt;Rust&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;A few things to note:&lt;ol&gt;&lt;li&gt;Because this is inline assembly, we need to use numeric labels. I&amp;rsquo;ve chosen
labels in the 90s for no particular reason. &lt;code&gt;90:&lt;/code&gt; declares a jump target,
and &lt;code&gt;90f&lt;/code&gt; is a forward reference to that instruction address.&lt;li&gt;Most of this assembly is just initalizing a struct&lt;sup id=fnref:3&gt;&lt;a href=#fn:3 class=footnote-ref role=doc-noteref&gt;3&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/sup&gt;. It&amp;rsquo;s not until
the &lt;code&gt;mov&lt;/code&gt; right before &lt;code&gt;90:&lt;/code&gt; (the critical section start) that anything
interesting happens.&lt;li&gt;Immediately before &lt;code&gt;92:&lt;/code&gt; (the abort handler) is an &lt;code&gt;.int&lt;/code&gt; directive that
emits the same four-byte signature we passed to &lt;code&gt;rseq(2)&lt;/code&gt; into the
instruction stream. This &lt;em&gt;must&lt;/em&gt; be here, otherwise the kernel will issue a
segfault to the thread. This is a very basic control-flow integrity feature.&lt;li&gt;We clear &lt;code&gt;RSEQ.crit_sec&lt;/code&gt; at the very end.&lt;/ol&gt;&lt;p&gt;This is a lot of boilerplate. In an ideal world, we could have something like
the following:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:7&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-rust highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;fn&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nf&gt;run_rseq&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;cs&lt;/span&gt;: &lt;span class=nc&gt;extern&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=s&gt;&amp;#34;C&amp;#34;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;unsafe&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;fn&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=kt&gt;u32&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;));&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:7&gt;Rust&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;Unfortunately, this is very hard to do, because the constraints on restartable
sequences are draconian:&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;Can&amp;rsquo;t jump out of the critical section until it completes or aborts. This
means you can&amp;rsquo;t call functions or make syscalls!&lt;li&gt;Last instruction must be the commit, which is a memory store operation, &lt;em&gt;not&lt;/em&gt;
a return.&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;p&gt;This means that you can&amp;rsquo;t have the compiler generating code for you; it might
outline things or move things around in ways you don&amp;rsquo;t want. In something like
ASAN mode, it might inject function calls that will completely break the
primitive.&lt;p&gt;This means we muyst write our critical section in assembly. That assembly also
almost unavoidably needs to be part of the boilerplate given above, and it means
it can&amp;rsquo;t participate in ASAN or TSAN instrumentation.&lt;p&gt;In the interest of exposition, we can build a wrapper over this inline assembly
boilerplate that looks something like this:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:8&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-rust highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=kd&gt;let&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;result&lt;/span&gt;: &lt;span class=nb&gt;Result&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;lt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(),&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;RseqAbort&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;rseq&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;!&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=s&gt;r&amp;#34;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=s&gt;    // Assembly for our critical section...
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=s&gt;  &amp;#34;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;// Inline asm constraints.
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;};&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:8&gt;Rust&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;When I wrote the snippet above, I chose numeric labels in the 90s to avoid
potential conflicts with whatever assembly gets pasted here. This is also why I
used a leading &lt;code&gt;_&lt;/code&gt; on the names of some of the assembly constraints; thise are
private to the macro. &lt;code&gt;rseq&lt;/code&gt; isn&amp;rsquo;t, though, since callers will want to access
the CPU id in it.&lt;p&gt;The intent is for the assembly string to be pasted over the
&lt;code&gt;// Do something cool here&lt;/code&gt; comment, and for the constraints to be tacked on
after the boilerplate&amp;rsquo;s constraints.&lt;p&gt;But with that we now have access to the full rseq primitive, in slightly sketchy
macro form. Let&amp;rsquo;s use it to build a CPU-local data structure.&lt;h2 id=a-checkout-desk&gt;&lt;a href=#a-checkout-desk&gt;A Checkout Desk&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;p&gt;Let&amp;rsquo;s say we have a pool of objects that are needed to perform an allocation,
our putative page caches. Let&amp;rsquo;s say we have the following interface:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:9&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-rust highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;impl&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;FreeList&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;unsafe&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;fn&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nf&gt;get_cache&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;amp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=bp&gt;self&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;-&amp;gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;*&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;mut&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;PageCache&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;unsafe&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;fn&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nf&gt;return_cache&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;amp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=bp&gt;self&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;*&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;mut&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;PageCache&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;);&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:9&gt;Rust&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;get_cache()&lt;/code&gt; grabs a cache of pages off the global free list. This requires
taking a lock or traversing a lockless linked list, so it&amp;rsquo;s pretty expensive.
&lt;code&gt;return_cache()&lt;/code&gt; returns a cache back to the global free list for re-use; it is
a similarly expensive operation. Both of these operations are going to be
contended like crazy, so we want to memoize them.&lt;p&gt;To achieve this, we want one slot for every CPU to hold the cache it (or rather,
a thread running on it) most recently acquired, so that it can be reused. These
slots will have &amp;ldquo;checkout desk&amp;rdquo; semantics: if you take a thing, you must put
something in its place, even if it&amp;rsquo;s just a sign that says you took the thing.&lt;figure&gt;&lt;img src=/assets/images/golden-idol.gif alt&gt;&lt;figcaption&gt;&lt;p&gt;Wait for it&amp;mldr;&lt;/figcaption&gt;&lt;/figure&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href=https://fowles.github.io/&gt;Matthew Kulukundis&lt;/a&gt; came up with this idea, and he&amp;rsquo;d
totally put this gif in a slide deck about this data structure.&lt;p&gt;As a function signature, this is what it looks like:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:10&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-rust highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;impl&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;lt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;T&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;PerCpu&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;lt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;T&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;fn&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nf&gt;checkout&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;amp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=bp&gt;self&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;replacement&lt;/span&gt;: &lt;span class=o&gt;*&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;mut&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;T&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;-&amp;gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;*&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;mut&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;T&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:10&gt;Rust&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;We can then use it like this.&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:11&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-rust highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=kd&gt;let&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;free_list&lt;/span&gt;: &lt;span class=kp&gt;&amp;amp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nc&gt;FreeList&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;..&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=kd&gt;let&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;per_cpu&lt;/span&gt;: &lt;span class=kp&gt;&amp;amp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nc&gt;PerCpu&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;lt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;PageCache&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;..&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
