&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;// If this happens, we need to throw away the cache.
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;free_list&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;return_cache&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;cache&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;);&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:11&gt;Rust&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;The semantics of &lt;code&gt;PerCpu&amp;lt;T&gt;&lt;/code&gt; is that it is an array of &lt;code&gt;nprocs&lt;/code&gt; (the number of
logical cores on the system) pointers, all initialized to null. &lt;code&gt;checkout()&lt;/code&gt;
swaps the pointer stored in the current CPU&amp;rsquo;s slot in the &lt;code&gt;PerCpu&amp;lt;T&gt;&lt;/code&gt; with the
replacement argument.&lt;h3 id=building-the-checkout-desk&gt;&lt;a href=#building-the-checkout-desk&gt;Building the Checkout Desk&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;The implementation of this type is relatively simple, but the devil is in the
details. Naively, you&amp;rsquo;d think you literally want an array of pointers:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:12&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-rust highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;pub&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;struct&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nc&gt;PerCpu&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;lt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;T&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;ptrs&lt;/span&gt;: &lt;span class=nb&gt;Box&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;lt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;[&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;*&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;mut&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;T&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;]&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;

&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:12&gt;Rust&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;Unfortunately, this is cache-hostile. We expect that (depending on how &lt;code&gt;ptrs&lt;/code&gt; is
aligned in memory) for eight CPUs&amp;rsquo; checkout pointers to be on the same cache
line. This means eight separate cores are going to be writing to the same cache
line, which is going to result in a lot of cache thrash. This memory wants to be
in L1 cache, but will probably wind up mostly in shared L3 cache.&lt;p&gt;This effect is called &amp;ldquo;false sharing&amp;rdquo;, and is a fundamental part of the design
of modern processors. We have to adjust for this.&lt;p&gt;Instead, we want to give each core a full cache line (64 bytes aligned to a
64-byte boundary) for it to store its pointer in. This sounds super wasteful (56
of those bytes will go unused), but this is the right call for a perf-sensitive
primitive.&lt;p&gt;This amount of memory can add up pretty fast (two whole pages of memory for a
128-core server!), so we&amp;rsquo;ll want to lazilly initialize them. Our cache-friendly
struct will look more like this:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:13&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-rust highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;pub&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;struct&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nc&gt;PerCpu&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;lt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;T&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;

&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;// This struct wraps a T and forces it to take up an entire cache line.
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=cp&gt;#[repr(C, align(64))]&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;struct&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nc&gt;CacheLine&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;lt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;T&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;T&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;);&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;unsafe&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;impl&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;lt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;T&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nb&gt;Send&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;for&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;PerCpu&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;lt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;T&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;{}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;unsafe&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;impl&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;lt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;T&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nb&gt;Sync&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;for&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;PerCpu&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;lt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;T&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;{}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:13&gt;Rust&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;Initializing it requires finding out how many cores there are on the machine.
This is a&amp;mldr; fairly platform-specific affair. Rust &lt;em&gt;does&lt;/em&gt; offer a &amp;ldquo;maximum
paralellism&amp;rdquo; query in its standard library, but it is intended as a hint for how
many worker threads to spawn, as opposed to a hard upper bound on the number of
CPU indices.&lt;p&gt;Instead, we call &lt;code&gt;get_nprocs_conf()&lt;/code&gt;, which is fine since we&amp;rsquo;re already
extremely non-portable already. &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;          &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nb&gt;Err&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;_&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;=&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;break&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;        &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;      &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;    &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:15&gt;Rust&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;This code listing is a lot to take in. It can be broken into two parts: the
restartable sequence itself, and the allocation fallback if the
pointer-to-cache-line happens to be null.&lt;p&gt;The restartable sequence is super short. It looks at the pointer-to-cache-line,
bails if its null (this triggers the later part of the function) and then does
an &lt;code&gt;xchg&lt;/code&gt; between the actual &lt;code&gt;*mut T&lt;/code&gt; in the per-CPU cache line, and the
replacement.&lt;p&gt;If the rseq aborts, we just try again. This is short enough that preemption in
the middle of the rseq is quite rare. Then, if &lt;code&gt;need_alloc&lt;/code&gt; was zeroed, that
means we successfully committed, so we&amp;rsquo;re done.&lt;p&gt;Otherwise we need to allocate a cache line for this CPU. We&amp;rsquo;re now outside of
the rseq, so we&amp;rsquo;re back to needing atomics. Many threads might be racing to be
the thread that initializes the pointer-to-cache-line; we use a basic cas loop
to make sure that we only initialize from null, and if someone beats us to it,
we don&amp;rsquo;t leak the memory we had just allocated. This is an RMW operation, so we
want both acquire and release ordering. Atomics 101!&lt;p&gt;Then, we try again. Odds are good we won&amp;rsquo;t have migrated CPUs when we execute
again, so we won&amp;rsquo;t need to allocate again. Eventually all of the pointers in the
&lt;code&gt;ptrs&lt;/code&gt; array will be non-null, so in the steady state this &lt;code&gt;needs_alloc&lt;/code&gt; case
doesn&amp;rsquo;t need to happen.&lt;h2 id=conclusion&gt;&lt;a href=#conclusion&gt;Conclusion&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;p&gt;This is just a glimpse of what per-CPU concurrent programming looks like. I&amp;rsquo;m
pretty new to it myself, and this post was motivated by building an end-to-end
example in Rust. You can read more about how TCMalloc makes use of restartable
sequences &lt;a href=https://google.github.io/tcmalloc/rseq.html&gt;here&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;div class=footnotes role=doc-endnotes&gt;&lt;hr&gt;&lt;ol&gt;&lt;li id=fn:1&gt;&lt;p&gt;This is annoyingly &lt;em&gt;different&lt;/em&gt; from the function calling convention, which
passes arguments in &lt;code&gt;rdi&lt;/code&gt;, &lt;code&gt;rsi&lt;/code&gt;, &lt;code&gt;rdx&lt;/code&gt;, &lt;code&gt;rcx&lt;/code&gt;, &lt;code&gt;r8&lt;/code&gt;, &lt;code&gt;r9&lt;/code&gt;, with the
mnemonic &amp;ldquo;Diana&amp;rsquo;s silk dress cost $89.&amp;rdquo; I don&amp;rsquo;t know a cute mnemonic for the
syscall registers.&amp;#160;&lt;a href=#fnref:1 class=footnote-backref role=doc-backlink&gt;&amp;#8617;&amp;#xfe0e;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;li id=fn:2&gt;&lt;p&gt;It&amp;rsquo;s actually worse than that. You&amp;rsquo;d think you could do&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:16&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-x86 highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;jmp&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;foo&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=nl&gt;pointers&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;:&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=kt&gt;int&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;foo&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=nl&gt;foo&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;:&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;mov&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;qword&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;ptr&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;[&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;rax&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;],&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;pointers&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:16&gt;x86 Assembly&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;but this makes the resulting code non-position-independent on x86. What this
means is that the code must know at link time what address it will be loaded
at, which breaks the position-independent requirement of many modern
platforms.&lt;p&gt;Indeed, this code will produce a linker error like the following:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:17&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language- highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  = note: /usr/bin/ld: /home/mcyoung/projects/cpulocal/target/debug/deps/cpulocal-a7eeabaf0b1f2c43.2l48u2rfiak1q1ik.rcgu.o:
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;      relocation R_X86_64_32 against `.text._ZN8cpulocal15PerCpu$LT$T$GT$8checkout17h42fde3ce3bd0180aE&amp;#39;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;      can not be used when making a PIE object; recompile with -fPIE
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;      collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:17&gt;Plaintext&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;Not only is &lt;code&gt;.int foo&lt;/code&gt; a problem, but so is referring to &lt;code&gt;pointers&lt;/code&gt;. Instead
we must write&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:18&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-x86 highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;lea&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;rcx&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;qword&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;ptr&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;[&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;pointers&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;+&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;rip&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;]&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;mov&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;qword&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;ptr&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;[&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;rax&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;],&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;rcx&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:18&gt;x86 Assembly&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;to be able to load the address of &lt;code&gt;pointers&lt;/code&gt; at all. This &lt;em&gt;can&lt;/em&gt; be worked
around if you&amp;rsquo;re smart; after all, it is possible to put the addresses of
functions into static variables and not have the linker freak out. It&amp;rsquo;s too
hard to do in inline assembly tho.&amp;#160;&lt;a href=#fnref:2 class=footnote-backref role=doc-backlink&gt;&amp;#8617;&amp;#xfe0e;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;li id=fn:3&gt;&lt;p&gt;Basically this code, which can&amp;rsquo;t be properly-expressed in Rust.&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:19&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-rust highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=kd&gt;let&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;cs&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;CrtiticalSection&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;version&lt;/span&gt;: &lt;span class=mi&gt;0&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;flags&lt;/span&gt;: &lt;span class=mi&gt;0&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;start&lt;/span&gt;: &lt;span class=cm&gt;/* &amp;amp;90f */&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;len&lt;/span&gt;: &lt;span class=cm&gt;/* &amp;amp;91f - &amp;amp;90f */&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;abort&lt;/span&gt;: &lt;span class=cm&gt;/* &amp;amp;92f */&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;};&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:19&gt;Rust&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&amp;#160;&lt;a href=#fnref:3 class=footnote-backref role=doc-backlink&gt;&amp;#8617;&amp;#xfe0e;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/ol&gt;&lt;/div&gt;</content>

  <entry>
    <title>3Hz Computer, Hold the Transistors
</title>
    <link href="/2022/07/24/curta"/>
    <updated>2022-07-24T00:00:00+00:00</updated>
    <id>/2022/07/24/curta</id>
    <content type="html">&lt;p&gt;I&amp;rsquo;m not really one to brag publicly about expensive toys, but a few weeks ago I
managed to get one that&amp;rsquo;s really something special. It is a &lt;em&gt;Curta Type II&lt;/em&gt;, a
mechanical digital&lt;sup id=fnref:1&gt;&lt;a href=#fn:1 class=footnote-ref role=doc-noteref&gt;1&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/sup&gt; calculator manufactured in Liechtenstein
between the 50s and 70s, before solid-state calculators killed them and the
likes of slide-rules.&lt;p&gt;I have wanted one since I was a kid, and I managed to win an eBay auction for
one.&lt;figure&gt;&lt;img src=/assets/images/curta/with_case.jpg alt=&#34;The Curta&#34;&gt;&lt;figcaption&gt;&lt;p&gt;The Curta Type II (and Solomon the cat)&lt;/figcaption&gt;&lt;/figure&gt;&lt;p&gt;It&amp;rsquo;s a funny looking device, somewhere between a peppermill and a scifi grenade.
Mine has serial number 544065, for those keeping score, and comes in a cute
little bakelite pod (which has left hand thread?!).&lt;p&gt;I wanna talk about this thing because unlike something like a slide rule, it
shares many features with modern computers. It has operations, flags, and
registers. Its core primitive is an adder, but many other operations can be
built on top of it: it is very much a platform for complex calculations.&lt;p&gt;I&amp;rsquo;m the sort of person who read &lt;em&gt;Hacker&amp;rsquo;s Delight&lt;/em&gt; for fun, so I really like
simple numerical algorithms. This article is a survey of the operation of a
Curta calculator and algorithms you can implement on it, from the perspective of
a professional assembly programmer.&lt;p&gt;Many of the algorithms I&amp;rsquo;m going to describe here exist online, but I&amp;rsquo;ve found
them to be a bit difficult to wrap my head around, so this article is also
intended as a reference card for myself.&lt;p&gt;Let&amp;rsquo;s dive in!&lt;h2 id=a-well-lubricated-alu&gt;&lt;a href=#a-well-lubricated-alu&gt;A Well-Lubricated ALU&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;p&gt;There are two Curta models, Type I and Type II, which primarily differ in the
sizes of their registers. I have a Type II, so I will focus on the layout of
that one.&lt;p&gt;The Curta is not a &lt;em&gt;stored program&lt;/em&gt; computer like the one you&amp;rsquo;re reading this
article on. An operator needs to manually execute operations. It is as if we
had taken a CPU and pared it down to two of its most basic components:
a register file and an arithmetic logic unit (ALU).&lt;h3 id=the-register-file&gt;&lt;a href=#the-register-file&gt;The Register File&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;The Curta&amp;rsquo;s register file consists of three digital registers, each of which
contains a decimal integer (i.e., each digit is from &lt;code&gt;0&lt;/code&gt; to &lt;code&gt;9&lt;/code&gt;, rather than
&lt;code&gt;0&lt;/code&gt; to &lt;code&gt;1&lt;/code&gt; like on a binary computer):&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;&lt;code&gt;sr&lt;/code&gt;, the &lt;em&gt;setting register&lt;/em&gt;, is located on the side of the device. The
value in &lt;code&gt;sr&lt;/code&gt; can be set manually by the operator using a set of knobs on
the side of the device. The machine will never write to it, only read from
it. It has 11 digits.&lt;li&gt;&lt;code&gt;rr&lt;/code&gt;, the &lt;em&gt;results register&lt;/em&gt;, is located at the top of the device along the
black part of the dial. It is readable and writable by the machine, but not
directly modifiable by the operator. It has 15 digits.&lt;li&gt;&lt;code&gt;cr&lt;/code&gt;, the &lt;em&gt;counting register&lt;/em&gt;, is located next to &lt;code&gt;rr&lt;/code&gt; along the silver part
of the dial. Like &lt;code&gt;rr&lt;/code&gt;, it is only machine-modifiable. It has 8 digits.&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;figure&gt;&lt;img src=/assets/images/curta/sr.jpg alt&gt;&lt;figcaption&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;sr&lt;/code&gt;, set to &lt;code&gt;1997&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;/figcaption&gt;&lt;/figure&gt;&lt;figure&gt;&lt;img src=/assets/images/curta/cr_rr.jpg alt&gt;&lt;figcaption&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;rr&lt;/code&gt; is the black dial; &lt;code&gt;cr&lt;/code&gt; is the silver one.&lt;/figcaption&gt;&lt;/figure&gt;&lt;p&gt;There are also two settings on the device that aren&amp;rsquo;t really registers, but,
since they are changed as part of operation, they are a lot like the control
registers of a modern computer.&lt;p&gt;The &lt;em&gt;carriage&lt;/em&gt; (there isn&amp;rsquo;t an abbreviation for this one, so I&amp;rsquo;ll call it
&lt;code&gt;ca&lt;/code&gt;) is the upper knurled ring on the machine. It can be set to a value
from &lt;code&gt;0&lt;/code&gt; to &lt;code&gt;7&lt;/code&gt;&lt;sup id=fnref:2&gt;&lt;a href=#fn:2 class=footnote-ref role=doc-noteref&gt;2&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/sup&gt;. To set it, the operator lifts the ring up (against
spring tension), twists it, and lets it spring back into the detent for the
chosen value. This is a one-hand motion.&lt;p&gt;There is a small triangle in the middle of the top of the device that points
at which of the digits in &lt;code&gt;cr&lt;/code&gt; will get incremented.&lt;figure&gt;&lt;img src=/assets/images/curta/ca.jpg alt&gt;&lt;figcaption&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;ca&lt;/code&gt; raised and in motion.&lt;/figcaption&gt;&lt;/figure&gt;&lt;p&gt;Finally, &lt;code&gt;rl&lt;/code&gt;, the &lt;em&gt;reversing lever&lt;/em&gt;, is a small switch near the back of the
device that can be in the up or down position. This is like a flag register:
up is cleared, down is set.&lt;figure&gt;&lt;img src=/assets/images/curta/rl.jpg alt&gt;&lt;figcaption&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;rl&lt;/code&gt; in the up position.&lt;/figcaption&gt;&lt;/figure&gt;&lt;h3 id=the-instruction-set&gt;&lt;a href=#the-instruction-set&gt;The Instruction Set&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;We have all this memory, but the meat of a machine is what it can &lt;em&gt;do&lt;/em&gt;. I will
provide an &lt;em&gt;instruction set&lt;/em&gt; for the Curta to aid in giving rigorous
descriptions of operations you can perform with it.&lt;p&gt;The core operation of the Curta is &amp;ldquo;add-with-shift-and-increment&amp;rdquo;. This is a
mouthful. At the very top of the machine is the handle, which is analogous to a
clock signal pin. Every clockwise turn of this handle executes one of these
operations. Internally, this is implemented using a variation on the
&lt;a href=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leibniz_wheel&gt;Leibniz gear&lt;/a&gt;, a common feature of
mechanical calculators.&lt;figure&gt;&lt;img src=/assets/images/curta/pturn.jpg alt&gt;&lt;figcaption&gt;&lt;p&gt;The handle in &amp;ldquo;addition&amp;rdquo; mode.&lt;/figcaption&gt;&lt;/figure&gt;&lt;p&gt;This operation is not that complicated, it just does a lot of stuff.
It takes the value of &lt;code&gt;sr&lt;/code&gt;, left-shifts it (in decimal) by the value in &lt;code&gt;ca&lt;/code&gt;,
and adds it to &lt;code&gt;rr&lt;/code&gt;. Also, it increments &lt;code&gt;CR&lt;/code&gt; by &lt;code&gt;1&lt;/code&gt; shifted by &lt;code&gt;ca&lt;/code&gt;. In other
words:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:1&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-text highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;rr += sr &amp;lt;&amp;lt; ca
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;cr += 1 &amp;lt;&amp;lt; ca
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:1&gt;Plaintext&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;Recall that this is a decimal machine, so &lt;code&gt;&amp;lt;&amp;lt;&lt;/code&gt; is the same as multiplication by
a power of 10, not a power of 2.&lt;p&gt;Addition can overflow, and it wraps around as expected: adding one to
&lt;code&gt;999_999_999_999_999_999&lt;/code&gt; already in &lt;code&gt;rr&lt;/code&gt; will fill it with zeroes.&lt;p&gt;Pulling the handle up reveals a red ring, indicating the machine is in
&lt;em&gt;subtraction mode&lt;/em&gt;. This flips the signs of both the &lt;code&gt;rr&lt;/code&gt; and &lt;code&gt;cr&lt;/code&gt;
modifications:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:2&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-text highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;rr -= sr &amp;lt;&amp;lt; ca
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;cr -= 1 &amp;lt;&amp;lt; ca
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:2&gt;Plaintext&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;figure&gt;&lt;img src=/assets/images/curta/mturn.jpg alt&gt;&lt;figcaption&gt;&lt;p&gt;The handle in &amp;ldquo;subtraction&amp;rdquo; mode.&lt;/figcaption&gt;&lt;/figcaption&gt;&lt;/figure&gt;&lt;p&gt;The Curta cannot handle negative numbers, so it will instead display the ten&amp;rsquo;s
complement&lt;sup id=fnref:3&gt;&lt;a href=#fn:3 class=footnote-ref role=doc-noteref&gt;3&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/sup&gt; of a negative result. For example, subtracting &lt;code&gt;1&lt;/code&gt; from &lt;code&gt;0&lt;/code&gt;
will produce all-nines.&lt;p&gt;You can detect when underflow or overflow occurs when the resulting value is
unexpectedly larger or smaller than the prior value in &lt;code&gt;rr&lt;/code&gt;, respectively.
(This trick is necessary on architectures that lack a carry flags register,
like RISC-V.)&lt;p&gt;Setting &lt;code&gt;rl&lt;/code&gt; will reverse the sign of the operation done on &lt;code&gt;cr&lt;/code&gt; during a
turn of the handle. In addition mode, it will cause &lt;code&gt;cr&lt;/code&gt; to be subtracted from,
while in subtraction mode, it will cause it to be added to. Some complex
algorithms make use of this.&lt;p&gt;Finally, the &lt;em&gt;clearing lever&lt;/em&gt; can be used to clear (to zero) &lt;code&gt;sr&lt;/code&gt; or &lt;code&gt;rr&lt;/code&gt;,
independently. It is a small ring-shaped lever that, while the carriage is
raised, can be wiped past digits to clear them. Registers cannot be partially&lt;figure&gt;&lt;img src=/assets/images/curta/pturn.jpg alt&gt;&lt;figcaption&gt;&lt;p&gt;The clearing lever.&lt;/figcaption&gt;&lt;/figure&gt;&lt;h3 id=notation&gt;&lt;a href=#notation&gt;Notation&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;Let&amp;rsquo;s give names to all the instructions the operator needs to follow,
so we can write some assembly:&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;&lt;code&gt;mr&lt;/code&gt;, or &lt;em&gt;Machine Ready!&lt;/em&gt;, means to clear/zero every register. All Curta
instructions use the term &amp;ldquo;Machine Ready&amp;rdquo; to indicate the beginning of a
calculation session.&lt;li&gt;&lt;code&gt;pturn&lt;/code&gt; is the core addition operation, a &amp;ldquo;plus turn&amp;rdquo;.&lt;li&gt;&lt;code&gt;mturn&lt;/code&gt; is its subtraction twin, a &amp;ldquo;minus turn&amp;rdquo;.&lt;li&gt;&lt;code&gt;set &amp;lt;flag&gt;&lt;/code&gt; requests the operator set one of &lt;code&gt;rl&lt;/code&gt; or &lt;code&gt;sm&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;li&gt;&lt;code&gt;clr &amp;lt;flag&gt;&lt;/code&gt; is the opposite of &lt;code&gt;set&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;li&gt;&lt;code&gt;zero &amp;lt;reg&gt;&lt;/code&gt; request a clear of one of &lt;code&gt;rr&lt;/code&gt; or &lt;code&gt;cr&lt;/code&gt; using the clearing
lever.&lt;li&gt;&lt;code&gt;add &amp;lt;reg&gt;, &amp;lt;imm&gt;&lt;/code&gt; requests manual addition of an immediate to &lt;code&gt;sr&lt;/code&gt; or &lt;code&gt;ca&lt;/code&gt;.
This is limited by what mental math we can ask of the operator.&lt;li&gt;&lt;code&gt;copy &amp;lt;reg&gt;, sr&lt;/code&gt; requests a copy of the value in &lt;code&gt;rr&lt;/code&gt; or &lt;code&gt;cr&lt;/code&gt; to &lt;code&gt;sr&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;li&gt;&lt;code&gt;wrnp &amp;lt;reg&gt;, &amp;lt;symbol&gt;&lt;/code&gt; indicates we need to write down a value in any
register to a handy notepad (hence &lt;code&gt;wr&lt;/code&gt;ite &lt;code&gt;n&lt;/code&gt;ote&lt;code&gt;p&lt;/code&gt;ad), marked with
&lt;code&gt;&amp;lt;symbol&gt;&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;li&gt;&lt;code&gt;rdnp &amp;lt;reg&gt;, &amp;lt;symbol&gt;&lt;/code&gt; asks the operator to &lt;code&gt;re&lt;/code&gt;ad a value recorded with
&lt;code&gt;wrnp&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;li&gt;&lt;code&gt;if &amp;lt;cond&gt;, &amp;lt;label&gt;&lt;/code&gt; asks the operator to check a condition (in terms of
&lt;code&gt;cr&lt;/code&gt;, &lt;code&gt;rr&lt;/code&gt;, and &lt;code&gt;sr&lt;/code&gt;) and, if true, proceed to the instruction at the given
&lt;code&gt;label:&lt;/code&gt;. Here&amp;rsquo;s some examples of conditions we&amp;rsquo;ll use:&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;&lt;code&gt;rr == 42&lt;/code&gt;, i.e., &lt;code&gt;rr&lt;/code&gt; equals some constant value.&lt;li&gt;&lt;code&gt;rr.ovflow&lt;/code&gt;, i.e., &lt;code&gt;rr&lt;/code&gt; overflowed/underflowed due to the
most recent &lt;code&gt;pturn&lt;/code&gt;/&lt;code&gt;mturn&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;li&gt;&lt;code&gt;cr[1] == 9&lt;/code&gt;, i.e. &lt;code&gt;cr&lt;/code&gt;&amp;rsquo;s second digit (zero-indexed, not like the
physical device!) equals &lt;code&gt;9&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;li&gt;&lt;code&gt;cr[0..ca] &amp;lt; sr[0..ca]&lt;/code&gt;, i.e., &lt;code&gt;cr&lt;/code&gt;, considering only the digits up to
the setting of &lt;code&gt;ca&lt;/code&gt;, is less than those same digits in &lt;code&gt;sr&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;&lt;code&gt;goto &amp;lt;label&gt;&lt;/code&gt; is like &lt;code&gt;if&lt;/code&gt; without a condition.&lt;li&gt;&lt;code&gt;done&lt;/code&gt; means we&amp;rsquo;re done and the result can be read off of &lt;code&gt;rr&lt;/code&gt; (or &lt;code&gt;cr&lt;/code&gt;).&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;p&gt;Note that there is a lot of mental math in some of the conditions. Algorithms on
the Curta are aimed to minimize what work the operator needs to do to compute a
result, but remember that it is only an ALU: all of the control flow logic needs
to be provided by the human operator.&lt;p&gt;None of this is real code, and it is specifically for the benefit of readers.&lt;h2 id=some-algorithms&gt;&lt;a href=#some-algorithms&gt;Some Algorithms&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;p&gt;So, addition and subtraction are easy, because there are hardware instructions
for those. There is, however, no direct way to do multiplication or division.
Let&amp;rsquo;s take a look at some of our options.&lt;p&gt;Given that a Curta is kinda expensive, you can try out an online simulator if
you want to follow along. &lt;a href=https://www.cailliau.org/en/Alphabetical/C/Computing/Curta/Simulator/&gt;This one&lt;/a&gt;
is pretty simple and runs in your browser.&lt;h3 id=multiplication&gt;&lt;a href=#multiplication&gt;Multiplication&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;The easiest way to do multiplication is by repeated addition; &lt;code&gt;cr&lt;/code&gt; helps us
check our work.&lt;p&gt;Given a value like &lt;code&gt;8364&lt;/code&gt;, we can multiply it by &lt;code&gt;5&lt;/code&gt; like so:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:3&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-curta highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=nl&gt;mul_by_5&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;:&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;mr&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;add&lt;/span&gt;   &lt;span class=n&gt;sr&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=mi&gt;8364&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=nl&gt;loop&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;:&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;    &lt;span class=k&gt;if&lt;/span&gt;    &lt;span class=n&gt;cr&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;==&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=mi&gt;5&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;end&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;    &lt;span class=n&gt;pturn&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;    &lt;span class=k&gt;goto&lt;/span&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;loop&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=nl&gt;end&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;:&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;done&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:3&gt;Curta &#34;Assembly&#34;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;Here, we input the larger factor into &lt;code&gt;sr&lt;/code&gt;, and then keep turning until &lt;code&gt;cr&lt;/code&gt;
contains the other factor. The result is &lt;code&gt;41820&lt;/code&gt;:&lt;figure&gt;&lt;img src=/assets/images/curta/mul.jpg alt&gt;&lt;figcaption&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;8364 * 5 == 41820&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/figcaption&gt;&lt;/figure&gt;&lt;p&gt;Of course, this does not work well for complex products, such as squaring
&lt;code&gt;41820&lt;/code&gt;. You could sit there and turn the handle forty thousand times if you
wanted to, or you might decided that you should get a better hobby, since modern
silicon can do this in nanoseconds.&lt;p&gt;We can speed this up exponentially by making use of the distributive property
and the fact that &lt;code&gt;turn&lt;/code&gt; can incorporate multiplication by a power of &lt;code&gt;10&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;p&gt;Consider:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:4&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language- highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;41820 * 41820
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;= 41820 * (40000 + 1000 + 800 + 20)
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;= 41820 * 40000 + 41820 * 1000 + 41820 * 800 + 41820 * 20
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:4&gt;Plaintext&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;Each nice round number here can be achieved in &lt;code&gt;cr&lt;/code&gt; by use of &lt;code&gt;ca&lt;/code&gt;. Our
algorithm will look a bit like this:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:5&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-curta highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=nl&gt;square&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;:&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;mr&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;add&lt;/span&gt;   &lt;span class=n&gt;sr&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=mi&gt;41820&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=nl&gt;loop&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;:&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;    &lt;span class=c1&gt;// Check if we&amp;#39;re done.
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;    &lt;span class=k&gt;if&lt;/span&gt;    &lt;span class=n&gt;cr&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;==&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=mi&gt;41820&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;end&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=nl&gt;inner&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;:&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;      &lt;span class=c1&gt;// Turn until the first `ca` digits of `cr` and the
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;      &lt;span class=c1&gt;// other factor match.
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;      &lt;span class=k&gt;if&lt;/span&gt;    &lt;span class=n&gt;cr&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;[&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mf&gt;1.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;ca&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;]&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;==&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=mi&gt;41802&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;[&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mf&gt;1.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;ca&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;],&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;inner_end&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;      &lt;span class=n&gt;pturn&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;      &lt;span class=k&gt;goto&lt;/span&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;inner&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=nl&gt;inner_end&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;:&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;    &lt;span class=c1&gt;// Increment `ca` and repeat until done.
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;    &lt;span class=n&gt;add&lt;/span&gt;   &lt;span class=n&gt;ca&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=mi&gt;1&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;    &lt;span class=k&gt;goto&lt;/span&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;loop&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=nl&gt;end&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;:&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;done&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:5&gt;Curta &#34;Assembly&#34;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;There are two loops. The inner loop runs as many turns as is necessary to get
the next prefix of the factor into &lt;code&gt;cr&lt;/code&gt;, then incrementing &lt;code&gt;ca&lt;/code&gt; to do the next
digit, and on and on until &lt;code&gt;cr&lt;/code&gt; contains the entire other factor, at which point
we can read off the result.&lt;p&gt;The actual trace of operations (omitting control flow), and the resulting
contents of the registers &lt;code&gt;sr/rr/mr/ca&lt;/code&gt; at each step, looks something like
this:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:6&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-curta highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;mr&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;// 00000000000/000000000000000/00000000/0
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;add&lt;/span&gt;   &lt;span class=n&gt;sr&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=mi&gt;41820&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;// 00000041820/000000000000000/00000000/0
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;add&lt;/span&gt;   &lt;span class=n&gt;ca&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=mi&gt;1&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;// 00000041820/000000000000000/00000000/1
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;pturn&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;// 00000041820/000000000418200/00000010/1

&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;// 00000041820/000000000083640/00000020/2

&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;pturn&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;// 00000041820/000000009200400/00000220/2
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;pturn&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;// 00000041820/000000013382400/00000320/2
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;pturn&lt;/span&gt;

&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;// 00000041820/000001330712400/00031820/4
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;pturn&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;// 00000041820/000001748912400/00041820/4
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;pturn&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:6&gt;Curta &#34;Assembly&#34;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;The result can be read off from &lt;code&gt;rr&lt;/code&gt;: &lt;code&gt;1748912400&lt;/code&gt;. In the trace, you can see
&lt;code&gt;cr&lt;/code&gt; get built up digit by digit, making this operation rather efficient.&lt;figure&gt;&lt;img src=/assets/images/curta/square.jpg alt&gt;&lt;figcaption&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;41820 * 41820 == 1748912400&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/figcaption&gt;&lt;/figure&gt;&lt;p&gt;We can do even better, if we use subtraction. For example, note that
&lt;code&gt;18 = 20 - 2&lt;/code&gt;; we can build up &lt;code&gt;18&lt;/code&gt; in &lt;code&gt;cr&lt;/code&gt; by doing only 4 turns rather than
nine, according to this formula. Here&amp;rsquo;s the general algorithm for &lt;code&gt;n * m&lt;/code&gt;:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:7&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-curta highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=nl&gt;mul&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;:&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;mr&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;add&lt;/span&gt;   &lt;span class=n&gt;sr&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;n&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=nl&gt;loop&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;:&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;    &lt;span class=k&gt;if&lt;/span&gt;    &lt;span class=n&gt;cr&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;==&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;m&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;end&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;    &lt;span class=c1&gt;// Same as before, but if the next digit is large,
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;    &lt;span class=c1&gt;// go into subtraction mode.
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;    &lt;span class=k&gt;if&lt;/span&gt;    &lt;span class=n&gt;m&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;[&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;ca&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;]&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=mi&gt;5&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;by_sub&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=nl&gt;inner&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;:&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;      &lt;span class=k&gt;if&lt;/span&gt;    &lt;span class=n&gt;cr&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;[&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mf&gt;0.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;ca&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;]&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;==&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;m&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;[&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mf&gt;0.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;ca&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;],&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;inner_end&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;      &lt;span class=n&gt;pturn&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;      &lt;span class=k&gt;goto&lt;/span&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;inner&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=nl&gt;by_sub&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;:&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;    &lt;span class=c1&gt;// Store the current `ca` position.
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;    &lt;span class=n&gt;wrnp&lt;/span&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;ca&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;   &lt;span class=n&gt;sub_from&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;    &lt;span class=c1&gt;// Find the next small digit (eg. imagine n * 199, we
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;    &lt;span class=c1&gt;// want to find the 1).
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;  &lt;span class=nl&gt;find_small&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;:&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;    &lt;span class=n&gt;add&lt;/span&gt;   &lt;span class=n&gt;ca&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;   &lt;span class=mi&gt;1&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;    &lt;span class=k&gt;if&lt;/span&gt;    &lt;span class=n&gt;m&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;[&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;ca&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;]&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=mi&gt;5&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;find_small&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;    &lt;span class=c1&gt;// Set the digit to one plus the desired value for that
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;    &lt;span class=c1&gt;// digit.
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;  &lt;span class=nl&gt;outer_turns&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;:&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;    &lt;span class=n&gt;pturn&lt;/span&gt;

&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;    &lt;span class=n&gt;wrnp&lt;/span&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;ca&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;   &lt;span class=n&gt;continue_from&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;    &lt;span class=c1&gt;// Go back to the original `ca` position and enter
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;    &lt;span class=c1&gt;// subtraction mode.
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;    &lt;span class=n&gt;rdnp&lt;/span&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;ca&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;   &lt;span class=n&gt;sub_from&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=nl&gt;subs&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;:&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=nl&gt;subs_inner&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;:&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;      &lt;span class=c1&gt;// Perform subtractions until we get the value we want.
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;      &lt;span class=k&gt;if&lt;/span&gt;    &lt;span class=n&gt;cr&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;[&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;ca&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;]&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;==&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;m&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;[&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;ca&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;],&lt;/span&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;subs_end&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;      &lt;span class=n&gt;mturn&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;      &lt;span class=k&gt;goto&lt;/span&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;subs_inner&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=nl&gt;subs_end&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;:&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;    &lt;span class=c1&gt;// Advance `ca` and keep going until we&amp;#39;re done.
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;    &lt;span class=n&gt;add&lt;/span&gt;   &lt;span class=n&gt;ca&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;   &lt;span class=mi&gt;1&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;    &lt;span class=k&gt;if&lt;/span&gt;    &lt;span class=n&gt;ca&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;!=&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;continue_from&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;subs&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;    &lt;span class=k&gt;goto&lt;/span&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;loop&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=nl&gt;inner_end&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;:&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;    &lt;span class=n&gt;add&lt;/span&gt;   &lt;span class=n&gt;ca&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;   &lt;span class=mi&gt;1&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;    &lt;span class=k&gt;goto&lt;/span&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;loop&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=nl&gt;end&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;:&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;done&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:7&gt;Curta &#34;Assembly&#34;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;Although more complicated, if we execute it step by step, we&amp;rsquo;ll see we get to
our answer in fewer turns:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:8&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-curta highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;mr&lt;/span&gt;

&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;// 00000041820/000001330712400/00031820/4
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;pturn&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;// 00000041820/000001748912400/00041820/4
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;pturn&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:8&gt;Curta &#34;Assembly&#34;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;In exchange for a little overhead, the number of turns drops from 15 to 10.
This is the fastest &lt;em&gt;general&lt;/em&gt; algorithm, but some techniques from &lt;em&gt;Hacker&amp;rsquo;s
Delight&lt;/em&gt; can likely be applied here to make it faster for some products.&lt;h4 id=cubes&gt;&lt;a href=#cubes&gt;Cubes&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h4&gt;&lt;p&gt;As a quick note, computing the cube of a number without taking extra notes is
easy, so long as the number is already written down somewhere you can already
see it. After computing &lt;code&gt;n^2&lt;/code&gt; by any of the methods above, we can do&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:9&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-curta highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=nl&gt;cube&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;:&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;mr&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;add&lt;/span&gt;   &lt;span class=n&gt;sr&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;   &lt;span class=n&gt;n&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=c1&gt;// Perform a multiplication by `n`, then copy the result
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;  &lt;span class=c1&gt;// into `sr`.
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;copy&lt;/span&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;sr&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;   &lt;span class=n&gt;rr&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;zero&lt;/span&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;rr&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;zero&lt;/span&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;cr&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=c1&gt;// Perform another multiplication by `n`, but now with
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;  &lt;span class=c1&gt;// its square in `sr`.
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;done&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:9&gt;Curta &#34;Assembly&#34;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;This sequence can be repeated over and over to produce higher powers, and is
only limited by the size of &lt;code&gt;rr&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;h3 id=division&gt;&lt;a href=#division&gt;Division&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;Division is way more interesting, because it can be &lt;em&gt;inexact&lt;/em&gt;, and thus produces
a &lt;em&gt;remainder&lt;/em&gt; in addition to the quotient. There are a few different algorithms,
but the simplest one is division by repeated subtraction. Some literature
calls this &amp;ldquo;division by breaking down&amp;rdquo;.&lt;p&gt;For small numbers, this is quite simple, such as &lt;code&gt;21 / 4&lt;/code&gt;:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:10&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-curta highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=nl&gt;div_by_4&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;:&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;mr&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;add&lt;/span&gt;   &lt;span class=n&gt;sr&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;   &lt;span class=mi&gt;21&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;pturn&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;zero&lt;/span&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;cr&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;zero&lt;/span&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;sr&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;add&lt;/span&gt;   &lt;span class=n&gt;sr&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;   &lt;span class=mi&gt;4&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;set&lt;/span&gt;   &lt;span class=n&gt;rl&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=nl&gt;loop&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;:&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;    &lt;span class=k&gt;if&lt;/span&gt;    &lt;span class=n&gt;rr&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;oflow&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;end&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;    &lt;span class=n&gt;mturn&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;    &lt;span class=k&gt;goto&lt;/span&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;loop&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=nl&gt;end&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;:&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;pturn&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;done&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:10&gt;Curta &#34;Assembly&#34;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;This works by first getting the dividend into &lt;code&gt;rr&lt;/code&gt; and resetting the rest of
the machine. Then, with &lt;code&gt;rl&lt;/code&gt; set, we subtract the divisor from &lt;code&gt;rr&lt;/code&gt; until we
get overflow, at which point we add to undo the overflow. The quotient will
appear in &lt;code&gt;cr&lt;/code&gt;: we set &lt;code&gt;rl&lt;/code&gt;, so each subtraction &lt;em&gt;increments&lt;/em&gt; &lt;code&gt;cr&lt;/code&gt;, giving us
a count of &lt;code&gt;mturn&lt;/code&gt;s executed. The remainder appears in &lt;code&gt;rr&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;p&gt;In this case, we get down to &lt;code&gt;1&lt;/code&gt; before the next &lt;code&gt;mturn&lt;/code&gt; underflows; the result
of that underflow is to &lt;code&gt;99...97&lt;/code&gt;, the ten&amp;rsquo;s complement of -3. We then undo the
last operation by &lt;code&gt;pturn&lt;/code&gt;ing, getting &lt;code&gt;5&lt;/code&gt; in &lt;code&gt;cr&lt;/code&gt;: this is our quotient. &lt;code&gt;1&lt;/code&gt; in
&lt;code&gt;rr&lt;/code&gt; is the remainder.&lt;p&gt;The same tricks from earlier work here, using &lt;code&gt;ca&lt;/code&gt; to make less work,
effectively implementing decimal long division of &lt;code&gt;n/m&lt;/code&gt;:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:11&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-curta highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=nl&gt;div&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;:&lt;/span&gt;

&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;add&lt;/span&gt;   &lt;span class=n&gt;sr&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;   &lt;span class=n&gt;n&lt;/span&gt;

&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;add&lt;/span&gt;   &lt;span class=n&gt;ca&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;   &lt;span class=n&gt;log&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;m&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;-&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;log&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;n&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;+&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=mi&gt;1&lt;/span&gt;

which is a ton of work. At the end, we get a quotient of &lt;code&gt;22931333&lt;/code&gt; and
reminder &lt;code&gt;32&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;figure&gt;&lt;img src=/assets/images/curta/quot.jpg alt&gt;&lt;figcaption&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;3141592653 / 137 == 22931333, rem 32&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/figcaption&gt;&lt;/figure&gt;&lt;p&gt;Unfortunately, we can&amp;rsquo;t as easily &amp;ldquo;cheat&amp;rdquo; with subtraction as we did with
multiplication, because we don&amp;rsquo;t know the value that needs to appear in &lt;code&gt;cr&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;h3 id=square-roots&gt;&lt;a href=#square-roots&gt;Square Roots&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;Computing square roots by approximation is one of the premiere operations on
the Curta. There&amp;rsquo;s a number of approaches. Newton&amp;rsquo;s method is the classic, but
requires a prior approximation, access to lookup tables, or a lot of
multiplication.&lt;p&gt;A slower, but much more mechanical approach is to use &lt;em&gt;Töpler&amp;rsquo;s method&lt;/em&gt;. This
consists of observing that the sum of the first &lt;code&gt;n&lt;/code&gt; odd numbers is the square of
&lt;code&gt;n&lt;/code&gt;. Thus, we can use an approach similar to that for division, only that we
now subtract off consecutive odd numbers. Let&amp;rsquo;s take the square root of &lt;code&gt;92&lt;/code&gt;:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:13&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-curta highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=nl&gt;sqrt_of_92&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;:&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;mr&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;add&lt;/span&gt;   &lt;span class=n&gt;sr&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;   &lt;span class=mi&gt;92&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;pturn&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;zero&lt;/span&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;cr&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;zero&lt;/span&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;sr&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;add&lt;/span&gt;   &lt;span class=n&gt;sr&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;   &lt;span class=mi&gt;1&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;set&lt;/span&gt;   &lt;span class=n&gt;rl&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=nl&gt;loop&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;:&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;mturn&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=k&gt;if&lt;/span&gt;    &lt;span class=n&gt;rr&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;ovflow&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;end&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;add&lt;/span&gt;   &lt;span class=n&gt;sr&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=k&gt;goto&lt;/span&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;loop&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=nl&gt;end&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;:&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;pturn&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;done&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:13&gt;Curta &#34;Assembly&#34;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;We get &lt;code&gt;9&lt;/code&gt; as our result, but that&amp;rsquo;s pretty awful precision. We can improve
precision by multiplying &lt;code&gt;92&lt;/code&gt; by a large, even power of ten, and then dividing
the result by that power of ten&amp;rsquo;s square root (half the zeroes).&lt;p&gt;Unfortunately, this runs into the same problem as naive multiplication: we have
to turn the handle &lt;em&gt;a lot&lt;/em&gt;. Turning this algorithm into something that can be
done exponentially faster is a bit fussier.&lt;p&gt;One approach (which I found on &amp;lt;curta.org&gt;) allows us to compute the root
by shifting. Several programmers appear to have independently discovered this in
the 70s or 80s.&lt;p&gt;It is based on the so-called
&lt;a href=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Methods_of_computing_square_roots#Digit-by-digit_calculation&gt;&amp;ldquo;digit-by-digit&amp;rdquo;&lt;/a&gt;
algorithm, dating back to at least the time of Napier. Wikipedia provides a
good explanation of why this method works. However, I have not been able to
write down a proof that this specific version works, since it incorporates
borrowing to compute intermediate terms with successive odd numbers in a fairly
subtle way. I would really appreciate a proof, if anyone knows of one!&lt;p&gt;The algorithm is thus, for a radicand &lt;code&gt;n&lt;/code&gt;:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:14&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-curta highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=nl&gt;sqrt&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;:&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;mr&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=c1&gt;// Put `ca` as far as it will go, and then enter
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;  &lt;span class=c1&gt;// the radicand as far right as it will go, so you
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;  &lt;span class=c1&gt;// get as many digits as possible to work with.
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;add&lt;/span&gt;   &lt;span class=n&gt;ca&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;   &lt;span class=mi&gt;8&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;add&lt;/span&gt;   &lt;span class=n&gt;sr&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;   &lt;span class=n&gt;n&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;lt;&amp;lt;&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mi&gt;8&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;-&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;log&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;n&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;))&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;pturn&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;zero&lt;/span&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;cr&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;zero&lt;/span&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;sr&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=c1&gt;// Put a 1 under the leftmost pair of digits. This
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;  &lt;span class=c1&gt;// assumes a number with an even number of digits.
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;add&lt;/span&gt;   &lt;span class=n&gt;sr&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;   &lt;span class=mi&gt;1&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;lt;&amp;lt;&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;ca&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;-&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=mi&gt;1&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;set&lt;/span&gt;   &lt;span class=n&gt;rl&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=nl&gt;loop&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;:&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;  &lt;span class=nl&gt;sqrt_loop&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;:&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;      &lt;span class=c1&gt;// Add an odd number (with a bunch of zeros
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;      &lt;span class=c1&gt;// after it.)
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;      &lt;span class=n&gt;mturn&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;      &lt;span class=k&gt;if&lt;/span&gt;    &lt;span class=n&gt;rr&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;ovflow&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;  &lt;span class=n&gt;sqrt_end&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;      &lt;span class=c1&gt;// Increment sr by 2 (again, with a bunch of

&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;    &lt;span class=c1&gt;// If `ca` is all the way to the right, we&amp;#39;re out of

&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;    &lt;span class=k&gt;if&lt;/span&gt;    &lt;span class=n&gt;ca&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;==&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=mi&gt;1&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;||&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;rr&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;==&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=mi&gt;0&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=n&gt;end&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;    &lt;span class=c1&gt;// Subtract ONE from the digit in `sr` we were
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;    &lt;span class=c1&gt;// incrementing in the loop. This results in an even
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;    &lt;span class=c1&gt;// number.
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;    &lt;span class=n&gt;add&lt;/span&gt;   &lt;span class=n&gt;sr&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;   &lt;span class=o&gt;-&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mi&gt;1&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;lt;&amp;lt;&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;ca&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;-&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=mi&gt;1&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;))&lt;/span&gt;

&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;add&lt;/span&gt;   &lt;span class=n&gt;ca&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;   &lt;span class=o&gt;-&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=mi&gt;1&lt;/span&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;// 00028000000/004000000000000/14000000/5
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;// More of the same...
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:15&gt;Curta &#34;Assembly&#34;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;Over time, the digits &lt;code&gt;14121356&lt;/code&gt; will appear in &lt;code&gt;cr&lt;/code&gt;. This is the square root
(although we do need to place the decimal point; the number of digits before it
will be half of what we started with, rounded up).&lt;figure&gt;&lt;img src=/assets/images/curta/sqrt.jpg alt&gt;&lt;figcaption&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;sqrt(2) ~ 1.4121356&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/figcaption&gt;&lt;/figure&gt;&lt;h2 id=wrap-up&gt;&lt;a href=#wrap-up&gt;Wrap-up&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;p&gt;There&amp;rsquo;s a quite a few other algorithms out there, but most of them boil down to
clever use of lookup tables and combinations of the above techniques. For
example, the so-called &amp;ldquo;rule of 3&amp;rdquo; is simply performing a multiplication to get
a product into &lt;code&gt;rr&lt;/code&gt;, and then using it as the dividend to produce a quotient
of the form &lt;code&gt;a * b / c&lt;/code&gt; in &lt;code&gt;cr&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;p&gt;I hope that these simple numeric algorithms, presented in a style resembling
assembly, helps illustrate that programming at such a low level is not &lt;em&gt;hard&lt;/em&gt;,
but merely requires learning a different bag of tricks.&lt;div class=footnotes role=doc-endnotes&gt;&lt;hr&gt;&lt;ol&gt;&lt;li id=fn:1&gt;&lt;p&gt;Although this seems like an oxymoron, it is accurate! The Curta contains no
electrical or electronic components, and its registers contain discrete
symbols, not continuous values. It is &lt;em&gt;not&lt;/em&gt; an analog computer!&amp;#160;&lt;a href=#fnref:1 class=footnote-backref role=doc-backlink&gt;&amp;#8617;&amp;#xfe0e;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;li id=fn:2&gt;&lt;p&gt;The Curta is a one-indexed machine, insofar as the values engraved on &lt;code&gt;ca&lt;/code&gt;
are not &lt;code&gt;0&lt;/code&gt; to &lt;code&gt;7&lt;/code&gt; but &lt;code&gt;1&lt;/code&gt; to &lt;code&gt;8&lt;/code&gt;. However, as we all know, zero-indexing
is far more convenient. Any place where I say &amp;ldquo;set &lt;code&gt;ca&lt;/code&gt; to &lt;code&gt;n&lt;/code&gt;&amp;rdquo;, I mean the
&lt;code&gt;n + 1&lt;/code&gt;th detent.&lt;p&gt;Doing this avoids a lot of otherwise unnecessary &lt;code&gt;-1&lt;/code&gt;s in the prose.&amp;#160;&lt;a href=#fnref:2 class=footnote-backref role=doc-backlink&gt;&amp;#8617;&amp;#xfe0e;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;li id=fn:3&gt;&lt;p&gt;The &lt;em&gt;ten&amp;rsquo;s complement&lt;/em&gt; of a number &lt;code&gt;x&lt;/code&gt; is analogous to the two&amp;rsquo;s complement
(i.e., the value of &lt;code&gt;-x&lt;/code&gt; when viewed as an unsigned integer on a binary
machine). It is equal to &lt;code&gt;MAX_VALUE - x + 1&lt;/code&gt;, where &lt;code&gt;MAX_VALUE&lt;/code&gt; is the
largest value that &lt;code&gt;x&lt;/code&gt; could be. For example, this is
&lt;code&gt;999_999_999_999_999_999&lt;/code&gt; (fifteen nines) for &lt;code&gt;rr&lt;/code&gt;.&amp;#160;&lt;a href=#fnref:3 class=footnote-backref role=doc-backlink&gt;&amp;#8617;&amp;#xfe0e;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/ol&gt;&lt;/div&gt;</content>
