&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=kd&gt;let&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;boxed&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;make_box&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;copy&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;y&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;));&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;// Copy onto the heap.
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:20&gt;Rust&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;We can could (modulo orphan rules) even implement &lt;code&gt;CopyCtor&lt;/code&gt; for Rust types
that implement &lt;code&gt;Clone&lt;/code&gt; by &lt;code&gt;clone&lt;/code&gt;ing into the destination.&lt;p&gt;It should be straightforward to make a version for move construction&amp;mldr; but,
what&amp;rsquo;s a &lt;code&gt;T&amp;&amp;&lt;/code&gt; in Rust?&lt;h2 id=interlude-ii-unique-ownership&gt;&lt;a href=#interlude-ii-unique-ownership&gt;Interlude II: Unique Ownership&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;Box&amp;lt;T&gt;&lt;/code&gt; is interesting, because unlike &lt;code&gt;&amp;amp;T&lt;/code&gt;, it is possible to &lt;em&gt;move out&lt;/em&gt; of a
&lt;code&gt;Box&amp;lt;T&gt;&lt;/code&gt;, since the compiler treats it somewhat magically. There has long been
a desire to introduce a &lt;code&gt;DerefMove&lt;/code&gt; trait captures this behavior, but the
difficulty is the signature: if &lt;code&gt;deref&lt;/code&gt; returns &lt;code&gt;&amp;amp;T&lt;/code&gt;, and &lt;code&gt;deref_mut&lt;/code&gt; returns
&lt;code&gt;&amp;amp;mut T&lt;/code&gt;, should &lt;code&gt;deref_move&lt;/code&gt; return &lt;code&gt;T&lt;/code&gt;? Or something&amp;mldr; more exotic? You
might not want to dump the value onto the stack; you want &lt;code&gt;*x = *y&lt;/code&gt; to not
trigger an expensive intermediate copy, when &lt;code&gt;*y: [u8; BIG]&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;p&gt;Usually, the &amp;ldquo;something more exotic&amp;rdquo; is a &lt;code&gt;&amp;amp;move T&lt;/code&gt; or &lt;code&gt;&amp;amp;own T&lt;/code&gt; reference that
&amp;ldquo;owns&amp;rdquo; the pointee, similar to how a &lt;code&gt;T&amp;&amp;&lt;/code&gt; in C++ is taken to mean that the
caller wishes to perform ownership transfer.&lt;p&gt;Exotic language features aside, we&amp;rsquo;d like to be able to implement something like
&lt;code&gt;DerefMove&lt;/code&gt; for move constructors, since this is the natural analogue of &lt;code&gt;T&amp;&amp;&lt;/code&gt;.
To move out of storage, we need a smart pointer to provide us with three things:&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;It must actually be a smart pointer (duh).&lt;li&gt;It must be possible to destroy the storage without running the destructor of
the pointee (in Rust, unlike in C++, destructors do not run on moved-from
objects).&lt;li&gt;It must be the &lt;em&gt;unique owner&lt;/em&gt; of the pointee. Formally, if, when &lt;code&gt;p&lt;/code&gt; goes out
of scope, no thread can access &lt;code&gt;*p&lt;/code&gt;, then &lt;code&gt;p&lt;/code&gt; is the unique owner.&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;Box&amp;lt;T&gt;&lt;/code&gt; trivially satisfies all three of these: it&amp;rsquo;s a smart pointer, we can
destroy the storage using &lt;code&gt;std::alloc::dealloc&lt;/code&gt;, and it satisfies the unique
ownership property.&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;&amp;amp;mut T&lt;/code&gt; fails both tests: we don&amp;rsquo;t know how to destory the storage (this is one
of the difficulties with a theoretical &lt;code&gt;&amp;amp;move T&lt;/code&gt;) and it is not the unique
owner: some &lt;code&gt;&amp;amp;mut T&lt;/code&gt; might outlive it.&lt;p&gt;Interestingly, &lt;code&gt;Arc&amp;lt;T&gt;&lt;/code&gt; only fails the unique ownership test, and it can pass
it dynamically, if we observe the strong and weak counts to both be 1. This
is also true for &lt;code&gt;Rc&amp;lt;T&gt;&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;p&gt;Most importantly, however, is that if &lt;code&gt;Pin&amp;lt;P&gt;&lt;/code&gt;, then it is sufficient that &lt;code&gt;P&lt;/code&gt;
satisfy these conditions. After all, a &lt;code&gt;Pin&amp;lt;Box&amp;lt;P&gt;&gt;&lt;/code&gt; uniquely owns its contents,
even if they can&amp;rsquo;t be moved.&lt;p&gt;It&amp;rsquo;s useful to introduce some traits that record these requirements:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:21&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-rust highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;unsafe&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;trait&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;OuterDrop&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;unsafe&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;fn&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nf&gt;outer_drop&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;this&lt;/span&gt;: &lt;span class=o&gt;*&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;mut&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=bp&gt;Self&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;);&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;unsafe&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;trait&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;DerefMove&lt;/span&gt;: &lt;span class=nc&gt;DerefMut&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;OuterDrop&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;{}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:21&gt;Rust&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;OuterDrop&lt;/code&gt; is simply the &amp;ldquo;outer storage destruction&amp;rdquo; operation. Naturally, it
is only safe to perform this operation when the pointee&amp;rsquo;s own destructor has
been separately dropped (there are some subtleties around leaking memory here,
but in general it&amp;rsquo;s not a good idea to destroy storage without destroying the
pointee, too).&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;DerefMove&lt;/code&gt;&lt;sup id=fnref:7&gt;&lt;a href=#fn:7 class=footnote-ref role=doc-noteref&gt;7&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/sup&gt; is the third requirement, which the compiler
cannot check (there&amp;rsquo;s a lot of these, huh?). Any type which implements
&lt;code&gt;DerefMove&lt;/code&gt; can be moved out of by carefully dismantling the pointer:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:22&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-rust highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;fn&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nf&gt;move_out_of&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;lt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;P&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;mut&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;p&lt;/span&gt;: &lt;span class=nc&gt;P&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;-&amp;gt; &lt;span class=nc&gt;P&lt;/span&gt;::&lt;span class=n&gt;Target&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;where&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;P&lt;/span&gt;: &lt;span class=nc&gt;DerefMove&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;P&lt;/span&gt;::&lt;span class=n&gt;Target&lt;/span&gt;: &lt;span class=nb&gt;Sized&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=o&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nb&gt;Unpin&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;unsafe&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;    &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;// Copy the pointee out of `p` (all Rust moves are
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;    &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;// trivial copies). We need `Unpin` for this to be safe.
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;    &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=kd&gt;let&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;val&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;amp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;mut&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;*&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;p&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;as&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;*&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;mut&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;P&lt;/span&gt;::&lt;span class=n&gt;Target&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;).&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;read&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;();&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;    
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;    &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;// Destroy `p`&amp;#39;s storage without running the pointee&amp;#39;s
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;    &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;// destructor.
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;    &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=kd&gt;let&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;ptr&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;amp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;mut&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;p&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;as&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;*&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;mut&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;P&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;    &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;// Make sure to suppress the actual &amp;#34;complete&amp;#34; destructor of
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;    &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;// `p`.
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;    &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;std&lt;/span&gt;::&lt;span class=n&gt;mem&lt;/span&gt;::&lt;span class=n&gt;forget&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;p&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;);&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;    &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;// Actually destroy the storage.
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;    &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;P&lt;/span&gt;::&lt;span class=n&gt;outer_drop&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;ptr&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;);&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;    
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;    &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;// Return the moved pointee, which will be trivially NRVO&amp;#39;ed.
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;    &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;val&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:22&gt;Rust&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;Much like pinning, we need to lift this capability to the stack somehow.
&lt;code&gt;&amp;amp;mut T&lt;/code&gt; won&amp;rsquo;t cut it here.&lt;h2 id=owning-the-stack&gt;&lt;a href=#owning-the-stack&gt;Owning the Stack&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;p&gt;We can already speak of uninitialized but uniquely-owned stack memory with
&lt;code&gt;Slot&lt;/code&gt;, but &lt;code&gt;Slot::emplace()&lt;/code&gt; returns a (pinned) &lt;code&gt;&amp;amp;mut T&lt;/code&gt;, which cannot be
&lt;code&gt;DerefMove&lt;/code&gt;. This operation actually loses the uniqueness information of &lt;code&gt;Slot&lt;/code&gt;,
so instead we make &lt;code&gt;emplace()&lt;/code&gt; return a &lt;code&gt;StackBox&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;p&gt;A &lt;code&gt;StackBox&amp;lt;&#39;a, T&gt;&lt;/code&gt; is like a &lt;code&gt;Box&amp;lt;T&gt;&lt;/code&gt; that&amp;rsquo;s bound to a stack frame, using a
&lt;code&gt;Slot&amp;lt;&#39;a, T&gt;&lt;/code&gt; as underlying storage. Although it&amp;rsquo;s just a &lt;code&gt;&amp;amp;mut T&lt;/code&gt; on the
inside, it augments it with the uniqueness invariant above. In particular,
&lt;code&gt;StackBox::drop()&lt;/code&gt; is entitled to call the destructor of its pointee in-place.&lt;p&gt;To the surprise of no one who has read this far, &lt;code&gt;StackBox: DerefMove&lt;/code&gt;. The
implementation for &lt;code&gt;StackBox::outer_drop()&lt;/code&gt; is a no-op, since the calling
convention takes care of destroying stack frames.&lt;p&gt;It makes sense that, since &lt;code&gt;Slot::emplace()&lt;/code&gt; returns a &lt;code&gt;Pin&amp;lt;StackBox&amp;lt;T&gt;&gt;&lt;/code&gt;, so
should &lt;code&gt;emplace!()&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;p&gt;(There&amp;rsquo;s a crate called &lt;a href=https://crates.io/crates/stackbox&gt;&lt;code&gt;stackbox&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/a&gt; that
provides similar &lt;code&gt;StackBox&lt;/code&gt;/&lt;code&gt;Slot&lt;/code&gt; types, although it is implemented slightly
differently and does not provide the pinning guarantees we need.)&lt;h2 id=move-constructors&gt;&lt;a href=#move-constructors&gt;Move Constructors&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;p&gt;This is it. The moment we&amp;rsquo;ve all be waiting for. Behold, the definition of a
move constructor in Rust:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:23&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-rust highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;unsafe&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;trait&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;MoveCtor&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;unsafe&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;fn&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nf&gt;move_ctor&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;    &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;src&lt;/span&gt;: &lt;span class=kp&gt;&amp;amp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=nc&gt;mut&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=bp&gt;Self&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;    &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;dest&lt;/span&gt;: &lt;span class=nc&gt;Pin&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;lt;&amp;amp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;mut&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;MaybeUninit&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;lt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=bp&gt;Self&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;gt;&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;);&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:23&gt;Rust&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;blockquote&gt;&lt;p&gt;Wait, that&amp;rsquo;s it?&lt;/blockquote&gt;&lt;p&gt;There&amp;rsquo;s no such thing as &lt;code&gt;&amp;amp;move Self&lt;/code&gt;, so, much like
&lt;code&gt;drop()&lt;/code&gt;, we have to use a plain ol&amp;rsquo; &lt;code&gt;&amp;amp;mut&lt;/code&gt; instead. Like &lt;code&gt;Drop&lt;/code&gt;, and like
&lt;code&gt;CopyCtor&lt;/code&gt;, this function is not called directly by users; instead, we provide
an adaptor that takes in a &lt;code&gt;MoveCtor&lt;/code&gt; and spits out a &lt;code&gt;Ctor&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:24&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-rust highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;fn&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class=nf&gt;mov&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;lt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;P&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;mut&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;ptr&lt;/span&gt;: &lt;span class=nc&gt;P&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;-&amp;gt; &lt;span class=nc&gt;impl&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;Ctor&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;lt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;Output&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;P&lt;/span&gt;::&lt;span class=n&gt;Target&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;where&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;P&lt;/span&gt;: &lt;span class=nc&gt;DerefMove&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;P&lt;/span&gt;::&lt;span class=n&gt;Target&lt;/span&gt;: &lt;span class=nc&gt;MoveCtor&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;unsafe&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;    &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;from_placement_fn&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;move&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;|&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;dest&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;|&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;{&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;      &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;MoveCtor&lt;/span&gt;::&lt;span class=n&gt;move_ctor&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;amp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;mut&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;*&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;ptr&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;,&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;dest&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;);&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;      &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;// Destroy `p`&amp;#39;s storage without running the pointee&amp;#39;s
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;      &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;// destructor.
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;      &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=kd&gt;let&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;inner&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;&amp;amp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;mut&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;ptr&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;as&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;*&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=k&gt;mut&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;P&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;      &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;mem&lt;/span&gt;::&lt;span class=n&gt;forget&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;ptr&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;);&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;      &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;P&lt;/span&gt;::&lt;span class=n&gt;outer_drop&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;inner&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;);&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;    &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;})&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:24&gt;Rust&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;Notice that we no longer require that &lt;code&gt;P::Target: Unpin&lt;/code&gt;, since the
&lt;code&gt;ptr::read()&lt;/code&gt; call from &lt;code&gt;move_out_of()&lt;/code&gt; is now gone. Instead, we need to make a
specific requirement of &lt;code&gt;MoveCtor&lt;/code&gt; that I will explain shortly. However, we can
now freely call the move constructor just like any other &lt;code&gt;Ctor&lt;/code&gt;:&lt;div class=codeblock id=code:25&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&#34;language-rust highlight&#34;&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;emplace&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;!&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=kd&gt;let&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;y&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;mov&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;x&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;));&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;// Calls the move constructor.
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=line&gt;&lt;span class=cl&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=kd&gt;let&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;boxed&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=o&gt;=&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;make_box&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;mov&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=n&gt;y&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=p&gt;));&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=w&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=c1&gt;// Move onto the heap.
&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;div class=codeblock-buttons&gt;&lt;a class=&#34;codeblock-button codeblock-anchor&#34; href=#code:25&gt;Rust&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;h2 id=the-langauge-lawyering-part&gt;&lt;a href=#the-langauge-lawyering-part&gt;The Langauge-Lawyering Part&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;p&gt;(If you don&amp;rsquo;t care for language-lawyering, you can skip this part.)&lt;p&gt;Ok. We need to justify the loss of the &lt;code&gt;P::Target: Unpin&lt;/code&gt; bound on &lt;code&gt;mov()&lt;/code&gt;,
which seems almost like a contradiction: &lt;code&gt;Pin&amp;lt;P&gt;&lt;/code&gt; guarantees its pointee won&amp;rsquo;t
be moved, but isn&amp;rsquo;t the whole point of &lt;code&gt;MoveCtor&lt;/code&gt; to perform moves?&lt;p&gt;At the begining of this article, I called out the difference between destructive
Rust move and copying C++ moves. The reason that the above isn&amp;rsquo;t a contradiction
is that the occurences of &amp;ldquo;move&amp;rdquo; in that sentence refer to these different
senses of &amp;ldquo;move&amp;rdquo;.&lt;p&gt;The specific thing that &lt;code&gt;Pin&amp;lt;P&gt;&lt;/code&gt; is protecting unsafe code from is whatever
state is behind the pointer being blindly &lt;code&gt;memcpy&lt;/code&gt; moved to another location,
leaving any self-references in the new location dangling. However, by invoking
a C++-style move constructor, the data never &amp;ldquo;moves&amp;rdquo; in the Rust sense; it is
merely copied in a way that carefully preserves any address-dependent state.&lt;p&gt;We need to ensure two things:&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;Implementors of &lt;code&gt;MoveCtor&lt;/code&gt; for their own type must ensure that their type does
not rely on any pinning guarantees that the move constructor cannot
appropriately &amp;ldquo;fix up&amp;rdquo;.&lt;li&gt;No generic code can hold onto a reference to moved-from state, because that
way they could witness whatever messed-up post-destruction state the move
constructor leaves it in.&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;p&gt;The first of these is passed onto the implementor as an &lt;code&gt;unsafe impl&lt;/code&gt;
requirement. Designing an &lt;code&gt;!Unpin&lt;/code&gt; type by hand is difficult, and auto-generated
C++ bindings using this model would hopefully inherit move-correctness from the
C++ code itself.&lt;p&gt;The second is more subtle.
In the C++ model, the moved-from value is mutated to mark it as &amp;ldquo;moved from&amp;rdquo;,
which usually just inhibits the destructor. C++ believes all destructors are
run for all objects. For example, &lt;code&gt;std::unique_ptr&lt;/code&gt; sets the moved-from value
to &lt;code&gt;nullptr&lt;/code&gt;, so that the destructor can be run at the end of scope and do
nothing. Compare with the Rust model, where the compiler inhibits the destructor
automatically through the use of drop flags.&lt;p&gt;In order to support move-constructing both Rust and C++ typed through a uniform
interface, &lt;code&gt;move_ctor&lt;/code&gt; is a fused destructor/copy operation. In the Rust
case, no &amp;ldquo;destructor&amp;rdquo; is run, but in the C++ case we are required to run a
destructor. Although this changes the semantic ordering of destruction compared
to the equivalent C++ program, in practice, no one depends on moved-from objects
actually being destroyed (that I know of).&lt;p&gt;After &lt;code&gt;move_ctor&lt;/code&gt; is called, &lt;code&gt;src&lt;/code&gt; must
be treated as if it had just been destroyed. This means that the storage for
&lt;code&gt;src&lt;/code&gt; must be disposed of immediately, without running any destructors for the
pointed-to value. Thus, no one must be able to witness the messed-up pinned
state, which is why &lt;code&gt;mov()&lt;/code&gt; requires &lt;code&gt;P: DerefMove&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;p&gt;Thus, no code currently observing &lt;code&gt;Pin&amp;lt;P&gt;&lt;/code&gt; invariants in unsafe code will notice
anything untoward going on. No destructive moves happen, and no moved-from
state is able to hang around.&lt;div class=footnotes role=doc-endnotes&gt;&lt;hr&gt;&lt;ol&gt;&lt;li id=fn:1&gt;&lt;p&gt;This isn&amp;rsquo;t exactly a &lt;em&gt;universal&lt;/em&gt; opinion &lt;em&gt;glances at Swift&lt;/em&gt; but it is if
you write kernel code like me.&amp;#160;&lt;a href=#fnref:1 class=footnote-backref role=doc-backlink&gt;&amp;#8617;&amp;#xfe0e;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;li id=fn:2&gt;&lt;p&gt;You can&amp;rsquo;t just have rustc consume a &lt;code&gt;.h&lt;/code&gt; and spit out bindings, like e.g.
Go can, but it&amp;rsquo;s better than the disaster that is JNI.&amp;#160;&lt;a href=#fnref:2 class=footnote-backref role=doc-backlink&gt;&amp;#8617;&amp;#xfe0e;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;li id=fn:3&gt;&lt;p&gt;Some WG21 folks have tried to introduce a weaker type-trait,
&lt;code&gt;std::is_trivially_relocatable&lt;/code&gt;, which is a weakening of trivally moveable
that permits a Rust-style destructive move. The libc++ implementation of
most STL types, like &lt;code&gt;std::unique_ptr&lt;/code&gt;, admit this trait.&amp;#160;&lt;a href=#fnref:3 class=footnote-backref role=doc-backlink&gt;&amp;#8617;&amp;#xfe0e;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;li id=fn:4&gt;&lt;p&gt;A lot of unsafe Rust code assumes this is the only kind of move. For
example, &lt;a href=https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/mem/fn.swap.html&gt;&lt;code&gt;mem::swap()&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/a&gt; is implemented using &lt;code&gt;memcpy&lt;/code&gt;. This is unlike the
situation in C++, where types will often provide custom &lt;code&gt;std::swap()&lt;/code&gt;
implementations that preserve type invariants.&amp;#160;&lt;a href=#fnref:4 class=footnote-backref role=doc-backlink&gt;&amp;#8617;&amp;#xfe0e;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;li id=fn:5&gt;&lt;p&gt;Because &lt;code&gt;Future&lt;/code&gt; objects collapse their stack state into themselves when
yielding, they may have pointers into themselves (as a stack typically
does). Thus, &lt;code&gt;Future&lt;/code&gt;s need to be guaranteed to never move once they begin
executing, since Rust has no move constructors and no way to fix up the
self-pointers.&amp;#160;&lt;a href=#fnref:5 class=footnote-backref role=doc-backlink&gt;&amp;#8617;&amp;#xfe0e;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;li id=fn:6&gt;&lt;p&gt;Among other things, this means that &lt;code&gt;std::unique_ptr&lt;/code&gt;s are passed on the
stack, not in a register, which is very wasteful! Rust&amp;rsquo;s &lt;code&gt;Box&lt;/code&gt; does not have
this issue.&amp;#160;&lt;a href=#fnref:6 class=footnote-backref role=doc-backlink&gt;&amp;#8617;&amp;#xfe0e;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;li id=fn:7&gt;&lt;p&gt;Rust has attempted to add something like &lt;code&gt;DerefMove&lt;/code&gt; many times. What&amp;rsquo;s
described in this post is nowhere near as powerful as a &amp;ldquo;real&amp;rdquo; &lt;code&gt;DerefMove&lt;/code&gt;
would be, since such a thing would also allow moving &lt;em&gt;into&lt;/em&gt; a memory
location.&amp;#160;&lt;a href=#fnref:7 class=footnote-backref role=doc-backlink&gt;&amp;#8617;&amp;#xfe0e;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/ol&gt;&lt;/div&gt;</content>
